# DeliDev desktop client

## Product identity presentation

All DeliDev-generated product text, including expanded details, tooltips,
accessible names and product Copy actions, omits internal UUIDs and UUID fragments.
Use already-authorized observed names without starting another read. Missing names
use a localized resource-kind unavailable label and a stable presentation number.
Duplicate observed names use the same original names plus distinct numbers. The
connection-owned registry keeps historical names and original-ID numbers through
reorder, pagination, removal, filtering, reflow and same-identity reconnect. Numbers
are never reassigned within that lifetime; replacing the connection identity resets
the registry. Labels confer no eligibility, resource existence or operation authority.

Saved Runner Device inventory rows label both the heading and the secondary
identity line with the Runner presentation kind, so a nameless row shows the
localized Runner fallback and Runner numbers stay independent from generic Resource
numbers. Original machine IDs remain the React key and the value passed to
inspection. The Agent Worker wizard retains only the exact optional document name or
alias of a selected account (`productResourceObservedName`); it never stores a
localized or numbered presentation string, so a nameless selected account derives
its Account fallback at render time and relocalizes after a failed poll or a language
change. A genuine alias that equals a generated fallback string stays a user name.

`apps/delidev/src/product-identity.ts` owns the shared pure typed projection;
`product-identity-labels.tsx` owns desktop observation of existing query-cache data.
The provider scans the query cache once when it is created (plus one catch-up scan when
it subscribes) and then observes only the data of added or updated queries from the
`QueryCache` subscription, so labels are current before observers re-render. Consumers
of `useProductLabels` only read the retained registry and never traverse the cache. The
excluded content keys (`documentJson`, `responseJson`, `reportJson`, `bundleJson`,
`native`, `metadata`, `content`, `output`, `text`, `prompt`, `frames`, `messages`) stay
unobserved.
Mobile imports the pure projection with its own connection/view lifetime. Preserve
original UUIDs in RPC requests, authorization, receipts, immutable retries, history,
selection, cache/React/DOM keys and machine-readable export formats. Preserve exact
user-authored names, native model/source identifiers, GitHub identifiers, transcripts,
tool output and terminal content, even when their original bytes resemble UUIDs.
Generated diagnostic prose may omit internal UUID references while keeping codes,
states and recovery guidance; this is not a renderer-wide content replacement.
Generated metadata previews project only declared internal identity fields, retaining
numeric precision and protected native/user subtrees. Original import/export bytes,
proofs and digests remain unchanged.
The configuration import "Complete change details" preview adds exact-path rules to
that field map instead of widening it: `plan.changes[].source_id` presents a Resource
label, `templates[]` of Agent change documents presents Template labels, and
`agents.ids[]` and `accounts.ids[]` of Project change documents present Agent and
Account labels, each scoped to `plan.changes[].before` and `plan.changes[].after`.
`source_id` and `ids` stay out of the global field map because other owners use those
names for external, native or user identifiers. Every `reviewer_selectors` subtree is
external GitHub actor and App identity and keeps its original bytes, including decimal
IDs above the JavaScript safe-integer range. The projection is display-only: Apply
sends the exact preview bytes, and numeric tokens and malformed JSON are unchanged.

Loading a pasted or file-read document that `JSON.parse` rejects with a `SyntaxError` (for
example `not-json` or an unterminated object) shows the localized `validation.4b7e1f93a2d6`
guidance: the document is not valid JSON, so correct the syntax or paste a current version 4
DeliDev export. The raw engine message is never shown. The draft stays editable, the stage
remains Load document, and no preview or apply request is sent. Only that parse failure maps
to this message: valid JSON with an unsupported version or shape keeps
`validation.71aacc919010`, oversized and invalid UTF-8 input keep their own messages, other
unexpected failures keep the generic read failure, and export-side validation of the
server-produced document never shows advice to edit pasted JSON.

The presentation owners include Home and repository navigation, Projects and
Repositories, resource/settings selectors and actions, accounts/providers/runners/
devices and saved connections, sessions/queues/terminals/storage/reviews, schedules,
usage/pricing/routing, GitHub-local associations and remediation, diagnostics and
backup inventory/operations/confirmation. Remove UUID-only Project disclosures and
Repository ID rows completely. Keep useful metadata, actions, statuses, semantic
layouts, themes, English/Korean, focus and disclosure lifetimes. Repository navigation
keeps its independent name-only floating Details popup. Backup labels remain keyed
by the original backup ID; inspection and deletion show the safe label, original
timestamp and exact size while immutable deletion authority remains bound to the
original inspected object, revision and SHA-256, including duplicate metadata and
reordered inventory.

## Known subscription model autocomplete

The Agent Worker wizard retains the Model step, 720px maximum column, controls
at least 40px high, theme, footer and narrow-width wrapping. The current inline
model flow uses a `Model for {source}` form label and the helper
`Choose a source suggestion or enter its exact native model ID.` This replaces
the earlier shared `Choose a model` heading, `Model` label and saved-model search
helper with one model choice per source. Follow the
[inline Worker model contract](cmds-delidev-catalog-contract.md#inline-worker-models-and-endpoint-only-completion-reservation).

System capability `KNOWN_SUBSCRIPTION_MODELS_V1 = 35` independently enables the
known-model read for supported subscription services. Missing catalog support
shows server-update guidance while retaining exact-ID entry. The inline Worker
flow requires protocol 2 and `INLINE_WORKER_MODELS_V1 = 42`; otherwise the current
client shows server-update guidance instead of opening the editor. This replaces
the earlier saved/direct fallback for older servers. Known suggestions remain
advisory, bounded read-only metadata, not native discovery, credential validation
or proof of account entitlement.
Reject invalid service echoes, catalog versions, dates, provenance categories,
duplicate IDs and incomplete or oversized inventories before displaying them.

Focus opens a keyboard-operated listbox with display names, exact native IDs and
Known labels. Name/ID search filters the complete validated list of at most 200
known candidates. Arrow keys, Home/End and Enter select through accessible active
descendants; Escape dismisses the list and returns focus from the results region
to the input. Keep the typed exact-ID option available when no suggestion matches.
Loading or failure preserves typed input, and a failed known-catalog refresh may
retain the last valid same-source candidates. Source/harness changes clear
incompatible selections and prevent stale responses from becoming candidates.

The independent saved Model registry and its autocomplete search, pagination,
Saved labels and Saved-over-Known precedence are superseded by inline Worker
models. API suggestions come only from the selected Provider endpoint and use
Endpoint suggestion labels. There are no saved-list page controls or separate
Model UUID/revision selections. Selecting a known or endpoint suggestion retains
its exact native ID and applicable non-secret metadata until the atomic Worker
save. Queries never register models. Preserve the original Worker revision
checks, source/account validation and immutable execution attribution. Endpoint
requests pin Account and Provider revisions and reject mismatched response
identity; source, Account, connection-generation or editor-lifetime changes clear
endpoint choices. Endpoint failure clears choices while permitting exact-ID entry.

Show `Known models · Catalog updated {date}`, with `Built-in catalog` or
`Cached catalog` when applicable, and
`Availability depends on your plan and installed harness.` Do not show the
unsupported subscription-discovery warning. The single current refresh control,
`Refresh models from endpoint`, replaces `Reload models`: for subscriptions it
rereads server catalog state without forcing an external download; for API
sources it requests a fresh selected endpoint list. Do not merge saved records,
persist endpoint catalogs or add background endpoint discovery. Recommendation
removal cannot delete Worker configurations or immutable execution history;
pricing and native-account lifecycle remain independently owned. These browser
interactions do not establish installed native/account/platform acceptance.

## Desktop validation ownership

PR validation is owned by the desktop Turbo task graph. Cache type checks, pure
UI/client assertions and deterministic frontend output using their declared
inputs. Execute real Go-server integration, QA, widget and native packaging
fixtures through uncached tasks. Client pure tests precede client Go integration;
each desktop shard runs its cached pure UI assertions before its uncached Go
integration assertions. The combined desktop integration task also follows
client integration, and combined QA follows type checks, desktop unit/integration
tests and the release check. The independent checks phase runs QA after its type
checks and release check; the release check owns its frontend build dependency.
The desktop launch fixtures build the real frontend, so they wait for the
workspace package builds (including the API client) before they start.
Sharing a runner-built Go executable never shares fixture processes, credentials
or data lifetimes.

The current matrix has one checks phase and four complete Vitest shards, each
with at most two jsdom workers on the shared two-core host. The desktop-owned
Vitest sequencer assigns unit and integration inventories independently. It
sorts files by descending committed duration weight, then assigns each file to
the shard with the smallest accumulated weight. File paths and shard indexes
break ties deterministically; new or renamed files receive a one-second weight,
and obsolete weight entries never add files to the inventory. Each selected
file runs exactly once across the four shards. Sharded execution starts longer
files first; unsharded local execution retains Vitest sorting. The weight table
and sequencer are inputs of every cached unit shard and uncached integration
shard. Weights are scheduling estimates from successful hosted executions, not
validation results or native acceptance evidence. This supersedes the
earlier four-worker ceiling without relaxing individual test or product
deadlines. Local `pnpm test` retains the complete validation sequence, including
client build, type checks, unit/integration tests, bundle/launch/widget/QA fixtures,
frontend build and release check. Follow the
[repository workflow contract](repository-workflow-contract.md) for exact task
dependencies, affected selection, cache authentication and evidence limits.
Fixtures and packaging do not establish native/account/platform acceptance.

## Startup Keychain access

Each fresh macOS app launch shows the Keychain access notice and starts checking
automatically after authenticated local connection. The native connector owns
the attempt across renderer remounts, polling, window reopening and sibling
local windows and binds it to the paired client. Only trusted local product
webviews receive the dedicated `credential-access` permission.
`desktop_credential_access` accepts closed Observe/Retry/Skip actions and the
original server/runtime generation; no renderer account, key, path, endpoint or
remote selector is accepted. After successful explicit local-registration
recovery on the same server, native code rebinds the retained attempt to the
replacement client only when Go confirms the old client is revoked. The attempt
and its current result survive without an automatic Keychain retry. Native
window authority is rechecked before dispatch and before delivering a result.
The Go resident host uses its original in-process server and reads through the
existing vault scope without initializing a missing scope, lock or pin. Follow
the [credential contract](cmds-delidev-credentials-contract.md#desktop-startup-access-confirmation).

The checking screen uses a centered 480px maximum card with 28px padding, existing
theme tokens and English/Korean catalogs. It has a title, access explanation,
OS-permission guidance, an announced progress indicator, Continue without
checking and Connections. Small windows retain 16px side padding
and vertical scrolling; reduced-motion preference suppresses spinner animation.
Successful access or no eligible key enters the product automatically and moves
focus to its heading. Failure remains on the same card with an announced safe
problem, explicit Retry and Continue. Retry names the exact failed attempt shown
in that window; a stale failure cannot retry a newer native attempt. Unknown
transport results only re-observe the same attempt; only a confirmed terminal
failure can start a fresh retry.
Skipping or a borrowed server displays a dismissible notice stating that startup
checking was skipped and saved account status is unchanged. Saved remote windows
and non-macOS launches retain their existing entry flow.

Access confirmation never changes saved account health or connection state and
does not validate providers or refresh OAuth. No account queries mount beneath
the startup gate until completion or explicit continuation. Continue stops later
credential reads but cannot promise to dismiss an in-progress OS-owned prompt.
Existing local Start/Stop, Worker supervision, diagnostics, saved authority and
35-second joined shutdown ownership remain independent. Deterministic fixtures
and builds do not establish installed-app interactive Keychain acceptance.

## Key-preserving API format editing

With ProviderInventory capabilities 9 and 10, Edit AI account enables supported
formats for connected API accounts and saves the format plus existing editable
preferences through `ChangeAccountApiFormat`. Capability 9 activates the
operation and capability 10 gates its revision-bound Provider check, so the
connected key-preserving operation is enabled only when both capabilities are
advertised. The request pins the revision of the Provider resource used to
display the selected profile. A missing Provider read blocks saving, and a
changed Provider revision requires a fresh read and explicit save. Uncertain
retries retain the original revision and complete request bytes. The saved key stays in place; the help states that
future executions use the new format, current executions retain their original
format, and separate Validate connection is required. Saving sends no provider
request. Provider identity and keyless/key ownership stay fixed. Without capability
9 or 10, the original capability-7 disconnect/cleanup/re-entry behavior remains.

Retain the existing 768px dialog, field order, checkbox controls, Provider lock,
small-screen scrolling/fixed footer, Settings lifetime, labeled native select,
keyboard selection, Escape/X/Cancel closure and opener focus restoration. The
capability-9 action reads Save changes. Capability/profile loading errors, pending
cleanup, an active save and an uncertain result retain existing protection. Exact
uncertain retries reuse the original request. Late responses after disposal cannot
close or refresh a replacement editor.

Observation-only account updates adopt the latest protected fields and bigint
revision while retaining editable draft values. Changes to editable preferences or
format elsewhere show a conflict and retain the draft. Provider cards remain locked
for current and retained account generations; reference-read failures block saves.
Incompatible Workers show the existing explicit reconfiguration notice. Native
window/provider acceptance is separate from component/browser fixtures.

## Modal background visibility

All app-owned dialogs and compact modal navigation drawers use the shared
`--backdrop: f` token: approximately 12% black dimming in light, dark and
system themes, including initial OS-dark paint. Opening a modal preserves the
underlying screen's visible content, layout, filters, pagination and scroll.
Do not hide category inventories, local Worker controls or pairing presentation,
or change category headings or column geometry solely because a dialog is open.
Keep dialog surfaces opaque with their existing borders and local shadows; do not
apply a viewport-sized shadow, additional overlay, blur or new animation to the
background. Native per-modal backdrops retain their existing stacking and may
compound for nested modals. Wide nonmodal navigation regions have no backdrop;
closing the final modal removes dimming.

Preserve native `showModal` input blocking, Settings background inertness,
initial focus, contained Tab navigation, existing Escape/backdrop-click behavior,
and available-opener focus restoration. A nested modal retains its parent's
presentation and blocks parent input. Existing same-window task steps still show
only their active step. Inactive application surfaces and closed disclosures keep
their existing visibility rules. Loading, empty, denied, progress and error states
retain their original data and lifecycle ownership. This presentation rule adds
no RPC, protocol allocation, storage migration or native execution authority and
does not change OS-owned dialogs. Protected external native browser children keep
their existing modal visibility and security boundaries.

## OAuth format selection extension

The [OAuth format reservations](cmds-delidev-account-oauth-contract.md#oauth-api-format-selection-reservations)
own the recorded capability 8 and Start/attempt format fields established
by reservation the originating change. Preserve manual
format profiles, original defaults and independent OAuth eligibility. The common
manual/OAuth connection UI requires selection for multiple profiles and displays
a sole profile read-only; server-owned Start pins explicit OAuth selections through
completion/recovery. Provider registration remains independently gated. No
database migration is added.

## API key format selection

The manual Add AI API key task requires Entry name, API format and API key in that
order. Format labels are OpenAI Responses, OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic
Messages, restricted to the selected provider's offered profiles and requiring an
explicit choice. Responses help identifies Codex compatibility. The existing
provider summary, key guidance, advanced preferences and secure-storage/validation
notes remain. Lists and connection details show the account's selected format;
Agent Worker account choices and compatibility checks resolve that format rather
than the provider default. Legacy accounts display the original default.

Custom Provider tasks replace the single protocol selector with three format
cards. Checked cards expose their own URL/authentication, at least one is required,
and account-referenced profiles are locked. Editing an Account format requires
completed Disconnect and credential cleanup. Keyless/key-required transitions
require a new account. Capability 7, current profile reads and reference reads gate
new saves; loading, permission refusal, unsupported servers and changed profiles
show a reason and block saving. Accepted uncertain requests retry only their
original bytes; profile changes dispose secret handoffs under the existing key
lifetime rules. Account preference edits preserve protected numeric tokens.

Both tasks retain the shared 768px Form dialog, fixed header/footer, scrolling
body, 40px controls, 8px corners, existing focus/Escape and English/Korean behavior.
At narrow widths and effective 200% zoom, footer actions stack and the body scrolls.
The approved desktop design previews remain outside the repository. Browser and
HTTP fixtures do not establish actual account/native platform acceptance. See the
[catalog contract](cmds-delidev-catalog-contract.md#api-account-format-selection)
for schema-3 compatibility, original-generation authority and portable version 4.

## Current session startup progress

Ordinary Session and General Chat share a read-only four-phase presentation inside the existing conversation region: Preparing workspace / 작업공간 준비 중, Waiting to start / 시작 대기 중, Starting agent / 에이전트 시작 중, and Waiting for response / 응답 대기 중. Use a centered indeterminate status for an accepted empty transcript and a compact tail row when only the original native input or an empty assistant start is visible. The first actual assistant, tool or progress content, unsupported content, or a terminal outcome removes generic startup feedback. Preserve normal transcript rendering, Info/tools, composer, drafts and original follow-up delivery projections.

Require a supported current session envelope, exact session/execution/input/preparation/job ownership, monotonic accepted resource revisions, a live successful connection and complete successfully accepted transcript coverage. Pending preparation comes first, then ready preparation with an independently observed eligible queued input and no claim, then the matching active claimed execution before acceptance, then matching running native acceptance without visible response. Native thread binding and READY startup are not input acceptance and reveal no live initialization subphases. Supported legacy acceptance needs an independently observed exact accepted queue input. Historical start-preparation compatibility metadata and preceding execution outcomes cannot establish live activity.

The feature permits only the exact server `InitialExecutionPending` code, message and guidance to coexist with Preparing workspace or Waiting to start. Require blocked/not-started first-generation state, no prior/current/active execution or startup record, sequence/count one, complete current original queued-input proof without a claim/native request, and valid pending/ready preparation. Changed or extended problems retain failure precedence. Hide its compact blocked notice only while this valid projection is visible; preserve its original reason/guidance in Info. This exception grants no dispatch, retry or account/native readiness authority.

Pause/Stop, archive, problems, budget blocks, recovery, startup failure, uncertainty, original approval/user-input waits and unconfirmed responses suppress generic activity. Failed, malformed, disconnected or stale observations keep original notices and controls. Incomplete/unread transcript or queue coverage never proves absence of a response or uncertainty; do not enumerate unread history to show progress. Current message evidence extends the existing bounded page projection with owner/input/sequence/kind metadata only, retaining no text, arguments, output or raw claim tokens. Preserve the bounded payload window (twenty transcript pages), bounded live tail, original tokens, revisions, removals and source-page focus protection. A per-original-claim/turn suppression latch survives removal, payload eviction and later empty revisions after response/content uncertainty was observed. Exact new execution ownership resets evidence; late older revisions cannot reanimate a stale phase.

Use semantic colors, a decorative spinner and one stable polite status announcement. Repeated successful reads keep the same label/node; locale changes update that node without remounting controllers. Reduced motion disables animation; narrow and 200% reflow use wrapping within the existing region. Rendering/navigation/reconnect/polling never start, resume, retry, dispatch or duplicate execution. No RPC, allocation, persistence, migration, native bridge, dependency, feature flag, percentages, ETA or clone-specific progress is added. Fixture/type-check evidence and skipped owner-assigned native/platform acceptance remain separate.

## Screen shortcuts and help

The connection-owned `ShortcutProvider` and `useShortcuts` register stable enum action IDs, a Surface or global scope, key bindings, typed localization keys, active/enabled conditions, an unavailable reason, input policy and an existing action callback or explicit native behavior. Registration is memory-only. Connection-owned keydown/keyup, window blur and document visibility listeners serve the connection; Strict Mode and connection replacement remove the original listener/registrations. Surface navigation and same-identity reconnect preserve original drafts, queries and mutation receipts. The lightweight Surface module retains the existing enum values and the existing views export.

Dispatch and the read-only help use the same declarations. Match input-target registrations before screen and global registrations. Conflicts at the winning priority execute nothing and log only the stable event classification, scope and action IDs. A disabled matching action cannot fall through. Preserve original button/form guards and original RPC/request authority; a shortcut is not a new execution capability. Never log key events, input, aliases or native/browser content.

Common shortcuts are logical `?` for help, unshifted primary+N for New session and fixed primary+comma for Open Settings. Open Settings uses the existing category-free navigation callback and is available from ordinary text fields. A fresh Settings visit opens AI Subscription through the existing focus handoff; invoking it during an active visit retains the current category, draft, pending requests and focus. The read-only Common catalog, Help and Settings button accessibility annotation share the same binding declaration. This shortcut performs no configuration save or execution action and retains the existing event, modal, terminal and capture guards. Primary means Command on the local macOS renderer and Control on Windows/Linux, independently of the selected server or Worker. Session and New session use primary+I to focus their message input and primary+Enter to submit only from that input. Session submission queues a message; New session submission creates through the original guarded form. The feature gives Session and General Chat follow-up composers fixed Enter submission and native Shift+Enter newline. Preserve New session's guarded Enter submission and native Shift+Enter newline. Search uses primary+I to focus the existing query and retains native Enter form submission. Search has no global entry shortcut. Primary+K opens the fixed command menu described below; it never submits a Search query. The sidebar Search button remains available without shortcut guidance. Ordinary Search entry retains its existing once-only autofocus; Search primary+I focuses the retained query and opens the existing compact drawer when needed. Files, Diff and Diagnostics register their existing focus-local Escape closure and original opener restoration. Other screens initially expose common shortcuts only. Control aria-keyshortcuts derives from the same platform-resolved bindings. The logical help binding carries a physical Shift+/ ARIA annotation for English/Korean slash-key layouts; it never changes logical character matching.

The fixed Session Open tool / 도구 열기 action uses primary+T (Command+T on macOS,
Control+T on Windows/Linux) for the active, selected, nonembedded Session, with
ordinary editable input allowed. `ShortcutId.OpenTool` is a read-only catalog
entry and never one of the seven editable action IDs. The tab-bar `+` button (the only trigger; there is no wrench button and no direct
New browser page button) and the
effective shortcut open the same single native `DialogSurface` modal, which
performs no tool action or resource read on open. Keep the five original rows in
order: Diff, Files, Terminals, Browser and Diagnostics. The Browser row opens the
New browser page dialog (never a Browser workspace tab) under
`cmds-delidev-browser-contract.md`; it is the only entry to that dialog. The eligible existing
Open Sidechat action follows as an additional row; this feature neither moves nor
redesigns it. Keep all original eligibility, including disabled Terminals for a
Sidechat parent snapshot. Child controllers stay mounted across dialog visits.

Terminal opening has one desktop eligibility rule derived from the authenticated
Session document (`TerminalOpenEligibility`: `Eligible`, `SidechatBlocked`,
`PreparationNotReady`). Terminals is eligible only when the document's
`preparation.state` is `ready` and the Session is not a Sidechat parent snapshot;
a missing, pending, failed, canceled, uncertain or stale preparation, and a
Session that has not loaded, is `PreparationNotReady`. The Terminals row, the
Open terminals shortcut (primary+backtick) and the open handler (including its
no-Session pending branch) share it, so an unready gesture creates no open intent
and sends no `CreateTerminal` request. Additional-terminal creation (the + button
and the terminal-input primary+T shortcut) is disabled by the same readiness
while existing terminal tabs stay unchanged. While preparation is not ready the
Terminals row is disabled and muted and its Help entry reports the localized
`shortcuts.terminalsPreparing` reason (Available when workspace is ready. /
작업공간 준비가 끝나면 터미널을 사용할 수 있습니다.); the Sidechat-specific
`shortcuts.terminalsUnavailable` reason wins when Sidechat is the blocker. The
same text appears only as a hover tooltip: no persistent helper text is added, the
pointer target is a noninteractive wrapper around the disabled button (which
receives the text through `aria-describedby`), the disabled button stays outside
keyboard activation and the enabled-row focus order is unchanged, and the tooltip
is positioned inside the row so the scrolling dialog, narrow viewports and 200%
zoom never clip it. Its colors use only the shared inverse theme tokens
(`--inverse-surface`, `--inverse-border`, `--on-inverse`); no raw color literals
appear in `session.css`. Regained readiness re-enables the row and shortcut without
opening anything; a fresh gesture follows the original reuse-or-create flow. An
unsent open intent that is waiting for inventory reads is discarded when
readiness is lost (checked again immediately before `CreateTerminal`) and is not
replayed when readiness returns; already accepted or uncertain terminal requests
keep their reconciliation behavior. The server readiness rule, RPC shapes and
Worker connection behavior are unchanged.

The dialog uses the localized Open tool / 도구 열기 title and a named close button.
It has no search field or footer. Width is `min(360px, viewport minus 32px)` with
20px padding, 12px corners, 44px row and close targets, semantic theme tokens and
visible focus; height is bounded to the viewport minus 32px and scrolls
vertically, including at 200% zoom. Opening focuses the first enabled row. Tab is
contained to the close button and enabled rows; arrows and Home/End navigate
enabled rows; native Enter/Space activates a row. Escape, the close button and
backdrop dismissal restore the available opener (the focused element that opened
it, otherwise the trigger). Selecting a row closes the dialog synchronously
before invoking the original callback once and preserves the destination-tab
focus instead of restoring the opener. Session, surface and connection departure
dispose the presentation without restoring focus into hidden content. Connection
departure includes losing connection readiness while the Session and connection
identity stay unchanged: App passes `connectionReady` through `SessionView` to
`SessionToolMenu`, an open dialog closes immediately so recovery content is no
longer blocked, focus moves to the Session heading (the recovery control)
instead of the native modal-close restoration to the unavailable opener, and
the trigger and the OpenTool shortcut stay inert while the connection is
unavailable. Restoring readiness never reopens the dialog; only an
explicit user action does. Session drafts and pending operations are untouched.

The read-only Reload page / 페이지 새로고침 action (`ShortcutId.ReloadPage`) uses primary+R
(Command+R on the local macOS renderer, Control+R on Windows/Linux, chosen by
`shortcutPlatform()`) and reloads the current product webview once per eligible key
press. `ReloadShortcutOwner` (`reload-shortcut.tsx`) owns it: `Desktop` mounts it above
`App` and under `ShortcutPreferenceProvider`, so the identity-read, local startup,
saved-connection, disconnected recovery and every connected top-level screen receive
it. It listens on `window` in the capture phase with `bindingMatches` against the
shared `globalShortcutBindings` declaration, so it runs before terminal hosts, product
inputs and ordinary dispatch, and works from text fields, terminal input events that
reach the renderer and open product modals. An accepted event is `preventDefault`-ed
and `stopImmediatePropagation`-ed before reload, so no field submission or terminal
byte is delivered. Only the exact chord is accepted: plain R, Shift, Alt, AltGraph,
the wrong-platform modifier, IME composition/keyCode 229, repeat and already handled
events are ignored. While a Settings shortcut capture listener is installed
(`shortcutCaptureListening()` in `shortcut-capture.ts`), the owner stays out so R is
recorded as the chord. The default calls `window.location.reload()`; no native menu
accelerator, RPC, Browser reload bridge, storage or migration is added, the focused
external Browser CEF content keeps its own key ownership, and nothing is logged beyond
existing safe classifications.

Reload page is a read-only entry in `readOnlyShortcutCatalog` (Common group, Global
scope) and in `readOnlyShortcutPolicies` with key `r`: a committed editable unshifted
primary+R override suppresses it in every scope with the localized
`shortcuts.reloadSuppressed` reason. It stays inactive (`shortcuts.preferencesPending`)
until the first saved-preference read settles, and it fails closed for every
preference problem except Unavailable (`ReadFailed`, `InvalidDocument`,
`UnsupportedVersion`, `OutcomeUnknown`, `WriteFailed`, `Changed`) with
`shortcuts.reloadUnverified` until a successful reinspection clears the problem
(`shortcutSnapshotVerified`); problem Unavailable uses the default binding. Saved
bytes and the seven editable IDs are untouched. Help lists the action through a
`ShortcutExecution.Native` definition registered by `App` (never dispatched by the
store) and Settings through the read-only catalog loop, both with the effective
platform keycaps, the existing disabled treatment and the English/Korean reason; no
button or dialog is added.

#### Product route retained across reload

The whole-webview reload above keeps the current top-level screen and its selected
item. `product-route.ts` owns a typed product route in the `index.html` URL query
string (no server path, so no native fallback is needed). The only parameters are
`screen` (a `Surface` value), `session` and optional `sidechat` (Sessions), `item`
(Inbox entry, Schedule or Pull requests repository), `category` (a
`SettingsCategory`) and `tab` (a `UsageTab`). Selections are canonical entity IDs
(`isEntityId`) and enums only, never titles, prompts, credentials, search text or
other user content. New session, New general chat and Search keep their screen
only; Sessions Home and every selection-free screen write no selection, so a stale
selection is never restored. Unrelated query parameters, the path and the `#main`
skip-link hash are preserved.

Native product-window admission checks the original local origin, entry-document
path, registered window and role after a route update. A same-document query is
allowed because it does not select a different document or grant native authority.
This includes preserved unrelated query parameters. Foreign origins, other paths
and URL credentials remain denied.

`Shell` in `App.tsx` mirrors committed in-app navigation and selection into the
query with `history.replaceState` (never `pushState`), so Back/Forward gain no
entries; a throttled or failing write is logged (`delidev.product_route.write_failed`)
and ignored. Each mounted screen reports its own selection to `Shell`: Inbox
(`selectionChanged`), Schedules, Pull requests (repository), Settings
(`categoryChanged`) and Usage (`tabChanged`, `UsageTab` in `usage-tab.ts`).

On document startup `readInitialRoute` parses the URL for a connection identity
scope (the same server, endpoint and device identity key `App` already uses; an
unpaired connection is scoped by its transport object). The read is pure, so React
may invoke it any number of times for one render (StrictMode lazy initializers,
discarded renders) and every call answers the same. The `Shell` records ownership of
the URL with `commitInitialRouteScope` from a layout effect, i.e. only when it
commits. A different identity never receives the previous identity's route. An unknown `screen`
falls back to Sessions Home; malformed IDs, unknown categories and tabs, and
parameters that do not belong to the screen are dropped. Screens without a selection
(and the Settings category and Usage tab, which need no read) open immediately, so a
pending route never flashes Home. A Session, Sidechat, Inbox entry, Schedule or
repository selection stays pending until the connection is ready, then
`product-route-restore.ts` verifies it with a fresh, uncached read through the
current transport (`GetResource` for Session and repository, `GetSchedule`,
`GetInboxEntry`; a Sidechat must resolve to a child of the requested parent). While
the connection is unavailable the route stays pending, the URL keeps the original
route, and the selection resumes only when the same connection becomes ready. A
restore read is current only for the transport and the `ConnectionEpoch` it started
in: a same-identity reconnect keeps the transport while the peer behind it can be
replaced or downgraded, so an epoch change aborts the read and restarts the restore. A
deleted, denied, malformed, wrong-kind or wrong-connection selection (not found,
permission denied, unauthenticated, invalid argument such as an ID of another entity
kind, an unexpected shape or an invalid envelope with a non-positive revision or an
unsupported schema version, checked the same way for every restored kind) clears the
selection and shows the requested screen's list, default category or Sessions Home.
Failure codes are classified once, for every restored kind, by
`routeFailureDispositions` in `search-session-routing.ts`, an exhaustive table over
`FailureCode`: `invalid_argument`, `not_found`, `permission_denied` and
`unauthenticated` are definitive (clear); every other code, including
`recovery_required` (gRPC failed precondition), `unavailable`, `server_unavailable`
(deadline exceeded and unmapped transport errors), `canceled` and `internal`, is
retryable (retain). A retryable read failure
reopens the Session or repository so its own mounted retry and error state shows; a
Schedule needs the fresh resource, so it is cleared and the list's own retry applies.
`readRouteSession` restores a Session selection strictly from two typed decision
tables in `product-route-restore.ts` (`sessionSlotTable`, `sidechatSlotTable`).
Each read is classified once relative to the requested parent: `TopLevel` (a
Session that is not a Sidechat: work Session, General Chat or Fork),
`SidechatOfRequestedParent`, `SidechatOfOtherParent`, `Rejected` (not found,
denied, unauthenticated, an ID of another entity kind, a resource of the wrong kind,
an invalid envelope, or malformed or unknown provenance such as a missing workspace
or invalid Fork metadata) and `Transient` (any retryable failure). A Sidechat is
valid only in the `sidechat` slot under a parent that this restore itself read as
`TopLevel`; its retained original parent is never trusted unread.

| `session` slot read                               | `session` only                                          | with `sidechat`                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| TopLevel                                          | open the Session                                        | read the `sidechat` slot (below)                                               |
| SidechatOfRequestedParent / SidechatOfOtherParent | clear                                                   | clear (child not read)                                                         |
| Rejected                                          | clear                                                   | clear (child not read)                                                         |
| Transient                                         | open the Session unverified (its own retry state shows) | open the requested Sidechat under the requested parent with a placeholder name |

| `sidechat` slot read (parent verified `TopLevel`) | result                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SidechatOfRequestedParent                         | open the Sidechat with its verified name                          |
| TopLevel, SidechatOfOtherParent or Rejected       | open the verified parent only; the `sidechat` ID leaves the URL   |
| Transient                                         | retain the requested Sidechat under the parent (placeholder name) |

"Clear" opens nothing and removes the selection from the URL, so the requested
screen's list shows. A `Transient` row opens its Session without a verification
read, so the Shell remembers the pair (the top-level Session and its optional
Sidechat) and the mounted top-level pane judges it once loaded
(`verifyRestored`). That pane keeps its Session metadata read active for as long
as the pair is unverified, whichever of its tabs is selected: a selected Sidechat
tab pauses the ordinary stream, and without this read the requested parent would
never be verified. A Sidechat, malformed provenance or an invalid envelope there,
or a definitive failure of the read itself (not found, denied, unauthenticated,
invalid argument), is cleared exactly like a `Rejected` row: the Session and any
provisional Sidechat under it end and the URL drops them. The pair is the
restore's own state, so it ends whatever the user did since; a different Session
the user selected meanwhile is left alone. A retained Sidechat is mounted under
the requested parent so its own retry and error state runs, and the URL keeps the
`sidechat` ID. A Sidechat tab opened without a verified name never shows its
internal ID in its text, `title` or accessible name: it carries a localized
product-identity label (the Session presentation label) and is marked
provisional. The child's own pane judges its descriptor once it loads the Session
(`loadedSessionProvenance`, the same checks route verification applies): a
Session that is not a Sidechat of the requested parent, including malformed or
unknown provenance or an invalid envelope, or a definitive read failure of the
Sidechat itself, ends the placeholder tab and its `sidechat` ID leaves the URL.
Only the acceptance (taking the verified name) waits until the requested parent
has been verified as a top-level Session, because a child's own retained metadata
cannot prove that the parent it names is itself valid.

The URL mirror is a typed decision table (`product-route-mirror.ts`,
`deriveProductRoute`) over the visible surface, the Schedules mode and the restore
state. It derives the route only from state the visible, accepted destination
shows, so a selection that a hidden workspace retains never describes another
destination. Each surface owns fixed slots (`surfaceSlots`): Sessions the
`session` and `sidechat`; Inbox, Schedules and Pull requests the `item`; Settings
the `category`; Usage the `tab`; New session, New general chat and Search none. A
`sidechat` is written only under a selected `session`.

| Restore state | Mirror                                                                                               |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pending       | hold: the URL keeps the original route until the selection is verified                               |
| Provisional   | write the visible selection as requested (unverified after a transient failure; a reload retries it) |
| Settled       | write the visible selection                                                                          |

| Schedules mode   | `item`                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Workspace        | the selected Schedule (the editor and New schedule report no selection)                                                |
| OccurrenceReview | none: the workspace and the Schedule it retains are hidden, so a reload opens the selection-free Schedules destination |

The Settings category is dropped when the Settings visit ends (Settings remounts
for every visit and reports its own category), so a visit never starts with an
earlier visit's category in the URL. Usage stays mounted and shows its retained
tab, so that tab is the visible one.

Restore supersession uses one monotonic navigation-intent token owned by `Shell`
(`navigationIntent`, a ref). Every handler that actually changes the surface, the
selection or the tab, or opens a new-item, editor, review or project destination,
registers an intent synchronously, never from an effect, through the closed
`NavigationIntentSource` enum in `navigation-intent.tsx`. `Shell` handlers call
`userNavigated(source)` directly: every surface change (`setSurface`), every
Session or Sidechat opening (`openSession`), the Search result opener and the
project creation opener. Child screens call the same function through
`useNavigationIntent()` from their own handlers: Session tab selection, Inbox row
selection and closing the detail, Schedule selection, New schedule, Edit schedule
and returning to the list, Pull requests repository selection, Settings category
changes and Usage tab changes. There is no window-level click or key listener:
controls that do not navigate (retry, reconnect, refresh, dismiss, copy and
similar) never register an intent, so a selection that waits for its connection is
not cancelled by them and resumes when the same connection becomes ready.
Registering an intent also aborts the pending restore's read and clears the pending
selection in the same handler, and logs `delidev.product_route.navigation_intent`
with the closed source value. A pending restore captures the token when it starts
and compares it when its read settles, before any side effect (state change,
Session opening or URL write), so a read that settles in the same tick as a click,
before React renders the choice or flushes a passive effect, still cannot override
it. The restore itself opens the Session through `showSession` and selects the
repository through `selectRepositoryId`, which do not register an intent.
Selection reports from screens only feed the URL mirror; they never decide
supersession. A new navigation handler must add a `NavigationIntentSource` value,
call the registration from the handler and add a driver to the exhaustive
`Record<NavigationIntentSource, ...>` in `product-route-restore.test.tsx`, which
fails typecheck without it.
Restoration only selects and reads: no mutation is dispatched, no pending operation
is replayed, and drafts, filters, search text, scroll, dialogs and in-memory
presentation reset as before. The structured log `delidev.product_route.restore`
carries only the screen and a closed outcome (including `superseded`).

The reload shortcut, its saved override policy, capture and IME/modifier guards,
focused external Browser ownership and the English/Korean copy are unchanged. No
native, server, RPC, storage or migration change is involved. Regression coverage:
`product-route.test.ts` (parse, serialize, hash and history, pure identity read and
commit),
`product-route-restore-table.test.tsx` (both decision tables row by row, and every
slot by resource kind by read outcome by parent outcome through `readRouteSession`),
`product-route-mirror.test.ts` (the mirror table: surface by retained state, restore
state, Schedules mode, Sessions slots and the URL round trip),
`product-route-restore.test.tsx` (mirroring, restore per screen, fallbacks, pending
routes, reload-shortcut remount, envelope validation per kind, slow-read supersession
per kind, same-tick supersession per restore kind and for New schedule and surface
changes, non-navigation controls that keep a waiting selection, one driver per
`NavigationIntentSource` handler, retained Sidechat selections after transient
failures, placeholder Sidechat labels without a raw ID, provisional Sidechat pairs
whose requested parent is itself a Sidechat, malformed or deleted (including a
child that loads before its parent is verified), the Schedule retained behind an
occurrence review, the Settings category of an earlier visit, a StrictMode scope change, an epoch
bump with a retained transport, unpaired transport replacement, and a failure-code by
restore-kind matrix including wrong-kind IDs) and
`search-session-routing.test.ts` (the failure classification table).

Read-only shortcut defaults yield to existing editable chords through one shared
policy, `readOnlyShortcutSuppression` in `shortcut-preferences.ts`, keyed by
shortcut ID and the unshifted primary key it protects. OpenTool protects `t`. A new
read-only default chord that can collide with an editable unshifted primary chord
must be added to `readOnlyShortcutCatalog` with a `readOnlyShortcutPolicies` entry;
dispatch, conflict validation, Help, the Settings catalog and ARIA derive from that
one policy. Any
committed editable override that is an unshifted primary+T binding suppresses
only the new OpenTool default, in memory and across all scopes. Disabled
overrides and Shift+T overrides do not suppress it; removing or changing the
committed override restores the default immediately. Effective dispatch, conflict
validation, Help, the read-only Settings catalog (which follows the committed map,
not the unsaved draft) and the trigger `aria-keyshortcuts` share this policy, and
Help and Settings show localized custom-binding-priority guidance while it is
suppressed. Saved preference bytes, the seven editable IDs and native
validation/storage never change, so every previously valid custom T preference
stays valid. Terminal-targeted bindings keep their independent admission and are
never suppressed by this policy. Handled-event, IME/229, repeat, modifier,
hidden/inert, capture, other-modal, terminal-passthrough and focused native
Browser fences are unchanged. The dialog adds no RPC, protocol allocation,
migration, dependency or key/content logging.

The read-only Session Open Files / 파일 열기 action (`ShortcutId.OpenFiles`) uses
primary+E (Command+E on macOS, Control+E on Windows/Linux) for the active
selected nonembedded parent Session, including its composer and resource panes,
with ordinary editable input allowed. It is a read-only catalog entry outside the
seven editable IDs and invokes the original Files entry callback once. Repeated
opening selects the singleton Files tab without closing, duplicating or forcing
refresh of it. Original availability, drafts, mode, requests, observation
ownership and focus-local Escape stay unchanged, and an inactive session or
embedded Sidechat registers no independent Files action. It reuses the shared
`readOnlyShortcutSuppression` policy, which protects the unshifted primary key
`e` for this ID: any committed editable unshifted primary+E override suppresses
only this new default, in memory and across all scopes. Disabled and Shift+E
overrides do not suppress it, and removing or changing the committed override
restores it immediately. Conflict validation uses the same effective policy, so
existing E overrides stay valid without changes to preference bytes, the seven
IDs or native validation. Dispatch, Help, the read-only Settings catalog (which
follows the committed map) and the Files entry badge/ARIA share the effective
platform binding. The Files row in the Open tool dialog shows a decorative
muted shortcut hint (Command+E or Ctrl+E) that wraps inside the original row
geometry; the hint and its `aria-keyshortcuts` are omitted while suppressed, and
English/Korean Help and Settings explain the suppression. The preference
controller exposes an initial-read readiness flag that is false only while the
first read of the current bridge is unsettled and defaults to true outside a
provider. While it is false the empty startup overrides are not a committed map:
every `readOnlyShortcutSuppression` policy ID (Files primary+E and the same-race
Open tool primary+T) has no bindings, is disabled with the localized
`shortcuts.preferencesPending` reason, runs no callback and advertises no hint or
`aria-keyshortcuts`, consistently in dispatch, Help and the read-only Settings
catalog. Editable defaults are never gated. After the read settles, success,
read failure and the unavailable fallback use the committed-map rules above; later
refreshes and saves keep the last accepted bindings and never re-enter the gate.
Owned Help closes
before the callback and retains destination focus. Existing terminal, native
Browser, capture, modal, handled-event, repeat, IME, modifier and hidden/inert
fences remain. Opening Files adds no execution, recovery, RPC, migration or
native authority.

The fixed Session Open terminals / 터미널 열기 action uses primary+logical grave (`). Register it only for the active selected nonembedded Session, with ordinary editable input allowed and the original Sidechat parent-snapshot guard. Invoke the existing Terminals open action once, retaining the composer draft, original inventory, revision-bound reuse/create intent, pending/uncertain recovery and Worker ownership. Repeated opening selects the destination without closing it or replacing its controller. Help, the read-only Session Settings catalog and the original tool entry ARIA share the same platform binding. Accepted invocation from Help closes Help before the original callback and preserves destination focus. Grave matching has no physical Backquote fallback. Terminal input, focused native Browser pages, shortcut capture, unrelated modals and the existing handled/IME/repeat/extra-modifier/hidden/inert fences remain excluded. The seven editable actions and native preference format stay unchanged.

The read-only Session New terminal / 새 터미널 action (`ShortcutId.TerminalCreate`, `ShortcutTargetContext.Terminal`, priority 2, target input permission) uses primary+T and applies only while the visible terminal input host has focus. It runs the same additional-creation callback as + (Worker default shell, original session revision, fresh request identity, 24×80), selects and focuses the returned terminal tab only when no newer Session navigation (any selected-tab change recorded by the tab store's per-Session navigation generation, including leaving and returning to the origin terminal) happened after the request was sent; otherwise the user's later selection survives and the acknowledged terminal is only retained and listed for later explicit opening, and a request without its captured origin (for example after a remount) never selects. It is consumed before PTY delivery so an accepted chord sends no bytes. A matching chord blocked by inactive, opening, unsupported, busy, uncertain or archived creation gates is consumed without creation or terminal input. It has no editable preference, never reserves T globally and does not participate in the Open tool custom-override suppression; saved custom unshifted T overrides stay valid and unchanged. Help lists it with its terminal-focus restriction and cannot invoke it. The terminal input host and the renderer's input field carry `aria-keyshortcuts` derived from the effective platform binding. The handled/IME/repeat/AltGraph/extra-modifier/modal/hidden/inert fences remain.

Primary letter/digit matching and capture share one canonical resolver. Physical `KeyA`–`KeyZ` and `Digit0`–`Digit9` codes resolve to lowercase ASCII letters and digits before translated logical keys. Recognized codes take precedence over inconsistent `event.key`; unavailable or unrecognized codes retain the existing logical fallback, including Numpad behavior. Named Enter/Escape and default logical Help retain their existing rules and held-key release ownership. Stored `{key, shift}` chords, editable IDs, reservations and preference bytes remain unchanged. Input-layout selection alone does not block dispatch or capture; active composition remains excluded.

Logical `?` accepts the layout's producing Shift state and remains ordinary text in input, textarea, select, editable/combobox contexts. Ignore handled, composing, keyCode-229, AltGraph and repeated events. Ignore hidden/inert targets and terminal passthrough, except the fixed `SessionCloseTab` (primary+W) action and the numeric tab actions, which remain eligible from terminal focus and Keyboard Help; external native child views receive no new bridge. Visible modals, including the compact sidebar drawer, suspend background dispatch and help opening. The owned help dialog has only the action-dismissal exception described below. The wide sidebar region is not a modal. The help dialog cannot stack over another modal; Escape and Close dismiss only help.

The Settings-adjacent rail help button opens a 640px maximum-width central dialog with 24px padding, 12px corners and existing semantic light/dark tokens. Use Keyboard shortcuts / 키보드 단축키 and the localized current screen, followed by Common and screen-specific read-only lists. Show each registered binding, native behavior and disabled reason; show an explicit screen-specific empty state. Never execute a list row. English/Korean catalog changes update presentation without remounting the help or changing focus. On opening focus the named 40px Close button and contain Tab. On Escape or Close dismissal, restore the available opener or fall back to the current main. Retain 16px viewport margins, vertical scrolling and stacked rows at narrow widths/200% reflow. Device-local customization follows the preference boundary below; no dependency, API/schema/migration, OS permission or OS-global shortcut is added.

Validate matching, precedence/conflicts, inactive/disabled registration, editable/IME/repeat/passthrough behavior, native defaults, original form authority, modal suspension, focus restoration, Search drawer entry, locale changes and Strict Mode/connection disposal. Run package-local pnpm test and localization checks. Browser geometry/reflow checks and actual packaged CEF/platform acceptance remain separate; record revision, commands, results and unavailable native checks in PRs/issues/CI artifacts, not repository evidence documents.

Keyboard shortcuts help permits eligible existing non-input-target actions from its own dialog. Match current registrations with the same precedence, enabled and input rules. An accepted unambiguous action closes the native help dialog before its original callback runs exactly once; dismissal must not restore the opener over destination focus. Disabled/conflicting actions and excluded events keep help open with the existing event-consumption rules. Help focus never satisfies a background input target. Keyboard invocation of the effective committed Help binding opens held help and retains the originating physical key code, with the logical opening key as fallback when code is unavailable. Release of that original key closes held help even after Shift release; unrelated keyup is not consumed. Blur, hiding and provider disposal retire held ownership without reopening on return. Early Escape/Close/action dismissal retains the pressed identity until release, preventing reopening during that press; later release never restores stale opener focus. The rail button opens persistent help: Help presses/releases, blur and hiding neither convert nor close that instance. Locale changes retain the same help instance and focus. Other visible modals and compact navigation still block dispatch and help opening. Ordinary Escape and Close retain opener restoration or main fallback.

### Device-local shortcut preferences

- The feature gives Session and General Chat follow-up composers fixed unmodified Enter send and native Shift+Enter newline. Keep the customizable primary send chord independent, including disabled/custom overrides, seven editable IDs and the existing preference schema. Show fixed Enter alongside the editable Settings send row; Help and ARIA derive effective runtime declarations. Skill completion takes Enter first; preserve IME/229/repeat/handled/target/modal/native fences, original canSend/form/enqueue/receipt/draft/image/Plan Mode ownership and exact pending/uncertain locks. Creation, Search, terminal and mobile behavior remain separate.

Native IPC admission uses the closed `device-shortcuts` app permission and compiled read/update and closed capture command manifest, granted only to existing main/local-* and saved server-* product capabilities. Compiled ACL fixtures verify these admissions and remote/external/tray/auxiliary denial independently of retained original generation checks.

Keyboard shortcuts is the System category after Appearance. Its static typed
catalog lists Common, Session, New session / New Chat and Search
without visiting those screens. Help, NewSession, SessionFocus, SessionSend,
NewSessionFocus, NewSessionSend and SearchFocus support one primary chord,
optional Shift and an ASCII letter/digit or Enter, or an explicit disabled
override. An absent override selects the original default. SessionSend retains fixed unmodified Enter when its primary chord is changed or disabled; show this fixed binding alongside its editable Settings row. SessionNewline is read-only native Shift+Enter. Skill completion accepts a selectable suggestion before send dispatch. The original form/enqueue admission, IME/229/repeat/handled/target/modal/native fences and pending/uncertain request locks remain authoritative. Native newline,
Search Enter, panel Escape, generic modal Escape, Tab and editing retain their
original behavior; NewSessionSend always retains guarded plain Enter. The reserved,
editable and default primary chords are defined once in the shortcut chord table
below; native editing chords cannot be assigned. Unshifted primary+N is the editable New session default (Command+N on macOS, Control+N on Windows/Linux) and is not a native reservation or alias: native File > New Window has no accelerator, Shift+N is not an additional default alias, and the Keyboard Help and Settings native/fixed list has no New Window row. The renderer and the native validator treat N like any other editable chord: capturing unshifted N for Help overlaps the New session default and is rejected, while Help Shift+N is accepted. Saved overrides keep their meaning without migration or rewriting of `shortcuts.json`: an explicit Shift+N New session binding stays authoritative and unshifted N does not bypass it, a disabled override disables the action, and every stored document that was valid before this default change stays valid. Installations without a New session override receive unshifted N. An unshifted N override of a higher-priority screen action takes precedence over the New session default under the existing cross-priority dispatch rule. The renderer and native chord validators share one fixture table of accepted and rejected chords and override maps. The former New Window primary+T chord is editable; no native T alias remains, and the read-only Open tool and Open Files defaults yield to their T and E overrides. No palette, window action or tab action is added.

Capture becomes active only after original-product-window native admission and
an acknowledged native-loop replacement of the exact original app menu with an
accelerator-free menu. The closed Begin/Inspect/End operation owns the original
window instance, device preference revision and random token. Capture admission
expires after 15 seconds; the renderer stops accepting values conservatively
before that deadline. Expiry retains the native menu fence until original-token
inspection/End or independent native focus, visibility, disposal or Quit recovery;
never restore native accelerators beneath a stale focused capture. Native blur
restores the menu for other windows but retains an expired original-token
context; original focus return synchronously reinstalls its fence until End.
Disposal/Quit retires that context, and no other window may adopt it. Native
page-load Started also retires the original document context; capture commands
capture its document epoch synchronously at already-ACL-resolved invoke dispatch
before an async task can first poll, then recheck before native-loop admission and response, and hold
the retained verified preference revision through physical Begin admission
without disk I/O or CEF URL getters on that loop. Renderer
retirement completions check the original capture generation so a delayed duplicate
Cancel/blur result cannot dismiss or mark a newer capture uncertain. Uncertain
admission/retirement requires exact-token inspection, with no repeated Begin or
blind renewal. Retired-token tombstones reject a delayed Begin after End and are
bounded to 1024 captures per app lifetime, failing closed at that bound.

Retain and restore the exact original menu, including partial failure recovery;
an old retirement cannot replace a newer menu generation. Fence queued native
New/Close actions across capture epochs and native CloseRequested for the original
capturing window. An owned native watchdog joins the existing WindowActions Quit
boundary. Explicit native/Dock Quit still follows original joined shutdown and
its 35-second owned-sidecar grace. No global OS keyboard registration, RPC,
protocol allocation, migration or new editable action is added. Capture consumes
keyboard events before dispatch. Escape cancels capture and
returns to its initiating control; composing, repeated, AltGraph, Alt/Option,
modifier-only, mixed-primary and unsupported keys receive localized guidance.
Validate the complete catalog across inactive scopes, including unavailable
actions. Reject same-priority winning-action conflicts in overlapping contexts;
permit mutually exclusive screen reuse and preserve target/screen/global priority.
Dispatch, read-only help and ARIA resolve the same verified committed map.
Disable removes only the customizable chord; original buttons remain usable and
the rail help action remains available.

The editor owns only a category-local draft. Disable, per-action/all defaults
and capture do not commit. Save changes is explicit; Discard changes or departure
discards drafts. A clean view adopts concurrent commits; a dirty view retains its
draft and blocks Save until explicit reinspection/discard resolves the conflict.
Category disposal cannot cancel an admitted native save or replay business work.

`ShortcutPreferenceProvider` stays above connection and Settings state. Native
`shortcuts.json` is a separate bounded 4096-byte version-1 document with a revision
and at most the seven closed action overrides. Read/update commands use original
product-window authorization and expected-revision atomic replacement, with
ordered changed events only to authorized product windows. External native
children receive no preference authority/events. Preserve invalid/newer files,
last verified effective bindings, stale-revision guards and explicit read-only
reinspection after failed/uncertain writes. Missing storage uses defaults; browser
environments expose persistence-unavailable and never use Web Storage. Preferences
survive restart and server changes and remain excluded from server backups and
portable configuration. Logs contain only stable operation/problem/action/revision
metadata, never captured keys, chords, text or native content.

**Shortcut chord table.** This table is the single definition of the reserved,
editable and default primary chords. The renderer validator, the native validator,
the English/Korean fixed-shortcut help text, the shared chord fixture and every
other document must match it; the table-sync tests in the renderer and native
suites fail when any of them disagree. Primary means Command on macOS and Control
on Windows/Linux. Update this table first when a chord changes.

| Row                                   | Value                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Reserved unshifted primary keys       | `a` `b` `c` `h` `k` `m` `q` `v` `w` `x` `y` `z` `1` `2` `3` `4` `5` `6` `7` `8` `9` |
| Reserved Shift primary keys           | `v` `z`                                                                             |
| Keys named in the fixed shortcut help | `K` `W` `Q` `H` `M` `1–9`                                                           |
| Editable New session default          | `N`                                                                                 |
| Native New Window accelerator         | none                                                                                |
| Shift+N New session                   | explicit saved override only, never a default alias                                 |

Every other ASCII letter, digit or Enter, with or without Shift, is editable.
Reserved keys are product or native chords: K command menu, W close session tab,
B sidebar, Q/H/M native Quit/Hide/Minimize, 1–9 tab positions and A/C/V/X/Y/Z
native editing; Shift+V and Shift+Z are native editing as well.

English/Korean fixtures cover capture, draft isolation, dispatch/help/ARIA,
conflicts, publication/recovery, keyboard and compact/effective-reflow layouts.
Native store fixtures cover invalid files, atomic write uncertainty, restart and
revisions. Run frontend/localization and root Rust suites; keep those checks
separate from packaged macOS/Windows/Linux persistence and multi-window acceptance.

## In-app toast notifications

`src/toast-notifications.tsx`, `src/toast-store.ts` and the static scoped stylesheet own transient in-app notifications. Each authenticated connection mounts one `NotificationProvider` inside its existing connection identity boundary. `useNotifications` exposes `notify({ kind, message, id?, durationMs? }): string` and `dismiss(id)`. `ToastKind` is the closed success/info/warning/error enum. Publishing updates only the viewport subscription, not conversation/query consumers. Isolated consumers without a provider receive an inert controller; missing optional presentation cannot turn an acknowledged business operation into a failed mutation.

Display the viewport at 80 CSS pixels below the webview top, centered across the complete webview rather than its main-content column. Use a maximum 420px width, minimum 16px side margins, 16px internal padding, 10px corners, 14px wrapping text and a named 32px close button. Reuse the semantic light/dark theme colors and decorative repository-owned SVG icons. Static CSS preserves the production CSP, reduced motion, underlying layout and pointer access outside the toast cards. Long content scrolls within the available viewport height. Notification content is inert text, bounded to 4,096 code units, with no HTML, implicit links, raw-error projection, persistence, telemetry or content logging.

Default visible duration is 5,000ms; zero requires explicit dismissal. Durations must be nonnegative integers within the browser timer range. Hover, internal keyboard focus, document invisibility and a visible native modal suspend the remaining countdown independently. The wide nonmodal sidebar region does not suspend presentation; its compact modal drawer does. Modals hide the toast viewport until closure without moving focus or expiring its items. Same-ID publication replaces content and duration in place while retaining arrival order and current hover/focus pauses.

Show the first three arrivals and retain later arrivals in FIFO order. Countdown begins only when an item becomes visible. Bound the complete list to 20 entries; overflow drops the oldest queued entry while retaining the three visible entries. Ordinary navigation and same-identity reconnect preserve the provider. Connection replacement/unmount disposes its entries and timers, and its old controller ignores late publication. Strict Mode cleanup/setup restores an active empty store without duplicate viewports, retained callbacks or timer leaks.

Success, information and warning content use polite status announcements; errors use assertive alerts. Include a non-color kind label for assistive technology and keep icons decorative. Creation never takes focus. Close supports pointer, Tab/Enter/Space and Escape within the toast, preserving global dialog Escape behavior. Explicit focused dismissal returns to the last connected, available external focus target or the main content fallback.

Notification preferences and general configuration editors publish fixed safe success copy only from their existing acknowledged-save callbacks. A configuration response with a job takes precedence over any resource and remains an accepted operation, not an immediate save completion. Unknown acknowledgments, queued/unverified jobs, failed/uncertain requests, cancellation and late results from disposed Settings visits do not publish success. Existing repository edits complete only after the original successful job is verified and its output confirms the original repository with a revision newer than the submitted expected revision. Publish one localized repository success toast under that stable job ID, then invoke the existing saved callback to close, refresh and restore the opener. Other immediate saves retain their original request IDs. Preserve existing mutation receipts/retry rules, query invalidation, focus handoffs, detailed errors and job inspection.

These toasts neither request OS permission nor claim/report native delivery, modify Inbox read state or enable session actions. OS notifications, durable Inbox reservations, synchronized preferences and native activation retain their existing owners and contracts. No Connect API, migration, storage, native permission or package dependency is added. Component and browser layout checks remain separate from packaged CEF/platform acceptance; record validation in pull requests, issues and CI artifacts rather than repository evidence files.

## Runner Device heartbeat observations

Runner Device settings retains the highest accepted business revision for its
original Machine. A fresh successful same-ID read at that revision may replace
the displayed observation because server-projected heartbeat timestamps advance
without a configuration revision. Detect a new successful query response by its
data identity, not by requiring wall-clock timestamps to increase. Track query
freshness separately from the business revision. At each Settings opening,
baseline the query result already in cache so it cannot be mistaken for a read
accepted during that Settings lifetime. Do not replay cached data over a newer
acknowledged mutation. If a fresh read and acknowledgement arrive together,
accept the read only when its business revision exceeds the acknowledgement;
equal or lower reads stay fenced. A compatible later read can update the
heartbeat, while lower revisions, failed reads and malformed or foreign
resources cannot replace the accepted configuration. Read failures retain the
existing error and action restrictions.

Equal-revision heartbeat refreshes preserve executable-path drafts and their
original request revisions. Only a changed business revision makes those drafts
stale. Keep the original inspection job, uncertain request and exact retry owner;
observation refresh grants no inspection, execution or cleanup authority. Dispose
the accepted observation with its original Settings task/connection lifetime,
and follow the [heartbeat projection contract](protos-delidev-v1-contract.md#machine-heartbeat-read-projection).

## Model request Diagnostics panel

The feature adds an explicit Diagnostics panel beside the retained session conversation. It uses generated owner/client Connect Query after `REQUEST_DIAGNOSTICS_V1` capability validation, with an optional exact execution UUID filter, explicit refresh and 50-record pages. Validate the entire page's original session/execution, closed source/operation/state/error/settings, identity spelling, timestamps and precise counters before rendering. Validate catalog and builtin reviewer identity independently: an unspecified attribution requires the exact catalog `model` (bounded `nativeId`, provider/subscription match, no deprecated `modelId`); the closed `CODEX_REVIEWER` attribution requires no `model`, no `modelId`, no subscription service, the Codex harness and the proxy-HTTP source and renders the canonical reviewer model `gpt-5.6-luna`; any other attribution value or malformed catalog record rejects the whole page, so a valid reviewer record never blanks adjacent catalog records. Keep native input selection/effective settings separate from proxy request/provider observations, and unavailable fields separate from zero/false. A send claim cannot prove provider acceptance; native terminal metadata cannot confirm native cleanup. Historical absence cannot be reconstructed. Escape/Close returns focus to Diagnostics and preserves the composer; inactive diagnostic queries are canceled/disposed. No mutation intent, automatic retry, payload display, usage reconstruction or public opener is introduced. See the [diagnostics contract](cmds-delidev-diagnostics-contract.md) and validation records in the integration PR.

## Session Diagnostics spacing

Session Diagnostics shares one 32px outer inset and left-aligned 1040px maximum
content width across the original technical portal and request diagnostics.
Top-level sections use normal semantic-theme dividers and 32px spacing. Headings
use 16px text with 16px below; body text uses 14px and 1.5 line height. Fact rows
use a 200px label column, a flexible value column, a 24px column gap and a 12px
row gap without default definition-value indentation. Complete references wrap;
ordered accounts keep their original numbering and order.

Below 640px of available Diagnostics panel width, the inset is 16px and facts
stack with 4px between each label and value and 12px between pairs, for both
wrapped `div` pairs and flat sibling `dt`/`dd` pairs (the last pair has no
trailing gap). Request diagnostics has no second inset. Its top divider, 16px
