### Standalone Pull requests

The Pull requests rail item selects `Surface.PullRequests`; it does not open Settings. The sidebar appends bounded 50-resource repository catalog reads through shared scroll continuation; it retains safe display projections and at most three complete payload pages with original-token restoration. Repository selection remains keyed by exact local UUID internally. Visible names, accessible labels and the separate Details region omit that UUID; equal names use stable exact-ID presentation numbers in the connection-owned view. Numbers survive catalog reorder, removal and same-identity reconnect, are not reused, and reset with connection identity replacement. User-supplied names retain their original bytes. The initial state has no selected repository. Selection automatically loads page one only after current authenticated resource metadata validates its supported schema, selected profile and GitHub owner/name. Missing configuration shows existing guidance without a GitHub read.

Different repository selection resets Open state, empty search and PR page size 20. State and page-size changes apply immediately; a page-size change replaces the existing `scopeKey`, so it resets the current repository/state/search chain to page one, disposes the selected PR and old enrichment, aborts old reads and rejects late old responses, while the same value, locale changes and rendering repeat no read. Valid trimmed plain title/body search applies after a 300 ms debounce outside IME composition; invalid search cancels pending application and shows the existing error. Equivalent trimmed terms, same-repository selection, Details, locale, layout and harmless rerenders do not repeat reads. Leaving cancels timers and disposable reads; returning reloads page one with retained filters. Original query/revision fences reject late responses. Automatic activation never closes the drawer or changes focus. The PR page-size select offers exactly 10, 20 and 50 (default 20) and is the only page-size UI. 50 is enabled only when `GetStatus` advertises System `PULL_REQUEST_PAGING_50_V1`; otherwise the option is disabled with localized guidance (`pull-requests.pageSizeUnsupported`, or `pull-requests.pageSizeChecking` before status settles), a held 50 value falls back to 20 and no 50-item request is ever sent. The capability is trusted only from a `GetStatus` observation made through the current transport during the current connection epoch (the App-provided counter that increments on every verified connection attempt): a same-identity reconnect that preserves the query client, whether or not it keeps the transport object, discards the previous peer's observation in the same render, and a retained 50-item result scope pauses its reads until the new peer confirms the capability, so a downgraded or replaced peer never receives a 50-item refresh. Retain cumulative scroll continuation, detail/back and deliberate refresh. Changed repository selection immediately clears previous content; changed filters leave the existing result labeled with its last applied conditions. Reuse validated PR detail, immutable diff and complete published feedback in the workspace. Shared backend/CLI Checks, statuses, rules, required CI, reviewer verification and retained problem/remediation history remain intact; their technical actions are absent from the ordinary workspace. Do not add cross-repository aggregation, GitHub query syntax or execution capabilities. Repository configuration association follows the inline setup contract below. Repository settings targets Repositories in the current Settings visit through its explicit category-entry workflow, creating a fresh visit when Settings was inactive. Never restore abandoned Settings-local drafts. A selected repository with incomplete GitHub configuration retains a GitHub profiles button alongside inline association or current-repository setup guidance. It targets the existing Git Profiles category through the explicit GitProfiles destination, closes the compact drawer and transfers focus through the existing App navigation. No selection, unavailable selected resource or complete configuration shows no shortcut. The GitHub profiles navigation action performs no PR query, profile mutation, token validation or repository association; ordinary Settings metadata reads remain allowed. Keep English “GitHub profiles” and Korean “GitHub 프로필”, 40px controls, visible keyboard focus and responsive wrapping.

The approved name-only redesign replaces the feature's always-visible UUID presentation and remains scoped to `Surface.PullRequests` on the existing sidebar root. Keep the same rail, pane, portal, controller/query instances and drawer, with the independently scrolling list above normal bottom padding. Order the content as one semantic Pull requests h2/action row with a trailing icon-only repository Refresh, glyph/name rows with separate Details buttons or the decorative folder empty block, shared continuation, a divided Query options section for the selected repository, and the full-width secondary Repository settings action. Selection and Details are sibling buttons, never nested. One expanded repository UUID stays in bounded connection memory across navigation and same-identity reconnect, clears with identity replacement, and exposes a labeled region through `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`. Display only the already-loaded configured GitHub owner/name in that region; never display or announce the internal local UUID. Missing mappings show configuration absence. Expansion never selects a repository, submits a form, fetches metadata or persists state. Do not add raw inspected URLs, credentials or checkout paths. A successful empty catalog page says exactly **No repositories on this page.**, never that the entire catalog is empty. Preserve page-scoped loading/failure/cached-refresh states. Selected row groups retain pale blue `#e7efff`, with `aria-pressed` on the selection button and original-name presentation labels in accessible names. Stable numbers distinguish equal names without exposing internal UUIDs. Decorative outline SVGs are accessibility-hidden. Automatic-load guidance remains visible with both empty and selected states; no Load pull requests button remains. Repository Details alone uses an icon-only disclosure: no independent border, background or shadow in resting, hover, selected or expanded states. Center its existing 14px right/down chevron within the trailing 40px column with at least 40px height, muted/selected tokens and visible inset focus. Preserve DisclosureButton/DisclosureContent, separate selection, exact identity, aria associations, connection-memory expansion and collapse focus restoration; expansion performs no read, persistence, selection or drawer close. Other disclosures retain their boxed presentation.

Repository Details uses a row-owned read-only, nonmodal manual native popover inside the original compact drawer DOM. Its fixed top-layer box contributes no flow height. Opening, switching and closing preserve all later row/control rectangles within one CSS pixel, and preserve sidebar scrollHeight, clientHeight and scrollTop. Prefer an 8px gap to the row's right; otherwise use available space below or above. Clamp to an 8px visual viewport inset, wrap metadata and scroll inside the card. An oversized wrapped opener with no usable vertical side space uses the available viewport height. Existing typography, theme tokens and the icon-only 40px trigger remain authoritative.

Only one original repository popup is visible. Trigger activation toggles it or reopens its retained identity after presentation dismissal. Escape from that opener or its popup closes only the card and restores the surviving opener without scrolling; unrelated inputs/dialogs retain their own Escape behavior. Outside pointer or keyboard activation dismisses visible details without taking focus from the activated control. Hidden, clipped or removed openers and inactive panes retire visible presentation. Keep the original expanded UUID in connection memory through navigation and same-identity reconnect; never attach it to a different row. Dispose native layers, observers and listeners with their row owner. No fallback may insert a details panel into the list flow. Details performs no read, selection, submission, persistence or mutation. The separate `pr-list-cards-layout.fixture.tsx` and `scripts/test-pr-cards-layout.mjs` exercise actual App presentation with host-supplied Playwright/Chrome through `DELIDEV_LAYOUT_PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE` and optional `DELIDEV_LAYOUT_BROWSER_CHANNEL`. Optional `DELIDEV_PR_CARDS_SCREENSHOT_DIR` output stays outside the repository. Temporary bundles/server/browser are disposed after checks; the fixture grants no native/account authority and stays outside release inputs.

When Pull requests becomes inactive, cancel and remove its disposable GitHub observation/history reads. Returning restores control selections and shows Pending PR actions alongside automatic page-one reactivation. Retain only target IDs and confirmation identity/revision in connection state; keep immutable mutation requests in the bounded existing registry. Exact receipt retries remain available without reconstructing payloads from a new result or forcing a GitHub read. Never keep full GitHub response documents solely to preserve a read. Unsent confirmations cannot authorize a new mutation without fresh matching evidence. Only unsent drafts/confirmations may be canceled; pending, in-flight or uncertain actions cannot be cleared by navigation or repository/PR replacement.

Across all surfaces, distinguish first loading, successful empty pages, empty later pages, permission/authentication errors, connection failures and stale same-scope data. Never show old-scope rows as the new selection or claim a complete inventory from one bounded page. Navigation, filtering, collapse and paging remain read-only; existing explicit mutations keep their original revisions, authority and exact retry payloads. Native visual, focus and OS acceptance remains separate from component/browser evidence.

### Usage

Usage integration validation must independently settle the initial summary read and the current General Chat filtered read. Observe only the exact summary method and filter classification through the original transport; retain response-received, pending, success and failure flags without recording request or response content. Delay filtered response delivery, prove the current read has not succeeded while the surface is busy/loading, then release delivery and require the latest matching successful read, `aria-busy=false`, no current loading element and no alert before cleanup. Applied conditions and retained coverage text alone cannot establish current success. Preserve General Chat scope, unavailable actual cost, no exact response usage and incomplete-coverage assertions after settlement. Transport errors must rethrow and cannot satisfy success. Release the test delivery gate in `finally` while retaining component, query-client and fixture cleanup ownership. These fixtures do not establish native, account or platform acceptance.

The Usage surface follows the [exact native usage contract](cmds-delidev-usage-contract.md) through direct generated Connect Query. It defaults to 30 server-relative days and supports local-time range, session/project/account/provider/model and General Chat filters with immediate valid selection application, 300ms date validation and explicit Reset. Keep drafts mounted across navigation. The summary shows arbitrary-precision known subtotals, per-counter unavailable responses, original identity groups with optional current labels, accepted executions missing telemetry, unavailable actual cost and separate currency-denominated historical estimate subtotals. Resume/legacy/child/unsupported telemetry cannot appear as zero or complete. Usage history row Details show the exact native model ID verbatim (never a generated `Model N` label, and the unavailable copy when absent), and register every rendered group's session, project, account, provider and model names before reading labels so duplicate observed names are numbered on the first committed render. A model's presentation identity is scoped by its provider and subscription service together with its native ID, because a native ID is unique only within its source; the same native ID under different sources numbers separately. Every Usage subview that labels a model (the history table, Claude and OpenCode native accounting groups and model rows, Grok closed-input accounting groups and model rows, and the Model prices tab) must derive that scoped identity from the same helper so the shared registry never attributes one observed name to two identities of the same model. The Model prices tab registers every loaded pricing model and its matching observed name before reading any picker label, so duplicate names are numbered consistently on the first committed render. Usage history directs users to Model prices, or opens the exact original model from a retained record. Usage → Model prices reads current model/price revisions and creates an explicit source/date/currency/input-mode/rate/exclusion version. Nullable decimal fields preserve blank versus zero; stale drafts and exact uncertain requests remain retained. Source descriptions render as inert text. Historical Usage details expose retained price versions and priced/missing/unsupported category counts, with exact amount strings and no client-side recomputation. No complete-category count implies complete telemetry, verified spend or budget compliance. Refresh failures label cached values, and opening a session never starts execution.

The feature adds a visible **Token Usage** page while preserving the Usage navigation entry. It presents an overall known-total/input/output hierarchy, the remaining three token measures, explicit measured/unavailable response counts, incomplete-coverage evidence and unavailable actual cost above historical estimates. Filter drafts live in the Usage context pane, persist across navigation, and distinguish pending/invalid date edits from the displayed valid query; Reset remains explicit. Datetime-local values use a frozen detected IANA zone for each applied request and calendar bucket; UTC is the explicit fallback. Applied timestamps are first server-retention times with an exclusive upper bound. The existing session table retains its grouping/order, full source identities, disclosures, and open-session navigation.

The feature presents the empty recorded response subtotal as zero in the six top-level cards only when all measures are present, empty and have zero measured/unavailable counts. Missing/inconsistent evidence stays unavailable. Keep incomplete-coverage warnings, detail/chart semantics, precision and stale refresh behavior under the [usage contract](cmds-delidev-usage-contract.md).

Daily analytics show clipped chronological zone-local buckets with exact response evidence; model analytics show the top five measured original provider/model groups and the server's Other aggregate, while full data tables retain every model identity including unmeasured groups. Both data tables show all six exact measures and their measured/unavailable counts; wide table regions remain keyboard-scrollable. Charts distinguish no records, unavailable totals, partial known totals and measured zero without relying on color alone. SVG geometry uses bounded integer ratios; visible numeric output retains exact decimal strings. Hover/focus details, one keyboard entry point per chart (arrows, Home/End, Escape), and semantic data tables expose the same values. Production styling uses static CSS and SVG attributes, preserving the existing CSP and adding no chart dependency. If an older server has no `analytics`, existing summary/table/cost surfaces stay available and the page states that charts need a server update; present empty analytics means a supported empty query.

The feature adds a separate Verified Grok closed inputs section to Usage. The existing generated summary query explicitly requests NATIVE_UNITS_V1 and checks its echo; old servers keep the response surface with update guidance. Exact BigInt display, native unit counts, original session/project/account/model/provider attribution and semantic daily/model/session tables come from one server snapshot. Show every original project ID alongside its optional current label, preserving identity across duplicate labels and renames. Exclude native-only groups/models from the response detail table and response-chart model inventory, including View data. Retain the no-response detail state when no response groups remain, preserve the complete analytics snapshot for Grok accounting, and keep response groups/models with unavailable counters in the response views. Do not add these inputs to Codex response cards/charts, renderer aggregates, historical price estimates or budgets. Applied conditions explicitly label response first-retention time. The Grok section separately explains that its filters and daily buckets use the server's first retention of verified completion after confirmed cleanup. Daily Grok tables display both exact localized interval endpoints, including seconds and offsets, in the returned IANA timezone; Until is explicitly exclusive, and clipped partial days must not appear as complete days. Retain mounted filters, stale-data disclosure and session navigation.

The feature replaces the previous feature navigation with topmost Overview (default), Usage history and Model prices tabs. English/Korean labels are Overview / 개요, Usage history / 사용 기록 and Model prices / 모델 단가. Use the [shared tab strip presentation](#shared-tab-strip-presentation): unboxed semantic items with muted inactive text, semantic selected text, a 2px underline, shared baseline, 40px controls and visible focus. Left/Right/Home/End select and focus without changing filters, summary reads or execution authority. Narrow tab strips scroll horizontally.

Overview shows the applied period, concise incomplete/stale notices and separate Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode and Grok Build rows. Read their exact server values without adding tools, currencies, accounting units or overlapping reports. Codex response totals and historical estimates remain available independently of native accounting profile negotiation; Claude Code and OpenCode rows require the negotiated profile and complete native source summaries. Absent Claude totals remain unavailable. Grok evidence is labelled input tokens, never an inferred total or price. No-record numeric cells use an em dash with status; reported zero stays zero. Separate estimated amounts by source and currency and state that they are not actual charges. A retained source choice exposes source-specific daily trends. How usage is counted links the original accounting definitions and exact records; Coverage details retains every original coverage counter and caveat.

Usage history preserves the ordered response records, four original response cards and secondary breakdown, expanded keyboard-accessible daily/model charts and exact data tables, independent native source records, daily/model/session details and immutable historical pricing. Supported empty native sources remain initially collapsed with unavailable/no-record warnings; populated sources remain expanded. Keep user disclosure choices and unsupported/inconsistent evidence guidance. Model links select their exact original model/provider/service identity in Model prices without changing applied filters. Explicit response and native model activation moves focus once to the rendered selected Model prices tab, only while Usage remains active and the connected destination has no hidden ancestor. Departure consumes the pending handoff; passive query, refresh, locale and retained-state updates preserve current focus.

Model prices replaces the standalone Model details block and its navigation buttons. Its authorized configured-model selector and current manual pricing editor are independent of the historical range. Rates, currency, source/date, exclusions, original identities and immutable version remain available through Price details. The compact rate summary follows the input pricing mode: a UNIFORM basis shows its input rate with the cache-inclusive wording (`Uniform input (cache included)` / `균일 입력(캐시 포함)`) and no independent cached-input row, since uniform input already includes cached input; CACHED_DISCOUNT shows the separate cached rate, a known zero or Unavailable when absent; unknown or absent bases keep explicit Unknown mode / Unavailable states without borrowing another rate. Nullable rates stay distinct from zero, and stored versions, estimates and queries are unchanged. Deleted, retired or changed original identities retain read-only historical prices. Keep manual editor drafts and exact uncertain requests mounted across tab/navigation/Refresh. Automatic controls require separately implemented server support; this UI-only change exposes manual pricing. Group Time range/Scope/Source in the scrolling context pane above fixed Reset and retain automatic filters, exact bounds, timezone, query ownership and drawer focus. No new usage RPC, migration, native change, polling or external pricing fetch is added.

The feature makes the response section within Usage history trend-first. A compact strip shows dates, the frozen IANA zone and scope. Its keyboard Details retains precise original endpoints, offsets, exclusive Until, all exact filter IDs and first-retention-time guidance. Incomplete coverage stays visible; both exact missing execution/context-action counts and full caveats remain in Coverage details. Session rows retain eight data columns and a Details action. Use readable session/project, account and model/source labels without exposing raw identifiers in compact cells. Row Details preserves every original identity, all six counter measures with measured/unavailable evidence and the complete historical estimate reasons and currency subtotals. Session and model/pricing actions retain their exact identities and guards. No currency conversion, ranking reconstruction, record truncation, sorting or new reads are allowed.

At widths below 759px, the same mounted rows become labelled stacked records; wider tables provide contained keyboard scrolling. Right-align numeric cells. Use 14px/20px body text, 12px/18px supporting text, 40px controls, 8px corners and 24px section gaps. Existing bounded SVG chart keyboard inspection and exact semantic tables remain available without a trends disclosure. Preserve mounted tabs/disclosures across navigation/Refresh, all loading/empty/unsupported/failed/stale states, strict empty-summary zeros, incomplete coverage, native separation and automatic filter/query/focus lifetimes. This presentation adds no RPC, migration, dependency, native authority, polling or content/filter logging.

### Local native connection

Registered Local product documents (`main`/`local-*`) receive `local-bootstrap` under exact native role and instance admission. They share the process-owned launch observation and connection, without repeating startup or pairing when another window opens. The feature treats each fresh trusted main desktop process as intentional local Start. The host locates the bundled sibling `delidev` binary, runs Go-owned `server desktop-launch` once with the exact app/development origins, then `device pair-local` and `device inspect` against its fixed private `desktop-client` subdirectory. This off-UI-thread operation belongs to the host lifetime and finishes before supervision begins. Additional Local windows, CEF helpers and Saved windows cannot create another automatic launch or supervisor. The resident host operations and current lifetime boundary follow [app-owned sidecar shutdown](#app-owned-sidecar-shutdown). Go owns singleton startup, compatibility, private filesystem validation and all pairing mutations. A newly admitted server runs in that original Go child; compatible live reuse exits the controller without transferring server ownership. The native host independently checks the returned metadata before reading that one credential file; only the separate revocable client credential enters the trusted renderer. It never returns the owner token or permits renderer-selected executable/argv/filesystem paths.

Registered Local product documents additionally access `inspect_local_registration` and `recover_local_registration` under their original native role, instance and connection authority. Capture that authority before asynchronous work and recheck it before returning or adopting its result. A recovery result updates process-wide supervision only after the original Local window role, instance and revision checks pass; a stale or rejected result leaves the supervised connection unchanged. These commands call the closed Go local-registration operations, never accept paths/argv/origin overrides, preserve canonical UUIDs and decimal uint64 revisions, and do not start/stop a server. Recovery passes only the original device/revision/request identity. After publication, native code independently reinspects the fixed client metadata and reads only its new client credential. The owner token never crosses native IPC; saved-server windows have neither capability.

The persistent native Connection panel exposes Check desktop registration, reached through Settings > System > Connections or startup Troubleshooting. A verified revoked registration offers Re-register this desktop, with explicit confirmation that the old registration remains revoked, server sessions/settings/Workers are retained, and adopting the new identity clears window-local drafts and pending actions without resuming sessions. Unknown/file/permission/owner failures cannot offer speculative replacement. A lost receipt retains the exact request through dialog hiding; after app restart, inspection recovers the same pending request from Go. A fresh non-recovering inspection of a different device/revision on the same server retires an obsolete pending request and its confirmation; a revoked replacement requires a new explicit confirmation/request, while an authorized replacement offers no further registration. Preserve the exact uncertain request when inspection still identifies its original registration. A conflicting in-progress request or foreign server remains an evidence error and cannot discard pending ownership. Double clicks are serialized. Both native registration commands pin the current private desktop runtime endpoint through a Go-side precondition checked before recovery intent or pairing, so another loopback listener cannot be replaced before an incompatible-endpoint error. Successful adoption verifies the new direct Connect transport and disposes the old connection's memory cache. There is no automatic registration on mount, polling, reconnect or failure.

Local connection and registration permission errors share guidance covering device authorization, file ownership and owner-only access. A permission denial does not establish that the owner cannot read a file: a readable directory with group/other access is also rejected. On macOS/Linux, the guidance specifies 0700 private directories and 0600 private files, with existing data preserved before retrying. Keep the existing native error classification and strict Go privacy checks; the app never automatically changes permissions, resets data or offers replacement without verified revoked-client evidence.

Paired devices labels the current client and omits its Revoke action. The confirmation component independently blocks self-revocation submission/retry, including a stale mounted confirmation. Other devices keep their existing revision checks and exact retry behavior. This is an app UX guard; authenticated owner/other-client administration and the existing Device RPC remain available.

The initial Local window receives exactly one native-selected loopback origin before creation. The resident CLI binds `127.0.0.1:0` directly and returns the actual address, a UUID-v7 execution generation and a fresh 256-bit proof key through its private pipe. The same main process pins that port across server Start and CLI replacement. The bounded native stdin writer runs off the UI loop; a blocked write cannot delay cancellation, the original-child force deadline or observation of exit. An occupied pinned port is an error; no alternate port or existing listener is adopted. A running external server or native service owning the same data folder is preserved and reported as a conflict. Only a fresh admitted desktop launch may replace stopped historical listener configuration. The root still defaults to the platform configuration directory plus `delidev`, with an explicit absolute native `--data-dir` selecting another scope. Saved connection addresses remain independent.

One native supervision loop shares the resident session with all windows and native helpers. Healthy and stopped scopes are checked every five seconds; transient failures retain exponential equal-jitter delays capped at 30 seconds and incompatible states retain the one-minute inspection limit. Replacement requires observed exit of the retained original child and reuses the pinned port. It uses `runtime.ensure` and never replays an uncertain mutation or clears explicit Stop. Only a fresh main-process launch or explicit advanced Start may reopen stopped intent. Renderer remount, Retry, show/focus and tray restoration cannot do so. Native status exposes only closed states, bounded attempts/delay and redacted failures.

The desktop offers explicit server stop through direct authenticated Connect with retained mutation identity and a description of its effect on clients/Workers. Accepted stop, automatic-restart suppression and session cleanup remain distinct. Advanced local Start uses the existing closed native bootstrap command. Startup Retry is an explicit serialized native action using the resident `runtime.retry` operation; it never clears stopped intent. Renderer connection verification retries at most three transient status reads and never repeats a native startup/pairing operation or product mutation automatically. Reconnection to the same server/device/endpoint/credential revalidates active read queries without replacing drafts or pending mutation identities; an identity change still clears connection-owned state. Server Stop joins only the internal server; the resident CLI remains available for status, cleanup and explicit Start. A new runtime generation refreshes transport proof while same server/device/credential identity retains connection-owned drafts and request identities. After proof, only the transport copy of Authorization is wrapped with AES-256-GCM under a domain-separated key derived from the private execution secret. Fresh 96-bit nonces and authenticated generation/server/method/path/query context prevent a raced port successor from reading the original bearer. The matching listener unwraps before the unchanged bearer middleware. Stable tokens, product Connect framing and Saved transports retain their existing formats; no public schema or migration is added.

The host retains the joined launch outcome in memory. `launch_local` observes it without replaying startup or pairing; pending observations return no credential. Before returning an earlier successful result, Go's read-only `server desktop-status` checks current running intent and authenticated compatibility, and native code reinspects the original fixed client identity. Direct renderer status verification rejects stopping servers. Explicit Start and registration recovery update the host's connection observation only after their own native checks. Quit cancels and joins short controller/supervision work and applies the owned-sidecar shutdown boundary below; independent Workers and retained session data remain preserved.

Desktop launch and supervision hold the native server-service control lock before the startup and lifecycle locks, retain it through admitted startup and release it at readiness, and recheck original registration admission before intent publication and spawn. Compatible live service-owned servers may be reused without modifying service intent or registration. Stopped/unresolved registered scopes block detached launch with the stable `service-managed` classification; malformed or foreign private evidence remains an evidence/privacy failure. Ordinary explicit `server start` keeps its separate semantics. No app launch installs, starts, removes or repairs a native service.

Ordinary startup shows **Starting DeliDev…**, followed by the authenticated product after version/server verification. Failure uses an accessible product explanation, **Retry** and **Troubleshooting**. Stable missing-sidecar, timeout, permission, incompatible, credential, service-ownership and evidence distinctions appear only in troubleshooting. Sidebar connectivity uses generic current/disconnected wording without versions, lifecycle buttons or retry internals. Tray groups the main window as **This computer**, preserving timestamps, staleness, counts and saved names. Its explicit exit action reads **Quit DeliDev**; quitting stops app-owned sidecars while preserving borrowed runtimes, independent Workers and retained session data.

### App-owned sidecar shutdown

The Local Connect fetch first requests a fresh bounded challenge proof from
`/__delidev_desktop_runtime` without bearer or redirects. HMAC-SHA256 binds the
private key, execution generation, stable server ID and random 32-byte challenge.
Only a valid proof permits a generation-bound encrypted bearer transport copy to that exact origin; the original bearer is restored only by the matching listener before existing authentication. Native connection
responses include `runtime_generation` and `runtime_key`; neither is persisted or
logged. The exact runtime origin replaces fixed-port native checks and CSP entries.
Saved windows continue to use their selected exact origins without Local relocation.
Public Connect messages and SQLite versions remain unchanged.

Original device IDs/tokens, pairing documents and recovery receipts retain their
original bytes and logical addresses. The owner-private `desktop-runtime.json`
contains only current execution transport authority and is excluded from ordinary
`server.json` discovery. Retirement checks the original generation. Explicit
fixed Local Workers validate their retained local-pairing ownership and the immutable
owner-side pairing grant (server, endpoint and pairing identity must equal the saved
credential and journal) before following the locator or persisting the marker; their durable non-secret opt-in marker refuses obsolete-address
fallback after retirement. Saved/remote Workers never acquire this authority.

The trusted main process owns at most one resident `server desktop-host --control-version 2` CLI. CEF helpers route through their native entry point before any product spawning; all Local/Saved windows, pairing, recovery, state reads, browser observers and native update assistance share this session. The closed version-2 newline frames distinguish request UUID, operation enum, response and cancellation. They cannot execute arbitrary commands, paths or environment values. Requests are limited to 256 KiB, replies to 128 KiB and pending operations to 32. Mutation admission is serialized; four read slots and the immediate cancellation/shutdown path keep final browser discovery independent of long mutations. Routine deadlines remain 40 seconds, Go startup remains an aggregate 35 seconds and explicit native update preparation retains its bounded 660-second allowance. Logs remain separate from control stdout and drain continuously.

Fresh launch, explicit Retry and Ensure send `runtime.launch`, `runtime.retry` and
`runtime.ensure` through that retained session. Pairing and subsequent launch
observations use the same session and return its verified runtime transport.
They must not invoke the retired `server desktop-host --mode` controller or
start a separate short-lived inspector without the original runtime context.

Native code retains one original child/control session before readiness. A persistent spawning thread owns its process handle and joins observed exit before replacement. Windows atomically attaches the CLI to an unnamed non-inheritable kill-on-close Job via `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST`; silent child breakaway excludes independent Workers. The pinned native nightly toolchain supplies the narrow Windows attribute-list API. Linux installs a parent-death signal on the child from the retained spawning thread. macOS observes the original parent with `EVFILT_PROC/NOTE_EXIT` and also treats control EOF as shutdown. Parent loss, malformed control or failed delivery cancels host work and owned server cleanup; a host-side 35-second bound forces host exit if joins stall. Independent Worker process ownership is unchanged.

Normal Quit immediately fences new requests, server starts and CLI replacement and cancels pending interactive operations. The existing tracked worker preserves the CEF event loop while joining final bounded browser removal discovery through the same session. It then requests `runtime.shutdown`, suppresses only the original startup generation and joins the server and remaining host operations. The browser observer has independent local admission but cannot spawn after fencing. Shutdown/cancellation are processed outside mutation admission. Pipe EOF and desktop crash/forced exit now terminate the app-owned CLI/server; they never grant authority over external server PIDs or endpoints.

The native shutdown deadline remains 35 seconds, independent of startup and product/native cleanup deadlines. Normal Quit computes one absolute monotonic deadline at entry and shares it across the resident host session and app-owned Worker phases: graceful requests (`runtime.shutdown` to the resident host, the stop frame to hosted Workers) start together for every retained original child at the beginning of that window, each phase measures its remaining grace against the same deadline, and no phase receives a fresh 35-second allowance after another consumed the budget, so a hung host plus a hung Worker are both forced within one aggregate 35-second grace plus bounded scheduling and exit overhead. On expiry, force only the retained original child and observe its actual exit. An uncertain force/exit result retains ownership and reports uncertainty. Repeated Quit shares one operation off the UI loop; native exit remains gated by host completion and raw-browser close proofs. Close-to-tray keeps the main process, CLI and server alive. Normal setup failures also join the owned host. Crash and forced desktop termination no longer preserve app-owned sidecars; independent Workers, CLI/service servers and Saved/remote servers remain independent.

Structured logs distinguish request, restart suppression, joined server cleanup, force request and confirmed/unconfirmed process exit. Forced process exit does not prove native/session cleanup; original data, protected ownership and recovery state remain authoritative. Failure to force or observe exit retains original handles and reports uncertainty without a PID fallback. Actual macOS/Windows/Linux Quit and packaged CEF shutdown remain separate acceptance from controlled process fixtures and compilation. Record validation in PRs/issues and CI logs/artifacts, never repository evidence documents.

The 20 Settings categories are retained; Diagnostics is displayed as **Connections**. Its labelled Connection subsection opens the same persistent native connection panel used before transport. Local lifecycle controls, registration inspection/recovery and Saved servers live there. The panel and connection-scoped Stop mutation registry stay mounted outside the disposable Settings visit, so original confirmations and uncertain request bytes survive hiding and category/navigation changes. Registration confirmation visibility follows the panel without discarding its identity. Native dialogs retain Escape, contained focus and opener restoration. Doctor has its own read-only diagnostics subsection; selecting it never repairs or mutates. Saved windows place their verification and Show local window controls in their own advanced panel and remain connect-only.

The server launch amendment introduces no feature flag, persisted startup preference, migration, product RPC, new dependency, automatic revoked-client replacement, permission repair, reset, account login, Resume or harness activity. Automatic Worker startup follows the separate main-window Worker management contract below. Logs contain bounded lifecycle phases and stable classifications, never credentials, child output or private paths. Record actual native/platform acceptance and unresolved gaps in the feature, its pull requests and CI logs/artifacts under the root DeliDev validation policy.

Navigation is restricted to the app entry document, including Tauri’s empty custom-scheme path. External navigations and popups are denied. The main window CSP permits only the retained session's exact local RPC origin and native IPC; only the development policy permits the fixed development HMR connection and inline styles. The app webview is ephemeral. The DeliDev app icon uses a background-extracted version of the supplied 1254×1254 RGBA PNG as its canonical source: the outer dark rounded-square tile and the central dark play triangle are both transparent, while the colored ribbon retains its original shape, gradient, and proportions. The canonical artwork is uniformly enlarged to 1.2× its supplied size around canvas center `(627, 627)`, with zero rotation and the unchanged 1254×1254 canvas; only the outer transparent margins shrink. This approved enlargement is already baked into the canonical source and must not be repeated during export. Preserve all visible artwork without clipping. Derive the 256×256 RGBA PNG for the native window and tray and the Windows ICO entries at 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, and 256 pixels from this source, preserving alpha and clean antialiased edges. Tauri's explicit bundle icon list includes both PNGs and the ICO so the macOS bundle can derive an ICNS from the full-resolution source. Preserve the 1254×1254 canvas and the `icon-source@2x.png` density marker: the pinned bundler downsizes it to 1024px, which ICNS supports as 512 points at retina density only; a density-one entry fails packaging.

Icon export validation reads the final 256px PNG and all six ICO frames after their last conversion. Require near-opaque samples inside the colored ribbon, graded antialiased edge alpha, transparent background and center samples, and mean alpha coverage within one percentage point of the canonical source. The 256px ICO entry must match the native PNG exactly. Inspect the final PNG composited over light, dark, and checkerboard backgrounds. These checks must reject a mostly transparent ribbon even when its background and central cutout remain transparent; validating an earlier intermediate image is insufficient.

### Saved server windows

The main window's Saved servers dialog uses the [Go saved-connection boundary](cmds-delidev-connections-contract.md). Listing never contacts every server. A masked private pairing document shows its non-secret endpoint/server identity before explicit submission; its original profile ID/name/grant remain immutable through uncertainty and dialog visibility, then clear after confirmed pairing. Existing pending profiles retry only their retained Go intent. An old inventory read cannot erase newer mutation feedback. The native controller sends at most 32 KiB of pairing input through a joined stdin writer, never argv, and preserves the existing 40-second timeout and 128-KiB output bound, covering 32 maximally escaped profile labels. The dialog has no token reveal or arbitrary file/command operation.

Each paired profile opens one independent `server-<profile UUID>` window, initially maximized with native window decorations. The main window also starts maximized with native decorations. Users can restore and resize either window; showing an existing hidden or minimized window preserves its current geometry and maximization state. The native map pins profile/endpoint/server/device plus a fresh window instance; opening it again focuses the same window. With the tray installed, title-bar close hides this window and retains its drafts, connection and caches. Without an installed tray, ordinary close destroys the window and reopening creates a new client view without changing the pairing or server lifecycle. A stale completion after window destruction cannot deliver credentials to a replacement instance. Both native and renderer checks require the original identity before creating the direct Connect transport. Explicit destruction/removal or full app exit disposes the affected window's memory state; other server drafts/caches are never transferred.

Display-name editing captures the original profile revision and request identity, keeps stale drafts visible and retains exact uncertain retries through dialog visibility and refreshed inventory. An accepted rename changes only that profile's label. Existing native window bindings compare every authority field separately from the display name/revision, preserve their original instance, and update title and metadata monotonically. An identity-free native event asks only the receiving saved window to re-read its pinned context. The React subtree, transport, connection cache and open forms remain mounted; a stale notification cannot roll the name backward. Reopening an existing window refreshes CLI-edited labels. Saved windows receive only event listen/unlisten permission, never event emission or profile-management authority.

Only bundled app documents can receive saved credentials. Tauri's app-resource response callback replaces only `connect-src` with native IPC and the one canonical saved server origin while retaining script/style/other restrictions. It never grants wildcard HTTPS or the main window's unrelated local RPC origin. Saved windows deny external navigation/popups, use ephemeral storage and expose only `connection_context`, their argument-free `connect_saved`, profile-owned `saved_worker_proof`/`saved_worker_control` and native presentation of the main window. They cannot invoke local-server bootstrap, the main window's Worker controls, profile management or arbitrary credential-path reads. The main alone manages profiles. External development-server documents cannot open a saved credential window; use the bundled native development build.

`connect_saved` delegates fresh TLS/authenticated identity/version checking to Go, then reads only that profile's Go-validated paired client file. Ordinary product RPCs, including event streams, are direct frontend Connect requests under this window's exact CSP. Remote selection never invokes remote supervision/start/update or falls back to another profile/owner token. Status refresh failure displays disconnected state even when an earlier version response remains cached. A saved window uses only its own profile's Worker on this computer, never the main window's Worker proof. SSH setup and the complete real remote/platform matrix remain required separate integrations.

Connection removal explicitly confirms closing the selected server window and losing its unsent drafts, while retaining server sessions, independent Workers and work files. Capture the original profile revision; retain the exact request through uncertain delivery and dialog hiding. A stale fresh confirmation cannot submit. Cleanup-pending inventory exposes only its original removal retry, never open/re-pair/rename. The native main window checks current metadata before closing, blocks late credential/proof delivery and concurrent reopening, destroys only this window, and then calls the bounded Go removal command. A completed removal keeps a process-local admission barrier so a previously started open cannot recreate a window from stale metadata. The server/client device ID is never reused for a new pairing.

Completed removals have a separately paginated, read-only history in Saved servers. An explicitly selected retained Worker has its own status/start/generation-bound stop controls, with no new registration or token/Local-proof delivery. Keep pending stop identity through dialog visibility and block switching selected Worker while an operation or stop confirmation remains pending. No action on this history reconnects or restores the deleted client. Both the dialog and CLI distinguish local credential cleanup from explicit remote device revocation; copied tokens and other client processes are not claimed revoked.

Profile-owned Worker controls accept the same closed lifecycle action and original stop generation as local controls, with no renderer-selected profile ID. Go's `connection worker-*` commands validate the pinned client and retain grant/pairing requests before network effects. Native reads validate the same profile before and after private Worker proof retrieval; the command handler also rechecks the original window instance before returning. A saved window can therefore select Local sessions/schedules with fresh proof for this computer while its server runs elsewhere. Independent profile Workers have independent device/machine identities and process generations. Registration, current server authorization, controller status and session cleanup remain separate facts; no mutation is automatically repeated by status polling or window reopening.

### Destination windows

An internal destination control opens its target in one additional product window when the user primary-clicks it with the platform primary modifier. The window is created on the invoking window's original Local or Saved connection, shows the typed destination through its own authenticated route restoration, and grants no authority beyond a window created from the File menu. External URLs, protected browser pages, OAuth, File > New Window and every shortcut mapping keep their behavior. Web previews and mobile never attempt the native operation.

#### Click classification

`navigation-disposition.ts` owns the closed `NavigationDisposition` enum (`CurrentWindow`, `NewWindow`) and one pure classifier. A click selects `NewWindow` only when every condition holds: the primary mouse button, a pointer activation (`detail` above zero, so keyboard and assistive activation never qualify), exactly the platform primary modifier, no Alt. Shift is allowed. The platform comes from the shared shortcut platform probe (`ShortcutPlatform.Mac` when `navigator.platform` matches `mac`).

| Modifiers held (pointer click, primary button) | macOS         | Windows/Linux |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| none                                           | CurrentWindow | CurrentWindow |
| Shift                                          | CurrentWindow | CurrentWindow |
| Command (Meta)                                 | NewWindow     | CurrentWindow |
| Command + Shift                                | NewWindow     | CurrentWindow |
| Control                                        | CurrentWindow | NewWindow     |
| Control + Shift                                | CurrentWindow | NewWindow     |
| Control + Meta (with or without Shift)         | CurrentWindow | CurrentWindow |
| any primary modifier + Alt                     | CurrentWindow | CurrentWindow |
| Alt only                                       | CurrentWindow | CurrentWindow |

| Activation                                                       | Disposition                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Middle or right button, any modifiers                            | CurrentWindow                    |
| Keyboard or assistive activation (`detail` 0)                    | CurrentWindow                    |
| Primary modifier click while the host is a web preview or mobile | CurrentWindow, no native attempt |

A handled `NewWindow` click calls `preventDefault` and `stopPropagation` so no duplicate DOM, default or ancestor navigation runs, and it never runs the control's current-window handler.

#### Eligible controls

Only controls whose single purpose is to show a typed destination use the shared dispatcher (`useDestinationDispatch`); each passes a `ProductRoute` and its existing handler.

| Control                                                                     | Typed destination                        | Disposition source |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| Sidebar rail Sessions, Pull requests, Schedules, pinned Usage, More > Usage | screen                                   | click              |
| Sidebar header Inbox and Search                                             | screen                                   | click              |
| Sidebar Session and Sidechat rows                                           | Session, or parent Session plus Sidechat | click              |
| Search result (Sidechat results resolve their original parent first)        | Session, or parent Session plus Sidechat | click              |
| Inbox entry row, Inbox Open session                                         | Inbox entry, Session                     | click              |
| Schedule row                                                                | Schedule                                 | click              |
| Pull requests repository row                                                | repository                               | click              |
| Settings category list                                                      | category                                 | click              |
| Usage tab                                                                   | tab                                      | click              |
| Fork dialog Open forked session                                             | Session, or parent Session plus Sidechat | click              |

Excluded, never receiving the new-window disposition: New session, New general chat and New project, creation and mutation controls, disclosures, filters, sorting, pagination, menus and their triggers, the command palette, Session workspace tab selection, Settings search field targets, retry/refresh/dismiss controls and Pin Usage.

#### Renderer operation states

The Shell owns one controller (`useDestinationWindowController`). Descendants read it through `DestinationWindowProvider`; outside a Shell the inert default makes every control keep its current-window behavior.

| State       | Entered by                              | New-window click                                                      | Exits to                             |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Idle        | start, completed or failed operation    | admits one operation, clears a shown failure                          | Pending                              |
| Pending     | an admitted operation                   | suppressed (default and bubbling), dropped, not queued, no navigation | Idle on success, Failed on rejection |
| Failed      | native rejection or unknown error       | admits a new operation (the notice is cleared)                        | Pending, or Idle on dismiss          |
| Unavailable | host is not Tauri (web preview, mobile) | not claimed: the control's handler runs                               | n/a                                  |

Failure shows one localized `role="alert"` notice with a dismiss button through the existing notice treatment. It never navigates the current window, retries automatically, changes the selection, scroll, draft or drawer, or creates a resource. The notice is presented by exactly one surface, the nearest registered surface that encloses the control that was clicked. A modal dialog makes the rest of the document inert, so a notice rendered only in the page would be neither readable nor dismissible for a control inside a dialog.

| Caller context                                                                                 | Presenting surface                 | Lifetime of the notice                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Page content: Search results, Inbox, Schedules, Pull requests, Settings categories, Usage tabs | Shell main content                 | Until dismissed or the next operation starts                       |
| Wide sidebar pane and rail (not modal)                                                         | Shell main content                 | As the page                                                        |
| Compact sidebar drawer (modal dialog): Inbox, Search and Session rows                          | The drawer, at the top of its pane | As the page; closing the drawer moves a visible notice to the page |
| Open More list (popover): Usage                                                                | The list, below its rows           | As the page; closing the list moves a visible notice to the page   |
| Modal dialog: Fork dialog Open forked session                                                  | The dialog, below its heading      | As the page; closing the dialog moves a visible notice to the page |
| Nested modal dialogs                                                                           | The innermost enclosing dialog     | As the modal dialog                                                |
| Any surface that closed before the operation failed                                            | Shell main content                 | As the page                                                        |

Surfaces register through one shared hook; the shared Modal registers every modal dialog it presents. A control outside every registered surface uses the page. A new caller context needs a row in this table and a presentation test before it ships. A Search result opening shares the existing pending/unavailable Search status: the original parent is resolved first, an unreadable result shows the existing alert, and no window opens.

Destination window code paths log only phases, closed failure codes and closed reasons. They never log a route, an opaque Session, Sidechat or item ID, a title or connection data, including when the log site is shared with a current-window path.

| Log site                                                                           | Event                                      | Fields                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Controller admission (`requested`, `dropped`) and settlement (`settled`)           | `delidev.destination_window`               | `phase`                                        |
| Controller rejection (`failed`)                                                    | `delidev.destination_window`               | `phase`, closed failure code                   |
| Search result resolution for a new window (metadata read failed or malformed)      | `delidev.search.session_route_unavailable` | closed reason only (anonymous resolution mode) |
| Search result resolution for the current window (retained for its own diagnostics) | `delidev.search.session_route_unavailable` | closed reason and opaque Session ID            |
| Native command (`requested`, `authorized`, `created`, `failed`)                    | `destination_window` operation             | `operation`, `phase`, closed failure code      |

The Search resolution takes its logging mode from the caller: the destination window path always requests the anonymous mode, so a never-visited result whose metadata cannot be read or is malformed leaves no identifier in the renderer log. A repository scan test keeps the destination window sources limited to the fields above.

#### Native operation

`open_destination_window` (`window_host.rs`) takes only a `DestinationRoute` (`destination_route.rs`): a closed screen enum (Sessions, Pull requests, Usage, Schedules, Inbox, Search, Settings), optional canonical UUIDv7 `session`, `sidechat`, `item` and closed `category` / `tab` enums. Unknown fields, unknown enum values, creation screens, URLs and slots that the screen does not own are rejected as invalid input before any window work. The serialized initial route query is the only destination carrier; the new window is created with `WebviewUrl::App("index.html?...")` and does not use `window.open`, relax the popup policy or transfer state.

| Caller                                                                | Result                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Registered Local `main` / `local-*` document                          | admitted; creates a Local window                    |
| Registered Saved `server-*` document with an unchanged paired profile | admitted; creates a window for the same profile     |
| Saved profile revoked, replaced or removal-pending                    | `permission-denied` / `invalid-evidence`; no window |
| Source window closed, replaced or no longer registered                | `permission-denied` / `invalid-evidence`; no window |
| Tray panel, widget, browser, external or other auxiliary webview      | denied by the ACL; no command access                |
| Remote origin                                                         | denied by the ACL                                   |
| Most recently focused window                                          | never consulted; the IPC window is the caller       |

The ACL grants `destination-window` to the `main` / `local-*` and `server-*` capabilities only; `build.rs`, `permissions/destination-window.toml` and `permission_tests.rs` stay synchronized.

| Phase / fence    | Rule                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Requested        | validate the route; refuse when native shutdown has begun (`stopped`) or shortcut capture fences windows (`busy`)                                                  |
| Source admission | capture the invoking window's authority off the UI loop; one pending operation per source window instance (`busy`)                                                 |
| Authorized       | Saved callers re-inspect the profile and compare every authority field; recheck the source window after asynchronous work                                          |
| Creation         | the task joins the shutdown fence; the main-thread step rechecks the registered source, then reuses the existing admission, label, cleanup and cancellation guards |
| Created          | the window is registered ready and focused; cleanup on any late failure destroys the partial window                                                                |
| Failed           | the renderer receives the closed failure code; no fallback window, retry or partial window                                                                         |

Native logs (`destination_window`) record only the phase and a failure code, never routes, IDs, titles, URLs or connection data. No RPC, storage, schema or capability number is added.

#### Destination window initial route

The new renderer reads its route from the query before its first route read (`readInitialRoute`), so the destination is present at the first render. It restores selection through its own authenticated reads: stale, deleted or inaccessible targets show the existing route-restoration unavailable behavior, loading and error states apply unchanged, and nothing is created. The window starts with a fresh renderer: no drafts, query cache, unsaved configuration or other windows' state transfer.

### Native tray and menu bar

The native File menu item New Window has no keyboard accelerator: it is activated by menu click only, and Command/Control+N is the renderer New session shortcut that opens the New session page in the current window. Command/Control+T no longer opens a product window. Each menu click is handled by one app-level handler, creating one window per activation through the existing Local/Saved window admission. Close Window has no native accelerator; `CmdOrCtrl+W` is the fixed renderer SessionCloseTab shortcut closing only the selected closeable session workspace tab (Conversation stays pinned and the chord never closes or hides a window; W stays reserved against customization; external page-focused forwarding is unchanged; Keyboard Help dismisses before closure; terminal focus is eligible), and the existing menu order is preserved.

One native tray owns one quota-first auxiliary status panel and projects the original ready Local/Saved product windows. TypeScript reads `SystemService.GetOverview`, today's existing usage summary and bounded account pages directly through Connect Query. Overview and today's usage summary poll every 15 seconds, and account reads every 30 seconds while the app process runs, including hidden windows. A failed or missing usage read remains unavailable on publication instead of carrying an old total forward. Rust receives only a validated presentation projection, never RPC authority, account credentials, prompts, native tool identities or paths.

Show server observation time, exact active-session and unanswered-request counts, connected/registered Workers, known UTC-day tokens with incomplete telemetry, and separate account quota windows. Preserve zero and decimal precision; failed or missing evidence is unavailable. Today's half-open UTC range comes from the server. A quota cannot become pooled remaining capacity: preserve its own state, observation/reset times and stale result. At most 20 account aliases and eight windows per account are shown, with explicit Settings links for additional records. Email-shaped aliases are masked before native IPC and again before native menu rendering. The product window renders no status text for a tray publication, activation-listener or retained-action read failure; the publisher, the `tray-activate` listener and ticket acknowledgment keep their behavior.

Each publication uses the calling window's fresh scope and a strictly increasing revision. Stale scopes, another window's scope and reordered revisions cannot overwrite the current presentation. A native monotonic timer marks unrefreshed data stale after 45 seconds even if renderer timers are suspended. Cached read failures are also visibly stale. Native menus use only closed Sessions, Inbox, Usage and Settings destinations; opening them does not enqueue input, resolve/read a request or grant execution authority. Activation rechecks the original saved-window instance, retains a ticket in memory until the receiving view acknowledges that exact ticket and rejects an older acknowledgment that would erase newer navigation. This preserves activation across delayed mounts and React Strict Mode cleanup.

With a successfully installed tray, title-bar close hides the existing window without discarding unsent drafts. Show and navigation restore that same window while preserving its current geometry and maximization state. On macOS, the OS application-reopen event also unminimizes, shows and focuses the existing main window without recreating its renderer, resetting user-selected geometry or dispatching session work. Explicit Quit joins native presentation/supervision tasks and app-owned sidecars before terminating the desktop client; independently started servers and Workers remain running. A tray installation failure retains ordinary window-close behavior. Native initialization/build evidence is separate from actual menu activation and platform acceptance; Native notification delivery is defined below; the [macOS status widget](apps-delidev-widget-contract.md) reuses this projection in protected metadata snapshots, while signed updates remain a separate integration.

#### Auxiliary tray status panel

The exact `tray-status` bundled CEF document is process-owned presentation, not a
product window. Keep it outside Local/Saved admission, numbering, product
bootstrap, credentials, filesystem operations and preference writes. Its separate
entry mounts no Desktop, Connect transport, product queries or device preference
controllers. Native admission requires the exact bundled origin/path and original
instance query; external navigation and popups are denied. Only bounded retained
snapshot reads, one instance-scoped IPC change channel (without generic event
listen/emit permissions), closed activation and hide
operations are permitted. Project committed language, theme and date-format state
from their in-memory owners without inspecting preference files.

The 380px border-box panel has a maximum 640px height, 16px padding, 12px corners,
semantic themes, 40px action/disclosure targets and internal scrolling with a
fixed, reachable header/footer. Render no product-window label, selector or
selector-only overflow guidance. Show, in order: the DeliDev header with Close; a
compact connection/observation line; the Account quotas heading with Manage
subscriptions (the heading and action wrap at narrow widths and in Korean);
account cards; secondary 2x2 metrics; the incomplete-usage note; the initially
collapsed Usage details disclosure; and the fixed Open/Quit footer. Exactly one
ready-window snapshot is both the presentation source and the navigation target.
Each panel opening selects the native recent ready window, falling back to the
first ready row when that instance is absent. The choice is retained for the
visible visit, including preference updates and disclosure interaction, and is
replaced only when that window disappears. Snapshots are never merged, so
multiple windows connected to the same server cannot create duplicate account
cards or summed session, Worker or usage counts. This is representative snapshot
selection, not server aggregation or routing. Snapshots include at most 32
product windows and retain the recent window within that bound. Settings remains
the existing destination. Preserve the 20-account/eight-quota-window bounds and
explicit additional-record guidance. Render optional closed `chatgpt | claude |
grok` service only from explicit subscription-account metadata. Preserve complete
masked aliases and safe exact 128-character ASCII quota IDs; missing, invalid or
credential-shaped IDs use localized Quota N. Account cards are softly tinted with 12px
padding and 8px corners, show service metadata and the masked alias in the header,
and stack multiple quota rows with fine separators. Each independent quota shows
its safe ID, a 24px remaining percentage with basis-point precision, original
observation/reset evidence, state and a decorative bar; unknown, failed and
unsupported quotas show the unavailable text and no bar. Never pool quotas or
infer duration labels. Expired reset times await new
observation, and stale historical values remain visibly stale. Loading, accounts-unavailable, accounts-empty and recoverable read-error states
remain distinct muted inline messages with the existing Reload action. Secondary
metrics use 14px text with subtle borders and keep exact counts, UTC-day labeling
and unknown-versus-zero distinctions. Usage stays exact,
incomplete and separated by currency in an initially collapsed disclosure. Reuse the shared native disclosure family with its original 40px header. Opening or closing it preserves the mounted retained snapshot and grants no product read or activation authority.

On macOS/Windows, left-click toggles the panel adjacent to the native tray
rectangle; Linux keeps its native Open status menu and centers the same panel on
the pointer monitor, falling back to the primary monitor. Convert desired CSS
size with the monitor scale and clamp physical placement to its work area,
including negative origins and small monitors. Keep one hidden, undecorated,
nonresizable, taskbar-excluded native window and reuse it. Close, Escape and focus
loss hide only this panel. The first successful snapshot read of each opening
(initial load and the window focus event that follows a native show) focuses the
Close button; later snapshot updates never move focus. No selector exists to
autofocus. Keyboard Tab traversal, visible focus and native CEF
accessibility remain supported. A bounded focus-loss/mouse-up correlation
workaround prevents an icon click from reopening the panel it just dismissed.

Preserve native Open status, Show and Quit fallback actions. Construction/show
failure restores the full existing status menu with sanitized diagnostics. Panel
snapshot reads, representative-window selection, repainting and preference projection perform no RPC,
quota refresh, scope reset or product mutation. The existing polling, native
45-second monotonic staleness and widget writer remain authoritative. Activation
retains original window instance, scope and exact publication revision, rejects
replacement/stale targets, hides the panel and uses the existing acknowledged
navigation ticket. Open restores only the original window without changing its
route or geometry. Never hold tray locks across native UI/URL authorization or
storage. Quit fences auxiliary admission immediately and retires its window on
the existing joined cleanup worker before native exit; preserve the original
35-second sidecar grace and independent runtime lifetimes. Log only closed
operation/phase/action classifications, never aliases, quotas, IDs or endpoints.
Record automated fixtures/builds separately from owner-assigned installed
macOS/Windows/Ubuntu X11, focus, accessibility and Quit acceptance.

### Native inbox notifications

The React controller polls metadata-only `InboxService.ListNotificationCandidates` every 10 seconds while the process runs, including hidden windows. Server-side client preferences default to questions/approvals enabled and terminal notices disabled. The settings draft captures its original revision, remains mounted through visibility changes and exposes only the same retained request after uncertain saving. Preferences remain specific to the authenticated client and server; OS permission belongs to the app on the computer.

Before any native display, claim that exact candidate through direct Connect. Validate the fresh `may_present` grant, original request/claim identity, closed kind and exact inbox/session source. Never present from receipt replay, an uncertain claim acknowledgment or an unverified response. One serial batch and one latest replacement bound pending work; pages are capped at 50 (20 requested), and claim/report calls have ten-second deadlines and connection-owned cancellation. Report submitted/denied/failed/uncertain once. A report failure never retries display; the durable original claim preserves uncertainty and prevents reconnect/restart duplication. No presentation result changes inbox reading or source responses.

Rust receives only canonical claim/inbox UUIDs and a closed notification kind under its calling window's fresh presentation scope. Titles and body are fixed native strings; prompts, answers, paths, names, tokens and URLs never enter native notification payloads. The host never queries product RPCs. It validates the trusted original window and saved-window instance, reserves a claim before OS work, and keeps the claim seen for the whole process even after closing its notification. Scope replacement, exact scope disposal, window destruction and app exit cancel owned callbacks. A stale disposal cannot close a replacement scope. Native navigation tickets also retain their notification scope and cannot activate after that scope ends. Activation opens only the exact inbox ID through the original connection, freshly joins its current server state and cannot mark read, answer, approve, resume or switch the active session/composer. Missing/mixed sources are unavailable; paused, archived, recovering, replaced and failed-refresh requests cannot expose active response controls.

Permission reads have a five-second deadline and never prompt. Only the explicit settings button requests OS permission; one process-wide prompt admission remains occupied if its 120-second response becomes uncertain. Native presentation has a ten-second deadline, retains at most 256 active handles and expires each after 24 hours. Full exit cancels and joins owned notification and prompt tasks; cleanup has bounded waits and typed uncertainty logging. A process-lifetime 10,000-claim ceiling also bounds uncertain callback retention in the pinned macOS wrapper; capacity is an explicit unavailable state and never evicts a claim into a repeat display. Inbox remains usable. Remove this conservative callback bound only after all platform adapters prove owned cancellation, including the wrapper's response-delegate retention.

- macOS uses `mac-usernotifications` 0.3.1 and the native UserNotifications framework. It requires a real DeliDev app bundle, reads authorization plus alert/Notification Center settings and provides a fixed Open action. Unbundled execution reports bundle-required. Permission does not guarantee a visible banner under Focus or system suppression.
- Windows uses pinned `windows` 0.62.2 WinRT notifications under `io.delino.delidev`; it never borrows PowerShell or another application's identity. Retain activation/dismissal registrations, distinguish application/user/policy/manifest disablement, keep Action Center activation after banner timeout and unregister callbacks during cleanup. Installed AppUserModelID registration and actual supported-system delivery require packaging acceptance.
- Linux uses pinned `zbus` 5.19.0 with the Freedesktop notification service. Require actions, subscribe before Notify, bind signals and CloseNotification to the original unique bus owner and numeric ID, and use the pinned bundler's `DeliDev.desktop` basename. A replacement daemon cannot activate or close another notification with a reused ID. The interface has no standard user-permission query: display service-available without claiming permission or actual banner visibility.

Native status uses a connection-scoped React Query cache and 30-second reads. The product window renders no status text for a readiness, candidate or presentation-pump failure; requests remain in the inbox and the Settings notification status keeps the truthful native availability. Disabled/unavailable permission does not claim candidates. Settings explicitly distinguishes unrequested permission, denial, bundle/action/service/capacity failures and Linux service availability.
