API submission, platform permission and actual displayed/seen notifications are separate evidence. No browser notification API, network broker, arbitrary native payload or OS-permission request from a timer is allowed. Component tests, cross compilation and native host initialization do not establish real notification acceptance on any platform.

#### Sidebar, tray and notification failure diagnostics

The product window renders nothing for a sidebar-preference, tray or
desktop-notification failure, so the renderer records each failing phase as one
structured console warning. The record has the stable event name
`delidev.presentation.outcome` and exactly two fields: a closed phase and the
outcome `failed` or `recovered`. It never contains raw error text, identifiers,
paths, summaries, payloads or the sidebar problem classification. Every
reporter (sidebar provider, tray presentation, notification presentation and
the tray publisher and notification pump it owns) feeds one pure reducer in
`presentation-diagnostics.ts`; no reporter keeps its own failing flags.

A phase is one operation. Its failure records once on the healthy-to-failing
transition, so a repeating failure and bounded retries add no further warning;
its next success records one `recovered` info record. An operation that was not
attempted changes nothing. Phases never affect each other: a success of one
phase never recovers another phase, and two phases that fail in the same batch
each record their own warning.

One log belongs to one lifetime: the sidebar provider, one mounted tray
presentation or one notification connection. Disposal ends the log and a
disposed log ignores every later event. A replaced connection or a newly
mounted tray starts a new log with every phase healthy, so it reports its own
first failure.

Reducer table (`P` is one phase, `Q` any other phase):

| State of `P`  | Failure of `P`               | Success of `P`                      | Disposal of the log                  |
| ------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| healthy       | warn; `P` is failing         | no record                           | the log is disposed                  |
| failing       | no record; `P` stays failing | one `recovered` record; `P` healthy | the log is disposed; failing cleared |
| any, `Q` fail | independent of `Q`           | independent of `Q`                  | not applicable                       |
| disposed log  | no record                    | no record                           | no record                            |

| Phase                            | Failure event                                                                                                           | Result                                                                                                                          | Recovery event                                       |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `sidebar-read`                   | a snapshot with problem Unavailable, ReadFailed, InvalidDocument or UnsupportedVersion, including the first native read | warn; saves stay fenced until Reload                                                                                            | a healthy snapshot                                   |
| `sidebar-save`                   | a snapshot with problem WriteFailed, OutcomeUnknown or Changed                                                          | warn; saves stay fenced and the original save is never replayed                                                                 | a healthy snapshot                                   |
| `tray-begin`                     | `begin_tray` rejects                                                                                                    | warn; the next summary refresh begins again                                                                                     | `begin_tray` resolves                                |
| `tray-publish`                   | `publish_tray` rejects                                                                                                  | warn; the scope is dropped and the next refresh begins again                                                                    | a completed publication                              |
| `tray-action-read`               | `read_tray_action` or `acknowledge_tray_action` rejects or is invalid                                                   | warn once; bounded retry continues unchanged                                                                                    | a completed read or acknowledgment                   |
| `tray-activation-listener`       | the `tray-activate` listener cannot be registered                                                                       | warn; the tray still publishes and no activation is received                                                                    | none until the tray is mounted again                 |
| `notification-readiness`         | the permission read rejects                                                                                             | warn; no candidate is read and Settings keeps native availability                                                               | a later successful read                              |
| `notification-candidate-read`    | the candidate list read rejects                                                                                         | warn; the pump keeps its previous page and presents nothing new                                                                 | a later successful read                              |
| `notification-scope-begin`       | `begin_notifications` rejects or returns an invalid scope                                                               | warn; nothing is claimed and the next page begins again after a rejection                                                       | a valid scope                                        |
| `notification-candidate-invalid` | the page exceeds 50 entries or carries an invalid target                                                                | warn; the page is dropped before native initialization                                                                          | the next valid page                                  |
| `notification-present`           | native display is denied, failed or uncertain                                                                           | warn when the display result is known, before its report is sent; the batch stops after the report and display is never retried | a submitted display                                  |
| `notification-pump`              | claim verification or the claim request fails                                                                           | warn; pending work is dropped and a submitted notice is not repeated                                                            | a verified claim, including one that may not present |
| `notification-report`            | the report request rejects                                                                                              | warn; pending work is dropped and display is never retried                                                                      | a completed report                                   |

Notification pump cells. A page is one batch; each row lists the records the
batch produces in order, and every phase not named keeps its state. A claim that
is aborted or not found is neither a failure nor a success of `notification-pump`.

| Batch outcome                                         | Records                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| valid page, display submitted, report completes       | recovers each of `notification-scope-begin`, `-pump`, `-present`, `-report` that was failing, and `notification-candidate-invalid` at page validation |
| page invalid                                          | fails `notification-candidate-invalid`; no native call                                                                                                |
| `begin_notifications` rejects                         | fails `notification-scope-begin`; nothing is claimed                                                                                                  |
| scope invalid                                         | fails `notification-scope-begin`; nothing is claimed                                                                                                  |
| claim rejects or cannot be verified                   | fails `notification-pump`; no display; scope-begin recovered earlier in the same drain                                                                |
| display denied, failed or uncertain, report completes | fails `notification-present`; recovers every other failing pump phase                                                                                 |
| display submitted, report rejects                     | fails `notification-report` only                                                                                                                      |
| display denied, failed or uncertain, report rejects   | fails `notification-present`, then `notification-report`, in that order                                                                               |
| display or report settles after the pump closed       | no record; the report request is not sent after a closed display                                                                                      |
| connection replaced                                   | the new pump and its new log report their own first failure                                                                                           |

The sidebar provider does not record its loading placeholder: the initial
Unavailable value is not an observation. The first native read, even when it is
a real Unavailable snapshot, is recorded like any other snapshot. A problem in
the same phase as a failing one adds no record, a problem in the other phase
adds its own record, and a healthy snapshot recovers both sidebar phases.

Every phase leaves the product UI empty. The tray publisher and the
notification pump report only the phase and whether its operation failed; the
presentation component owns the log and decides what is recorded. A closed
tray publisher or notification pump reports nothing, so an operation that
settles after unmount, Strict Mode cleanup or connection replacement (for
example a pending `begin_notifications` that later rejects) adds no record to
the new lifetime.

#### Notifications settings presentation

`notification-settings.tsx` and `notification-settings.css` own the Notifications
body inside the feature's ordinary Settings page. The feature supersedes its
category-specific geometry and copy with the shared left-aligned 1040px column,
32px/24px/compact host padding, 26px/32px title, 16px/24px section headings,
14px/20px body, 12px/18px scope, 16px rows and 24px section gaps. Preserve one
host inset, complete wrapping content, 40px controls/8px corners, contrasting
focus and static semantic-theme CSS. Section actions still stack at an available
body width of 600px or less. Decorative outline SVGs are inaccessible; the
approved bitmap remains reference material. Rail/context-pane, compact drawer,
sibling categories and visit ownership stay with the shared host.

The feature distinguishes the saved summary from its editor. Render the saved
preferences as a heading-associated semantic section, retaining its search
targets, refs and focus ownership. Native status, saved rows and Inbox guidance
share the 1040px column and action trailing edge. The actual task-dialog editor
remains a form capped at 720px. The category header owns its single bottom
divider; the native section owns the next divider. Do not add shared top borders
or top-padding bands to either section. Keep 24px section gaps, 16px row padding
and actions stacked at an available Notifications width of 600px or less.

Read mode renders server-confirmed noninteractive Enabled/Disabled text, never disabled
checkboxes or guessed defaults. Explicit Edit captures the complete original
preference object and revision, then exposes two native labeled checkboxes with
separate `aria-describedby` descriptions. Preserve the existing active 5-second
poll, category-scoped mutation registry, fetch/error gates, stale alert and retained
draft, successful invalidation and exact request-ID/wire-byte uncertainty retry.
Busy/uncertain operations lock edit controls and Cancel. A peer revision change
retains the draft and blocks a new save; Cancel returns to current data. Initial
loading/failure contains no fabricated values and retains “Notification preferences
are unavailable until this server can be read.” Cached refresh failures retain
values, visibly disclose that they may be out of date and block new edit/save.
Saving, typed failures, revision conflicts and the existing “Retry the same
notification preferences” action remain distinct.

Edit focuses the first checkbox after commit. Cancel and acknowledged Save may
return focus to enabled Edit only while the workflow owned focus before its
controls were removed. Keep a one-shot intent through refetch; document/body
fallback from removal or disablement is not a deliberate transfer. Discard it on

category drawer or visible child dialog. A dialog appearing while refetch waits
consumes the intent permanently. Late callbacks read current visibility rather
than their original submission closure. Polling, disclosure changes, stale alerts
and reconnect never create an intent. Mounted state survives reflow and same-identity reconnect within the active
Settings category; category departure or leaving Settings
discards it under without changing accepted server/native effects or sibling
workflows. Page Escape and active Settings rail reselection preserve that visit.

After the rows, a quiet neutral Inbox strip always says “Inbox requests stay
available even when notifications are off.” and “Opening a notification never
marks an item read, answers a request, approves work or resumes a session.” the feature keeps this Inbox strip as the final content block with ordinary page padding. Remove the About notification delivery disclosure, its explanatory paragraphs, container and Settings search destination in both languages, without replacement content or a spacer. Delivery semantics remain defined by the Inbox and native contracts.

Native permission stays independent from readable preferences. Preserve explicit
request/Refresh admission, deadlines, 30-second reads and visit-scoped late-result
checks. Only NotDetermined offers Allow desktop notifications; pending request or
read disables its controls. Granted shows “Notifications allowed” and
“Focus or Do Not Disturb may still suppress banners.” Permission scope remains
“Permission is shared by DeliDev windows on this computer.” A read/request error

be confirmed.” Retain exact checking, unrequested, denied, Linux service-available,
bundle-required, actions-unavailable, capacity, other unavailable and non-desktop

Linux availability is not user-permission evidence. OS denial never gates otherwise
readable preference editing. No protocol, schema, native engine, migration,
dependency, telemetry, Inbox state or execution authority changes are permitted.

Record component/browser validation, packaging and actual native-window/platform
acceptance separately in PRs/issues/CI. Browser fixtures cannot prove native
geometry/keyboard behavior or real macOS/Windows/Linux notification delivery.

### Inbox workspace

Inbox is one persistent list/detail workspace for retained requests and terminal results. The list starts with no selection and fetches server-filtered pages of 20 using the generated source and read-state enums. Changing either filter resets pagination; expired cursors return to the first page. Rows show the retained Inbox record time and current read state. Selecting a row performs a fresh exact `GetInboxEntry`; opening from a native notification uses the same path and preserves the item's read state. Reading and notification activation never mark an entry read. Read-state changes are explicit revision-bound mutations.

The selected detail refreshes while Inbox is active and the window is visible, and revalidates on focus/visibility return. This selected-item read is separate from the existing metadata-only notification candidate poll, which remains on its ten-second process-wide schedule. A detail item outside the current list page remains viewable after its exact source is joined again. Missing, mixed, stale or unauthorized source state is unavailable or read-only; it cannot enable a response. Session pause/archive/recovery and active-execution ownership checks remain required in addition to the Inbox read.

Question/approval forms share their typed controls with the session view, but Inbox drafts remain React-memory-only and scoped to the effective connection identity. Each draft retains the original interaction ID, interaction revision and request identity. Preserve a draft after source/request changes for inspection and block applying it to a new request. Bound the serialized collection to 4 MiB and 1,000 nonempty requests per connection; a limit error keeps the previous draft intact. An uncertain submission retains its exact mutation identity and may be retried only after a fresh current-source read. The persistent Inbox controller preserves drafts while the user visits other app surfaces. This UI work does not establish native notification delivery on a supported operating system.

Files preview Back also restores the original compact panel and enclosing Session
scroll owners with preventScroll focus, alongside the inner tree position. These
memory-only snapshots belong to the original controller/repository and only
connected original ancestors containing the returned tree may receive them.

### Session terminals

There is no standalone Terminals management tab. The Terminals tool entry is an
explicit reuse-or-create intent that keeps the current pane selected until the
atomic admission returns a verified original terminal, then opens or selects that
terminal's direct tab. Each explicit creation or retained-resource selection
opens/selects the tab keyed by the original terminal ID. + and primary+T
additional creation applies the same rule only while no newer navigation
happened after sending, so a pending acknowledgment never overwrites a later
Conversation, Files or terminal choice. The toolbar reuse-or-create admission
always selects its admitted terminal.

Each direct terminal tab is labelled `Terminal N` / `터미널 N`. `N` is a monotonic
presentation number owned by the connection-memory terminal presentation record of
its Session. It is allocated once per original terminal ID in first
opened-or-authenticated-inventory encounter order (the explicit reuse-or-create
inventory numbers every validated row, page by page, before any admission
result opens, and invalid or aborted reads number nothing), is shared by the tab, its
tooltip, accessible names, the Close tab name and the inventory rows, and is never
reused. It survives close/reopen, paging, reorder, payload eviction, navigation and
same-identity reconnect; Sessions number independently, and a replaced connection
or app restart resets it. Labels never expose original or shortened UUIDs. The
number is presentation only: RPCs, receipts, tab/cache keys, selection and cleanup
proofs keep the original ID.

A General Chat terminal's native shell prompt shows the label `chat` instead of its
directory segment while the shell is at the session's original General Chat
directory, and its ordinary directory display elsewhere. This is Worker-side,
process-local shell integration: the desktop renders the unchanged native
output bytes, never rewrites prompts, and adds no RPC, preference or schema.
Repository Worktree and Local terminals, unknown shells, `cmd.exe` and prompts
whose directory segment cannot be identified keep their native prompt. See the
[terminal contract](cmds-delidev-terminals-contract.md).

Opening status, capability/read failures and uncertain-creation recovery render in
a non-modal strip directly below the tab row while the current pane stays mounted;
no placeholder tab is created. Read Retry is read-only and never creates a
terminal; from a non-terminal pane it enables exactly one bounded inventory
attempt that ends when it settles (success or failure), when a terminal pane is
selected, or on Session departure, so no interval-driven reads continue behind
Conversation or Files, and a failed attempt keeps the Problem with a Retry
button for the next bounded attempt. Repeated opening gestures coalesce into one admission using the captured
session, revision and request ID. Session departure or a later explicit pane
selection cancels an unsent intent; accepted or uncertain ownership survives.
Retained manager lifetime, explicit-open resolution (Session visible) and
selected-terminal observation/input (a terminal tab selected) are separate
activity gates, so opening from Conversation enables no background input or
unrelated observation. The active terminal occupies the complete content
region beside persistent Info; the former independent bottom dock and its
resize/Maximize/Restore presentation are superseded. Conversation authoring and
original terminal mutation controllers remain mounted. Departure disposes only
the output/input attachment, discards unsent bytes with its original notice and
never closes the Worker-owned process. Reopening an original ID beyond the
bounded inventory page uses an exact authenticated resource read before attachment.
Tab close is presentation-only. The terminal panel offers no process Close
action; Archive cleanup and verified exits own process termination.

Original authenticated inventory or stream resources dismiss a terminal only
when schema-v1 state is exactly `exited` and `cleanup_verified` is boolean true.
Connection-memory revision fences and original-ID tombstones prevent stale
history restoration or reopening from reviving dismissed tabs. Pending or
uncertain original controls retain their recovery presentation; only a missing
or null `pending` field means no operation, so an empty object, scalar or array
`pending` value stays unsettled and never dismisses. The same presence rule
gates replacement creation (an inventory row with present `pending` keeps
original cleanup unconfirmed) and terminal input or resize dispatch. Each original ID
retains one compact fingerprint (no document bytes) of its latest accepted
revision; an equal-revision observation whose state, cleanup proof or pending
evidence differs is contradictory and rejected without tombstoning (logging only a
content-free `revision-contradiction` diagnostic with the original terminal ID
and revision), while an
identical replay (including a deferred exit observed again after its control
settles) is accepted once without requiring a newer revision. Fingerprinting
walks the evidence with an explicit work list rather than recursion, so
arbitrarily deep nesting never overflows the call stack and every distinct
document, including deeply nested ones, keeps its own evidence-specific
fingerprint. A deeply nested state or cleanup proof is not exact exited and
verified evidence, and a deeply nested pending value is present, so such a
document never dismisses. An inactive exit
preserves selection/focus; a selected exit chooses its nearest remaining left
terminal, then the first remaining terminal. Shared content tabs use their
original opened-terminal order, skipping intervening nonterminal tools. If no
other terminal content tab exists, selection uses the remaining inventory
neighbor without creating a shell. The retained standalone dock uses inventory
order. One observation (inventory refresh, stream observation or both in the same
commit) tombstones every verified exit first, then derives the surviving
selection once from the batch-effective selection, so a refresh reporting exits
of selected A and B with live C selects and attaches C (never a dismissed
terminal or Conversation) and a user selection made before the deferred standalone
focus wins. Tombstoned terminal tabs are never fallback targets. The final
automatic dismissal fires only when no visible inventory row and no
non-tombstoned Terminal content tab in the Session tab store remains, so an
opened terminal absent from a replacement inventory chain, or an uncertain or
unsettled retained terminal, is never closed by it. It is also fenced while the
Session's own terminal creation is busy or uncertain (a lost CreateTerminal
response): tombstoning stays immediate, the Retry the same terminal creation
control stays reachable and sends only the original request on explicit
activation, and the deferred hide runs once after the original receipt settles; a
late receipt for a dismissed terminal never reopens it and creation in another
Session never fences it. The final automatic dismissal uses
the Session-owned presentation close and focus path, retaining mounted
conversation/composer/Info; it focuses the surviving selected tab button by key
after the tab bar commits (deferred frame, current index re-read, suppressed when
the selection changed or the target is gone), like the individual dismissal
callback. An explicitly opened empty inventory remains available
for creation. EOF, errors, missing resources and malformed/unsupported observations
never prove exit. Dismissal sends no process Close, deletion or replacement creation.

Authenticated generated operations follow the
[terminal contract](cmds-delidev-terminals-contract.md). Only advertised support
enables history reads/refresh/selection; capability errors remain distinct from
missing support. Already-loaded background history Refresh does not insert a loading
row or change the selected terminal geometry. Preserve Initial, Additional, Reload,
Restore and error/retry guidance, unchanged polling, original output ownership and
explicit user resize delivery. Opening, tab selection and reattachment cannot create shells.
The compact dark header exposes only the Terminals heading and a right-aligned +
button. There is no Details, Hide terminals, shell override, Create form, Refresh
control, Worker/shell/path/cleanup metadata or Close terminal control; + creates one
default-shell terminal (Worker account default shell, original session revision,
fresh request identity, 24×80). Retained-resource choices, compact connection
status, loading/empty/error notices, reattach and exact uncertain retries remain.
Retain the accepted creation and explicit selection beyond the bounded 50-record
history payload window.

Pin @wterm/dom and @wterm/ghostty to 0.5.4 with resolved
@wterm/core 0.5.4. The synchronous TerminalScreen facade retains its
open callbacks and serializes original Uint8Array writes through one async
initialization. Each renderer owns one Ghostty WASM instance with a 5000-line
scrollback limit, image storage disabled, debug off and accessible output.
The adapter owns input listeners; no React wrapper or engine transport takes
ownership of Connect requests, input admission, resize or native processes.

The version-pinned DOM patch exposes coordinated reset, input gating, optional
autofocus, inert links and localized accessibility labels. Reset cancels pending
render, search, selection, announcements and window queries, recreates both
native screens and parser state on the same core, and retains dimensions and
attachment focus. Disabled input suppresses keyboard, IME, paste, mouse, focus
reports and parser replies while selection and copy remain usable. The Ghostty
patch discards fragmented OSC 52 writes and queries before parsing, ends the
discard on BEL, ESC `\`, standalone C1 ST, CAN, SUB or any other ESC-introduced
sequence (which is then parsed normally; repeated ESC bytes collapse to the newest
pending ESC so no orphan ESC reaches the parser), and silences the raw WASM log import. OSC 8 remains inert, and title, working-directory and
shell-integration callbacks stay disconnected. Diagnostics contain only stable
stage/category values.

Full and incremental cell rendering constructs DOM nodes and textContent,
applying only generated, allowlisted declarations through CSSOM. Static CSS
retains the dark 14px monospace palette, selection, cursor, geometry, shared
focus and scrollbar tokens in all application themes. Preserve colored underline
and strike styling without injecting HTML style attributes or stylesheets.

The production rsbuild `output.assetPrefix` is `auto`, never `./`: with `./`,
emitted CSS in `static/css/` resolved raster harness marks (Codex, Claude Code)
to nonexistent `static/css/static/image/*`. With `auto`, CSS URLs resolve
relative to the stylesheet, so the output works at the root, under a nested base
path and at the bundled desktop origin, and JS chunks, CSS, fonts and WASM keep
loading. `scripts/asset-prefix.test.mjs` builds the real config, resolves every
file-backed CSS `url()` against its stylesheet at the root and a nested path,
compares served bytes with the `public/harness-marks` source digests and fails
under a `./` negative control. The Agent Worker layout fixture reads the
production prefix instead of overriding it. OpenCode and Grok marks stay inlined
SVG data URLs.

Bundle the exported Ghostty WASM as a hashed same-origin asset, pass its emitted
URL explicitly and serve it as application/wasm. Production adds only
script-src wasm-unsafe-eval and connect-src self to its existing restrictive
policy; style-src self remains unchanged. Saved and local connection rewrites
retain self plus the exact validated selected server origin and existing IPC
sources, never wildcard or unrelated origins. No CDN, runtime compiler,
unsafe-eval or production unsafe-inline is allowed.

Late initialization, failure and disposal fence all writes and focus work.
Renderer failure disables input and uses the existing original-terminal
reattachment/Close recovery. Dispose both WTerm and the supplied Ghostty core
on normal teardown, failure and late load. No native process operation is
implicit. Preserve full upstream licenses and modification notices in
public/terminal-notices and frontend distributions. English/Korean labels
cover terminal input/output, keyboard escape guidance, announcement limits and
selection status. Engine replacement introduces no control, search, graphics
surface, flag, fallback, selector, protocol, capability or migration.

Pass ordered Uint8Array output directly to the emulator with exact bigint
cursors and epoch checks. Keep at most 5000 scrollback lines. Explicit gaps reset
the parser and screen before retained suffix bytes; gap/connection/error notices
remain outside native bytes. Reattachment recovers only the available bounded
ring and never claims a full-screen application snapshot.

One retained control owner serializes input and resize. Admit each complete
paste atomically within 64 KiB of unsent bytes and send chunks of at most 32768
bytes. UTF-8 onData and binary onBinary preserve keyboard, IME, control and
bracketed-paste bytes; the native shell owns echo and line endings. Coalesce the
latest valid measured 1–500 rows/1–1000 columns after prior input acknowledgment.
Uncertain control retains its exact original request/revision and permits only
explicit retry. Definitive failures suspend dispatch until explicit reattachment.
Tab departure, hiding or detachment discards unsent bytes with a visible notice,
while dispatched uncertainty stays in the connection registry. Metadata/resize
acknowledgment never steals focus; first explicit attachment focuses once.
Hiding aborts observation only. Agent Stop preserves original processes;
explicit Close, Archive and deletion retain independent native cleanup gates.

### Project requirements

- Desktop lifecycle follows `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md#app-owned-sidecar-shutdown` and the CLI contract. Each main process owns at most one resident `server desktop-host --control-version 2` child; windows, browser cleanup and native helpers share its closed correlated operations. Directly bind `127.0.0.1:0`, pin the returned origin within the app lifetime, and prove the execution generation before bearer release. Preserve immutable pairing/recovery files and separate the private runtime locator from ordinary discovery; only explicitly paired Local Workers may follow it. Fence requests/replacement on Quit, cancel pending work, join final browser discovery, then shut down and allow 35 seconds before forcing only the retained original child and observing exit. EOF, desktop crash and forced exit terminate the owned host/server; tray hiding and independent Workers/CLI/service/remote servers retain their lifetimes. Reject occupied data scopes/ports without adoption or remapping. Keep Quit off the UI loop and distinguish forced-exit/native-cleanup uncertainty and actual platform evidence.

- macOS DeliDev development signing follows `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md#local-development-signing-and-recovery` and the credential contract. Keep explicitly registered local certificate authority separate from release signing, publish retained immutable executable copies, and preserve original server/Worker lifetimes and credentials. Changed running code requires recovery before fresh OAuth/protected access; no public RPC, capability or migration is added.

### Application integration

- `apps/delidev` owns DeliDev desktop presentation. Follow `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md` and scoped AGENTS. Keep direct Connect business flows, bounded in-memory connection state and exact mutation retries; frontend development uses fixed loopback port 46311. Component validation is separate from native desktop acceptance.

- Desktop local-agent support is default-off and exact-pinned to Codex `0.147.0`, Claude Code `2.1.233`, and OpenCode `1.18.18`. Keep executable overrides, health/version observations, consent state, explicitly saved per-repository prompts (including the configured issue tracker), and the 50 GiB LRU clone cache device-local; synchronize only bounded non-secret agent descriptors. Preserve v1-v6 prompt/profile records only as migration input; schema v7 rejects repository prompts from synchronized snapshots. Never install an agent or use a user working copy. Invoke with argv/stdin, an allowlisted environment, full-history managed/disposable clones, no LFS/submodules, ephemeral HTTPS askpass, a 15-minute timeout, and atomically purge-gated process-tree cancellation. Managed clones must refresh the remote default branch, preserve valid never-pushed repositories, reconcile interrupted cache publications, and reclone once when disposable cloning exposes corruption. Every agent invocation is credential-free, network-tool-disabled, and read-only: Draft output is reviewed strict JSON and the existing DevHUD client remains its GitHub writer; Direct output is strict marker readiness, after which the native host alone resolves the selected device-local PAT and runs one fixed argv-based `gh api` write. The agent never receives `GH_TOKEN`, a credential directory, the issue-input file, or the writer command. Every Direct result must reconcile the canonical repository URL and UUID-v7 marker. Delete finalized official uploads after definite pre-write failures, but retain them after the applicable DevHUD writer starts and a write becomes ambiguous. Never log prompts, output, child environments, full paths, or credentials, and never fall back automatically after failure.

- The owner permits Chromium without a process sandbox on Windows DevHud and DeliDev only while upstream lacks executable-host broker support. Keep this exception explicit in runtime selection, validation and user documentation. macOS/Linux require Chromium sandboxing. Desktop hosts use OS-backed secret storage except DeliDev macOS builds with `debug_assertions`, which use an explicit Mock cookie key in a separate development CEF root under the desktop/browser contracts. Keep Go credentials OS-protected, protected-browser IPC isolated, profile ownership exact and cleanup joined across both cookie paths. This exception grants no production Keychain or shutdown acceptance.

### apps/delidev constraints

- Repository heartbeat guidance follows `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md`: use the selected Machine's projected original Worker lease, classify offline only above 45,000 ms, and keep missing/failed current observations unknown. Read-only rechecks preserve selected machine/canonical root/drafts and never inspect, save, start or adopt another Worker.

- Terminal dependencies retain their original Apache-2.0, MIT and Unicode terms and complete upstream notices in public/terminal-notices, copied into frontend distributions. Preserve the version-pinned wterm/Ghostty modification notice; follow the desktop and repository license contracts.

- Subscription cleanup includes fully disconnected service-native accounts without synthetic login IDs. Explicit failed initial ChatGPT deletion uses the shared durable cleanup controller, preserves the original public deletion revision/receipt while checkpoint revisions advance, and never retries a terminal attempt without fresh explicit confirmation. Retain original actor/native/vault/reference checks; no new RPC, protocol allocation or migration. Follow the subscription and account contracts.

- Key-preserving API format changes follow `cmds-delidev-accounts-contract.md#connected-api-format-changes` after main reservation the originating change. Capability 9 owns the atomic format/preferences RPC and capability 10 gates its revision-bound Provider check; clients require both capabilities before enabling the connected operation. Preserve capability 7 and OAuth reservation 8, bounded server-owned generations sharing the original protected key, immutable original execution/continuation profiles, explicit current validation, all-generation cleanup and portable exclusions. Observation-only edits rebase protected fields/revision while retaining drafts; editable conflicts block saves. No migration, native change or format conversion.

- API key format selection follows the desktop/catalog/account contracts. Require an explicit per-key format, show it in list/details/Worker compatibility, use per-format custom Provider cards and shared Form dialogs, and negotiate capability 7. Preserve exact uncertain requests, secret disposal and numeric-token account patches; capability-7 changes require disconnect and confirmed cleanup; capability-9 changes retain the protected key and original execution generations. Keyless/key-required transitions require new accounts. Keep previews outside the repository.

- Direct startup follows `cmds-delidev-execution-startup-contract.md`. Remove the ordinary first-session checklist and required inspection controls; keep explicit Runner Devices diagnostics/path editing. Show session-owned safe failure summaries and validated metadata in the existing Info drawer. Retry startup uses original revision-checked Resume only after no-send/cleanup proof; uncertainty stays in recovery. Failure wording preserves independently acknowledged delivery and confirmed cleanup without granting resend authority. Preserve sidebar/composer, localization, contained focus/Escape and Settings lifetime.

- Trusted main DeliDev desktops automatically pair/start the fixed local Worker after authenticated local connection and own one joined native supervision task. Fresh launch or explicit Start may reopen ordinary stopped intent; ensure/retry preserve Stop, pending admission and updater ownership. Share current-user Worker service admission without manager writes. Retain original native child/control handles before readiness, recover only confirmed original exits, and stop only app-owned children on normal Quit under the existing 35-second grace. Preserve borrowed CLI/service Workers, saved connections, crash/EOF survival and all native execution uncertainty. Follow the desktop, CLI and user-service contracts; no protocol allocation or database migration.

- `subscription-cleanup.tsx` owns capability-41 one-click failed-login and disconnected-subscription cleanup, inline status/results and exact uncertain admission versus read-only status retries. Follow the subscription Settings contract; freeze account mutations but preserve navigation, category disposal, semantic 40px controls/8px corners, responsive wrapping and original focus. The server freezes all targets and owns deletion; presentation never replays login/callbacks or cancels admitted jobs.

- Normal desktop Quit follows `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md#app-owned-sidecar-shutdown` and the CLI contract: `server desktop-host --mode launch|retry|ensure` shares Go admission and runs newly admitted servers in their original child. Retain native child handles/control pipes before readiness, fence starts on Quit, join final browser discovery before Stop, then allow 35 seconds before original-child force and observed exit. Preserve close-to-tray, borrowed CLI/service/remote servers, independent Workers and crash/forced-desktop sidecar survival. EOF grants no Stop; original-generation suppression and forced-exit/native-cleanup uncertainty remain separate. Keep the complete Quit operation off the UI loop and record native/platform evidence separately.

- Agent Worker creation/editing follows the desktop wizard contract: Harness, same-source ordered multi-Accounts (minimum one), catalog/direct Model, Configure. Negotiate capability 33, save through the atomic typed RPC, retain exact revisions/retries and Settings disposal guards, and keep native/account readiness separate. Models settings is removed; Usage Model prices owns Token pricing, with original identities retained in record and price details.

- Harness selection uses the approved four-card grid in the existing 720px wizard, with decorative official local images preserving original colors and proportions. OpenCode/Grok use supplied light/dark variants under the resolved theme and initial OS fallback; retain source/version/hash, vendor usage conditions and separate licenses in `public/harness-marks`, independently of unchanged subscription assets. Follow the repository license and desktop contracts. Keep two columns at 640px available width and one below. Click or native Enter/Space confirmation immediately opens Accounts and focuses its heading, including current-card reselection; arrows and Home/End only change selection/focus. Harness has no Next button or form-submit advancement. Only a real harness change clears account/model choices; preserve server/mutation/size guards, the shared shell and later steps.

- The feature owns shared Settings body presentation in `src/settings-presentation.tsx`/`.css` (relative to `apps/delidev`). All 20 categories use one left anchor/1040px cap, 26px/32px H1, 16px/24px section titles, 14px/20px body, 12px/18px scope, 32px/24px/compact padding, 40px controls/8px corners, 16px rows, 24px section gaps and 720px flat forms with a 640px available-width column threshold. Keep two static loading skeletons, success-only 160px horizontal empties and compact singleton/table notices. Shared helpers own no RPC, permission, mutation, cursor, polling, lifecycle or persistent state. Notifications uses read-only saved statuses and explicit focus-owned Edit/Save/Cancel; Integrations keeps one header create action; subscription services are flat rows with negotiated account creation and independently gated native lifecycle; Appearance alone autosaves with native radios/CSS miniatures. Preserve all existing content/guards/visit semantics and ordinary-page rail/pane/drawer. Follow the desktop/subscription/diagnostics/transfer contracts, keeping browser fixtures/effective zoom separate from actual chrome zoom and packaged CEF/platform acceptance.

- Home New project/Create a project opens the existing Project editor directly over Sessions or New Session without selecting or mounting Settings. `src/project-creation.tsx` owns the independent scoped lifetime and mutation registry, original pending/uncertain task reopening, exact retries and active-query invalidation; App owns admission and disposal on another surface/conversation or connection identity. Preserve drafts, Home pages/filter/scroll, shared dialog geometry and visible opener/compact Home fallback focus. Keep Settings-internal creation unchanged and follow `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md#project-creation-outside-settings`.

- Multiple product windows follow `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md#multiple-product-windows`: retain one process-owned launch/supervisor, exact native Local/Saved role and instance admission, independent renderer memory and original callback epochs. New Window is a menu-click-only action handled by one native app menu handler with no accelerator (Command/Control+N is the renderer New session shortcut); Command/Control+T no longer opens a window. Close Window has no native accelerator; `CmdOrCtrl+W` is the fixed renderer SessionCloseTab shortcut closing only the selected closeable session workspace tab (Conversation stays pinned and the chord never closes or hides a window; W stays reserved against customization; external page-focused forwarding is unchanged; Keyboard Help dismisses before closure; terminal focus is eligible); only the last product window hides to tray. Saved profile removal blocks and closes all its views. Names update monotonically; Widget publication has one oldest-ready writer per profile. Preserve exact revisions, invalid/newer/linked files, atomic writes, uncertain recovery and authorized-window publication.
