### apps/delidev/scripts constraints

- Native builds and packaging must run the shared `prepare:assets` preflight before compilation. Hydrate only the exact DeliDev source-icon LFS path, first from the local cache and then by a path-scoped current-ref fetch. Validate the original pointer size/SHA-256 and PNG container, preserve local image/pointer edits, stop on failure or cancellation, and retain credential-free signing environments. A valid PNG needs neither Git nor network access. Follow `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md`.

- `dev:desktop` prepares the embedded frontend and sidecar. macOS uses the pinned Tauri CLI’s debug CEF app bundle, then signs/verifies and publishes a unique private copy before execution. Only its Go server uses the exact registered local self-signed Code Signing certificate and fixed `io.delino.delidev.development.server` identifier; the containing app remains ad-hoc signed with its original rights. `dev:signing --identity` stores only the public certificate fingerprint outside the checkout. Preserve `desktop-host`’s explicit `tauri-runtime-cef` dependency, `custom-protocol`, embedded assets, Chromium notices and bounded release-credential-free build environment. Share the package build lock through publication. Publish outside the checkout and Cargo target cache; retain those files across rebuild/cache cleanup/exit/crash while any original server or Worker can survive. Signal only the running desktop, never its sidecar process group. Keep application argv out of build options and logs. Follow `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md#local-development-signing-and-recovery`.

- Keep the background-extracted version of the supplied PNG as the canonical DeliDev app icon: both the outer dark rounded-square tile and the central dark play triangle are transparent. Preserve the colored ribbon's original shape, gradient, proportions, and transparent cutouts. The canonical artwork uses the approved 1.2× enlargement around the center of the unchanged 1254×1254 canvas, reducing outer transparent margins without clipping; preserve this enlarged scale rather than applying another enlargement during export. Generate the 256px native window/tray PNG and multiresolution Windows ICO from it, and include the full-resolution `icon-source@2x.png` in Tauri's bundle icons for macOS ICNS generation. Preserve the 1254px canvas and `@2x` density marker: the pinned bundler downsizes it to 1024px, which ICNS supports only at retina density. Track the source through exact-path Git LFS as documented in `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md` and `repository-workflow-contract.md`.

- Dialog layout fixtures follow the duplicate-dismissal contract in `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md`. Assert absence of audited duplicate buttons and empty footers, safe named header-close focus for destructive tasks, and retained distinct nested cancellation. Keep browser focus/layout evidence separate from packaged CEF/platform acceptance.

### apps/delidev/src-tauri constraints

- Image input previews and authenticated retained-image readback may use local `blob:` image sources under `cmds-delidev-image-input-contract.md`. Keep the allowance restricted to image CSP; no external image origin, filesystem authority or native transfer binding is added.

- Trusted main DeliDev desktops automatically pair/start the fixed local Worker after authenticated local connection and own one joined native supervision task. Fresh launch or explicit Start may reopen ordinary stopped intent; ensure/retry preserve Stop, pending admission and updater ownership. Share current-user Worker service admission without manager writes. Retain original native child/control handles before readiness, recover only confirmed original exits, and stop only app-owned children on normal Quit under the existing 35-second grace. Preserve borrowed CLI/service Workers, saved connections, Worker survival after desktop crash/EOF and all native execution uncertainty. Follow the desktop, CLI and user-service contracts; no protocol allocation or database migration.

- Normal desktop Quit follows `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md#app-owned-sidecar-shutdown` and `cmds-delidev-contract.md`: retain one `server desktop-host --control-version 2` session and use its correlated `runtime.launch`, `runtime.retry` and `runtime.ensure` operations. Retain original native child handles/control pipes before readiness. Fence requests, starts and replacement on Quit, cancel pending interactive work, join final bounded browser removal discovery through the same session, then request `runtime.shutdown` and join the owned server/host operations. Allow 35 seconds before forcing only the retained original child and observing exit. Preserve close-to-tray, borrowed CLI/service/remote servers and independent Workers. EOF, desktop crash and forced exit terminate the app-owned CLI/server; they grant no Stop authority over independent Workers or external servers. Original-generation suppression, forced-exit and native-cleanup uncertainty remain separate; retain original handles when force or exit cannot be proved. Keep the complete joined Quit operation off the UI loop and record native/platform evidence separately.

- Launch, Retry and Ensure use the retained version-2 host's `runtime.launch`, `runtime.retry` and `runtime.ensure` operations. Pairing and launch observations share that session and its runtime transport; never call the retired `--mode` controller. Validate the complete launch/pair/observe/shutdown path with the real Go sidecar in a temporary private scope, separately from framed fixtures and packaged native acceptance.

- `widget_writer.rs` owns the bounded FIFO persistence task and its terminal stale publication for this feature. `tray_host.rs` owns projection/admission and scope/revision/window/oldest-ready rechecks, releasing all state before the Swift ABI. Tray UI reads skip contention. Quit calls only nonblocking publication fencing on the UI loop; join widget, timer, notification, OAuth and window tasks on the tracked Quit worker before permitting native exit. Final-write failure reports uncertainty, never a fabricated durable stale result or blind retry. Follow the widget and desktop contracts and record native evidence separately.

- Multiple product windows follow `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md#multiple-product-windows`: retain one process-owned launch/supervisor, exact native Local/Saved role and instance admission, independent renderer memory and original callback epochs. New Window is a menu-click-only action handled by one native app menu handler with no accelerator (Command/Control+N is the renderer New session shortcut); Command/Control+T no longer opens a window. Close Window has no native accelerator; `CmdOrCtrl+W` is the fixed renderer SessionCloseTab shortcut closing only the selected closeable session workspace tab (Conversation stays pinned and the chord never closes or hides a window; W stays reserved against customization; external page-focused forwarding is unchanged; Keyboard Help dismisses before closure; terminal focus is eligible); only the last product window hides to tray. Saved profile removal blocks and closes all its views. Names update monotonically; Widget publication has one oldest-ready writer per profile. Window destruction listeners retain registry state only, never AppHandle cycles that outlive native shutdown. Never transfer drafts, replay startup/pairing, persist window inventory or grant authority from a label pattern alone. Local bootstrap, registration inspection/recovery and original Local Worker commands admit registered Local `main`/`local-*` documents; Saved `server-*` documents retain their independent profile/server bindings and cannot acquire Local authority. Capability label patterns never replace exact native role/instance admission, trusted-document checks or original authority rechecks after asynchronous work. Local connection/recovery results update process-wide supervision only after the original Local role/instance/revision authority passes its post-Go recheck; stale results leave the supervised connection unchanged. All Local windows share the original process launch observation; additional windows never replay automatic startup, pairing or supervision. Preserve closed structured failure diagnostics without credentials, user state or raw native content.

- Provider help accepts only a closed canonical preset/action on an original trusted main or saved-window instance. Declare `open_provider_guidance` in the build app manifest and grant its dedicated `provider-guidance` permission only to the `main` and `server-*` webviews. Test the generated manifests/capabilities with Tauri's authority resolver; parent windows and remote pages cannot grant this command to external children. Use Go-generated `provider-guidance.generated.json`, never RPC/renderer-selected URLs, and preserve regional key guidance. `browser_opener.rs` is an internal bounded OS dispatcher for separately validated callers, with minimal environment, silent streams and joined cancellation; it is not a generic native capability. Provider help opens through the selected general browser destination (see [Browser destinations for external links](#browser-destinations-for-external-links)); OAuth authorization keeps the system default. Follow the provider and desktop contracts.

- `src/oauth.rs` and `src/oauth_host.rs` implement the closed managed API browser/callback infrastructure under `cmds-delidev-account-oauth-contract.md`. Capture/recheck trusted-window native epochs, selected server and saved-window instance; bind both loopback families to one ephemeral port and retain one generation per opening. Bound parsing and single-use code transfer, return constant no-store/no-referrer callback pages, clear transient bytes and join listeners/openers on disposal. Scoped tombstones block a queued Begin after unknown-response disposal; late predecessor cleanup cannot revoke replacements. Every disposal, expiry, window-close and epoch insertion preserves the 4096-entry bounds. Known identities remain idempotent at capacity; overflow retains all revocations, stores no overflowing identity, closes admission and joins every original callback listener. Rust never exchanges a code or stores a provider credential, broadcasts callbacks or exposes a generic opener. Settings departure removes local authority without implicit business cancellation.

- Register `account_oauth_native` in the build-time app command manifest and grant only the `account-oauth` permission to the existing trusted `main` and `server-*` webviews. Test the generated allowed-command list and resolved ACL, including denial to raw child webviews inside trusted windows and remote documents. Keep runtime window/server/epoch checks independently enforced. Native OAuth logs contain only closed action, phase, outcome and failure metadata; omit successful callback polling and all URLs, codes, credentials and scope values.

- Closed GitHub presentation shell fixtures also publish through a joined child writer to exclude inherited writable script descriptors during parallel exec. Assert exact data-directory/closed-operation arguments and the exact closed NativeFailure for malformed output, rejected acknowledgment and nonzero exit; permit bounded benign stderr. Record every sidecar entry before validation, require one invocation for valid input, no invocation for rejected input, and no server-state bootstrap. Keep production deadlines and acknowledgment validation unchanged; unexplained CI failures remain uncertain until their closed error is recorded.

- Local connection and registration permission errors must explain both device authorization and owner-only private state; do not equate a permission denial with an owner being unable to read files or a revoked registration. Give macOS/Linux guidance of 0700 for private directories and 0600 for private files, preserve existing data, and never automatically change permissions or offer replacement without verified revoked-client evidence.

- CEF URL getters block on the native UI loop at the pinned revision. Keep every command reaching URL authorization asynchronous and move native callback authorization off that loop; recheck shutdown and notification generations before publishing navigation. Bundling must enable the local `custom-protocol` feature as well as the `tauri-runtime-cef` dependency.

- Enable native accessibility for each trusted CEF document after load, including saved-server windows created after the initial accessibility notification. Keep native content out of logs, use the UI-loop callback and retain the matching pinned CEF dependency. Record the Exit event, notification/tray task joins and runtime return separately, without equating an event or join with observed process termination. Record delayed native browser teardown separately from independent server lifetime.

- Desktop uses CEF at the existing immutable Tauri revision and the CEF helper entry point, with macOS 13 retained. Bind capabilities to trusted webview labels, never window-wide labels that grant future external child views app authority. Keep engine migration distinct from account-browser persistence and cleanup evidence.

- Refresh tray overview and the selected UTC-day usage summary every 15 seconds, including hidden windows, so native publication cannot keep resetting freshness for unchanged usage. Account reads refresh every 30 seconds; failed or missing usage stays unavailable.

- macOS application reopening restores the most recently used live product window through the same unminimize/show/focus path as tray activation. Never recreate the renderer, reset its geometry or submit work to restore presentation. Follow `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md`; keep actual OS reopen evidence separate from tray-menu activation.

- Session files follow `cmds-delidev-files-contract.md`. Use owner/client Connect Query reads in the right session application area, preserving the mounted composer and unsent draft. File contents are inert text; retain exact sizes, explicit binary/truncated/unavailable states, scoped repository selection and stale-page errors. Cancel inactive reads and discard their nonpersistent query data when navigation or closing removes the view. No filesystem Tauri binding or link/citation-derived authority.

- The Inbox is one persistent paginated list/detail workspace for requests and terminal results; tray activation selects the exact item through a fresh `GetInboxEntry` read and never marks it read. Use server-side source/read-state enum filters and pages of 20. Retain typed response drafts only in connection memory, bound them to the original interaction ID, revision and request identity, cap them at 4 MiB/1,000 nonempty requests, preserve stale drafts read-only, and allow an uncertain retry only after a fresh authorized source read. Keep active response controls gated by the current source/session state; retain the workspace across surface navigation and keep notification polling separate.

- Claude Code discovery uses only its pinned stream-json initialization profile in a fresh private bare runtime, with no inherited credentials, OAuth/keychain access, project extensions, persistent sessions or prompts. Accept one exact correlated control response with no token, explicit closed permission/remote-control state and bounded typed descriptors; reject unknown/duplicate/trailing output. Bound and join both streams and the input writer, preserve cleanup uncertainty, and publish only the handshake outcome. Model/agent advertisements cannot grant account readiness or execution; Claude session execution and subscription login require their separate adapters.

- Follow `cmds-delidev-credentials-contract.md` for protected server secrets. Keep wrapping material in the native OS store, payloads authenticated-encrypted, and immutable request references/deletion markers durable across uncertainty. Never silently unlock, enumerate user credentials, replace a missing sealed key, or use a plaintext fallback. Native tests must use temporary keychains/UUID entries or an explicitly disposable Secret Service container; never lock a user's shared collection. A stored secret does not establish account readiness.

- Native desktop registration inspection/recovery must pass the compiled fixed endpoint as a Go-side guard before recovery intent or pairing. An endpoint mismatch cannot create or publish a replacement; post-publication connection validation is additional defense, never the first endpoint check.

- Protected browser contexts follow `cmds-delidev-browser-contract.md`. Reserve exact presentation IDs on the UI loop before asynchronous Go reads, releasing the superseded raw child and invalidating late creation even if replacement preparation fails. Keep raw external CEF children outside Tauri browser-side IPC handlers and initialization scripts, explicitly reject their process messages despite the pinned runtime's shared renderer stub, and count native creation/close callbacks through exit. Never remove a profile before poller join, all native close proofs and independently observed CEF shutdown return; retain original offline removal intents and exact acknowledgment retries.

- Before forgetting a saved connection, persist its original browser scope for local purge. Discover completed CLI removals through retained connection tombstones; deny reopen and purge only after independently completed CEF shutdown, without using deleted client credentials or claiming remote acknowledgment.

- `src/browser_storage.rs` owns the compiled CEF storage mode, fixed cookie roots and shared host lease. Only macOS `debug_assertions` builds select explicit Mock; all other builds select System. Embedded development enables `custom-protocol`, so never use Tauri Auto as the mode gate. Retain the original System profile paths, shared tabs and deletion journals; place development CEF data under `browser-data/development`. Hold the owner-private non-symlink host lock from before CEF initialization through runtime return and durable cleanup, never unlink it, and reject competing hosts. Purge both cookie roots before acknowledgment or retiring a forgotten-scope marker, retaining exact failures and retry ownership. Never migrate/copy existing cookies or weaken Go credential storage. Logs expose only the closed mode/code and the development public-key notice; no raw cache/native content. Development Mock cannot prove production Keychain, renderer shutdown or release acceptance.

- Browser validation, profile reads and durable writes run on serialized workers without holding native state during I/O. Post only CEF/native presentation work to the UI loop, recheck trusted documents and exact generations after preparation, coalesce bounded address updates, and join their worker before post-shutdown purge.

- Stage durable tab-control writes before exact reservation validation. Fence final publication against UI reservation acceptance from a blocking worker; the UI callback must never acquire that fence or wait for storage, and stale preparations must leave the prior tabs intact.

- First-tab initialization must use the same staged publication fence and reservation check; a superseded initial open cannot publish its starting address into a replacement profile.

- Bound the worker's UI-reservation wait and cancel unexecuted late callbacks before releasing its publication fence. Native shutdown must not leave the address-worker join waiting for a reservation callback that the UI loop can no longer deliver.

- Observed-address writes must stage first and recheck the profile, child generation and current reservation under the same worker publication fence before replacing durable tabs.

- Quit closes address-callback acceptance under the bounded queue gate and drains previously accepted updates on the tracked worker. Shutdown alone cannot discard them; exact generation, reservation and removal checks still reject invalid writes. Join that worker before profile purge without making the UI wait for storage.

- Retain asynchronous raw-child creation failure only for its exact profile, generation and reservation. Native state polling and ordinary controls must surface the typed failure until explicit presentation retry; stale creation failures must not poison replacements or hide tracked removal.

- Initial native geometry/host failures in the after-created callback follow the same exact failure retention before requesting child closure. The close callback clears the child handle without clearing that failure; an explicit replacement presentation starts fresh.

- Shared-profile tab replacement must attempt every affected child even when an earlier creation fails. Retain each exact view's failure and return the first failure only after all replacements have been attempted.

- Replace shared browser children only when their selected tab identity changes. Closing a background tab or selecting the current tab preserves page state, navigation history, pending creation and exact retained failure.

- Before replacing a selected/final tab child or superseding a presentation, synchronously unmap every old child before dropping handles or advancing generations. An unmap failure retains the original views and cleanup identity; request asynchronous close only after releasing native state. Removal/quit retain each child handle until its exact callback, so concurrent Hide cannot mistake a delayed close for invisibility.

- Discovered profile removal and forgetting a saved server/device scope synchronously unmap every matching child before requesting asynchronous CEF closure. Mark all matching views closing before native work. Attempt every user even if one unmap fails, retain original handles and presentation identities for exact Hide retries and callbacks, and release native state before unmap and close requests. Keep unrelated scopes and pending-creation guards intact. Failed unmapping never grants profile-purge authority.

- Browser Hide is idempotent for an exact original view: synchronously hide only its matching native child before acknowledging success, or retain ownership until its exact close callback proves absence. Pending native creation and failed native hiding keep the original identity pending and deny ordinary controls. Confirm absence without touching a superseding view and return no browsing data from cleanup, including absent or unrelated-window requests. Preserve trusted-document checks and offline closure; native close accounting still gates process shutdown.

- Actual native window close and explicit saved-window destruction must invalidate its browser reservation and pending context creation and request raw-child closure on the UI loop before destroying the parent. The saved-window Destroyed fallback checks the original binding instance before closing its exact window view and releasing the binding. Tray hiding preserves presentation; window closure retains profiles and native callback counts until independent shutdown.

- Browser cleanup discovery uses an independent read-only controller with a two-second joined-child deadline; never hold the interactive connector gate through offline polling. Stage saved-connection purge only after fallible window setup, bind its exact original removal identity, and require a fresh retained Go removal receipt plus complete CEF shutdown before deleting bytes. Unchanged paired evidence cancels only the unaccepted intent; uncertain acceptance and independent account removal remain pending. Follow `cmds-delidev-browser-contract.md`.

- Advance the durable account-removal cursor before acknowledgment attempts, rotating retained intents across process exits so offline receipts cannot starve later local profile purges. Keep original request/revision ownership and the existing per-exit bounds.

- Forgotten-scope and account-removal cleanup have independent 45-second/64-intent budgets after native shutdown. A depleted budget or local queue failure cannot prevent the other queue from running, account cursor advancement or local account-profile purge. Preserve shared shutdown/discovery/storage prerequisites and return the first local failure after both passes.

- Quit denies presentations immediately but retains the CEF event loop until the worker's final bounded removal discovery finishes and every raw child closes. Perform that final discovery even when quit arrives during the poll sleep; never move its sidecar reads or durable intent writes onto the UI loop.

- Fresh main hosts own one joined launch before supervision; helpers/saved windows/renderer observations cannot replay it. Recheck current durable Stop and fixed client authority before returning cached success. Explicit Retry preserves Stop; advanced Start shares Go desktop-launch service admission and cannot bypass installed registration ownership. Advanced Start/recovery adopt only verified outcomes. Go automatic/desktop startup uses one 35-second aggregate wait budget below the native 40-second command bound; never reset it per joined phase. Cancel and join short controllers on Quit, then join only original app-owned server children under the app-owned sidecar shutdown contract; borrowed and abnormal-exit lifetimes remain independent. Keep lifecycle logs bounded and secret/output/path-free.

- Device appearance follows the feature and the desktop contract. Only registered local (`main`/`local-*`) and saved (`server-*`) documents may read/update the versioned `appearance.json` in `app_config_dir`. Keep it outside server data, pairing, backup and configuration transfer. Serialize bounded validated reads and atomic synchronized writes, publish committed changes to trusted windows only, and order snapshots with non-wrapping process revisions. Preserve invalid/newer files with System fallback; failed writes retain the last committed preference and uncertain outcomes require inspection before retry. Never grant generic filesystem authority or expose file paths/raw OS errors in diagnostics. Tests inject temporary directories.

- `choose_repository_folder` is one asynchronous folder-only dialog per process for this feature. Accept no renderer-selected path/authority; authorize a registered trusted local window or the exact saved-server binding before opening and after completion, bound the selected native path and return cancellation without Git/content access. Keep the repository-pinned optional rfd version and phase/code-only logs.

- The native service-ownership shell fixture publishes its executable through a joined child writer, so parallel fixture forks cannot inherit a parent-owned writable script description and cause Linux `ETXTBSY`. Keep the production connector unchanged and report only the observed closed failure classification on assertion failure; passing repetitions do not establish the cause of an earlier unexplained CI failure.

- Subscription recovery notifications use the closed subscription-recovery kind and fixed masked product text. Renderer input remains limited to original opaque claim/inbox identities; no account identity, alias, quota value or provider content enters native presentation.

- `worker_network_control` grants only Prepare/Import/Status on a registered trusted local or exact saved-server window's existing same-computer Worker. Native selects the scope, rejects foreign machine/input and rechecks saved-window generation after the joined sidecar operation. No renderer path, endpoint, key or saved-profile selector is accepted. Go owns X25519, import validation and protected storage; ciphertext/digest are bounded transient input and public result parsing rejects extra/private fields. Never implicitly register, start, stop or replace the Worker.

- Callback polling rechecks the non-secret authority captured by the original Go-verified local connection against its fixed descriptor; it cannot spawn sidecars or contend for the connector command gate. Exact BindOpen replay returns its original binding without reopening a browser. Changed binding evidence is refused.

- Signed updates and SSH Worker setup follow `cmds-delidev-updates-contract.md` and `cmds-delidev-ssh-setup-contract.md`. Preserve compiled release authority, exact confirmed host identity, protected credentials, original registration/workspaces, once-only remote effects and joined Worker replacement. Never replace live server/harness binaries or treat fixtures as installed-platform acceptance.

- Accepted desktop installations own a native tracked task and original outcome token independently of renderer/window lifetime. After accepted begin, pre-effect authority loss records Failed with no installer call; later results retain actual phase. Quit fences new work, cancels and joins installation plus bounded offline settlement before sidecar shutdown. Only the retained token may write its exact original journal outside ordinary connector admission. Retry the same phase after reply loss; never replay installation or replace original authority. Failed publication retains original uncertainty and inspection ownership.

- Declare `desktop_update_context` and `desktop_update_native` in the generated application manifest and dedicated `desktop-update` permission only for main/local-* and server-* product documents. Keep external/child/remote webviews outside that ACL, and require native registry admission plus original window, saved binding, epoch and server/lifetime checks after the label-pattern grant. Generated ACL fixtures/builds do not establish installed-platform update acceptance.

- Desktop updates remain under the original trusted window/saved binding and native lifetime epoch. Go owns signature verification and durable installation claim; Rust hashes exclusive staged bytes and owns a concrete native confirmation plus closed OS installation. Preserve old same-volume macOS bundles, exact AppImage mount authority and truthful NSIS uncertainty. Decode bounded kernel mountinfo mount-point/source escapes once before exact AppImage correlation; malformed or unsupported escapes grant no authority. Keep absolute-path, executable, regular-file and symlink checks. Record results even offline, forbid installation replay and omit private paths from renderer results.

- Preserve the app Cargo manifest's exact-path LF attribute so the pinned CLI cannot dirty a Windows checkout through newline serialization. Keep revision-bound package validation strict; formatting normalization cannot permit actual manifest/source changes.

- Subscription browser controls share the trusted OAuth host under the managed subscription contract. Bind the original official ChatGPT URL, state, server/window/opening epoch and operation; initial binding replay never opens twice. Deliberate reopen uses the same URL even after a lost binding reply. Local login retains the original server callback; remote login owns both loopback families at the pinned registered 1457 callback. Accept only exact localhost or 127.0.0.1 `/auth/callback` URIs, retain the original spelling and require its exact HTTP Host. The receiver consumes only one closed code/state/scope query and joins on terminal/departure disposal. Never remap, switch to device authentication, log URLs/codes/identities or forward callbacks after lifetime loss.

- Sidecar PATH includes OS defaults, bounded sanitized absolute inherited entries and macOS Homebrew paths under the desktop contract. Deduplicate, exclude empty/relative entries, never run shell startup files and preserve the cleared environment allowlist.

- General API OAuth adds closed accepted Hugging Face profile inventory and browser/callback control. Read the same compiled public registration metadata as Go, bind fixed official authorization fields and original state, and transfer one code/state or access-denied callback to the owning window. Pending profiles grant no listener or opener authority. Keep subscription callback ownership separate. Follow `cmds-delidev-account-oauth-contract.md`.

- The accepted Gemini public profile uses the exact IPv4 loopback callback and closed Google authorization fields. Bind original state and allow only bounded authuser/prompt callback metadata for this profile; Hugging Face and subscription callbacks cannot gain those fields. Follow `cmds-delidev-account-oauth-contract.md`.

- Baseten Device OAuth retains original window/server/opening/generation ownership without a listener. Advertise it only with the accepted shared compiled registration and exact approval URI; BindOpen cannot receive query credentials, arbitrary paths or another provider URL. No native polling, Device code, token or public Take callback is supported.

- Claude subscription browser Open/Reopen uses closed pinned original URLs and trusted main-window/server/Settings lifetime/operation/generation ownership. The native validator accepts the auth-login profile and, separately, the server-owned setup-token profile (exactly the `user:inference` scope, the manual code callback and `code=true`; never a localhost callback), matching the frontend and Go validators. Keep browser binding kinds disjoint from provider/Codex callback flows; create no listener or code receiver, never exchange or persist code. Initial replay cannot reopen; explicit reopen preserves exact original URL. Disposal or scope changes erase presentation authority under the desktop/subscription contracts.
- Grok Build subscription browser Open/Reopen (`grok-subscription-open`, `grok-subscription-reopen`, `BrowserBindingKind::GrokSubscription`, TypeScript `OAuthNativeAction.GrokSubscriptionOpen/GrokSubscriptionReopen`) uses the same trusted main-window/server/Settings lifetime/operation/generation ownership and stays disjoint from provider, Codex and Claude kinds; it adds no `OAuthProfile`. The native validator accepts only a raw `https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/authorize` URL (no port, credentials or fragment; `url.as_str()` equal to the input) with a closed query: `response_type=code`, client `b1a00492-073a-47ea-816f-4c329264a828`, S256 with a 43-character challenge, nonempty `[A-Za-z0-9-_.~]` `state` and `nonce` (at most 512 bytes), optional `referrer=grok-build`, optional space-separated `scope`, and `redirect_uri` exactly `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` with a numeric unprivileged port. Duplicate or unknown keys are refused. A valid URL opens once; initial replay never reopens; Reopen opens only the original URL once. Local login (`local=true`) binds nothing and only opens the URL because the server owns the loopback listener. Remote login is refused with `Incompatible` (after validation, before any browser or listener exists) until the server advertises the Grok flow: the server's `ForwardSubscriptionCallback` is now service-aware (a Grok account relays to the dynamic loopback port and original state of its own login; the ChatGPT/Codex login keeps `auth.openai.com`, port 1457), but the capability stays unadvertised, so a consumed one-shot code is never produced before it can be delivered. The native host gates this on a private flag that stays false until the server validates and forwards Grok callbacks by service (Grok host, state and the bound dynamic port) while Codex forwarding stays unchanged. With that flag enabled, remote login binds IPv4 `127.0.0.1` on that same port only, accepts one loopback-peer `GET /callback` with exact Host `127.0.0.1:<port>` and a closed `code`/`state`/`scope` query whose state equals the original, and Take returns that query once for the existing TypeScript path to forward through `ForwardSubscriptionCallback` bound to the operation id. A bind conflict fails as `SidecarFailed` and never remaps the port; a denial or `iss` redirect is refused until the real redirect shape is recorded. Second, late, expired or post-close deliveries are dropped: the listener handler reads no longer than the attempt deadline and rechecks it immediately before the one-shot claim, so a peer accepted just before expiry cannot store a code afterwards, codes are zeroized on drop, and URLs, codes and state are never logged. The receiver joins on disposal, window close or expiry. Grok device sign-in uses the separate stateless `grok-device-authorization-open` action (`OAuthAction::GrokDeviceAuthorizationOpen`, TypeScript `OAuthNativeAction.GrokDeviceAuthorizationOpen`) with the same trusted window/server/Settings lifetime checks and the original operation ID as the attempt identity. It requires an empty generation, refuses a disposed opening, and accepts only a raw `https://accounts.x.ai/oauth2/device` URL (no port, credentials or fragment; `url.as_str()` equal to the input) with either no query or exactly one `user_code` matching `[A-Z0-9-]{4,32}`; anything else is `InvalidInput` before any browser opens. It binds no listener, records no attempt or disposed entry and returns an empty result, so a browser login in the same window is undisturbed; each deliberate click opens the page once through the OAuth dispatcher (`browser_opener::dispatch`), which always uses the operating-system default browser, never the General/Local choice or `open_external_url`.

- `credential_access.rs` retains one startup Keychain attempt and its paired client in the native Connector across renderer/window lifetimes. Reconcile the client only after successful explicit local-registration recovery for the same server; preserve the attempt/result and fail closed unless the previous client is revoked. Grant `desktop_credential_access` only to trusted Local webviews through its dedicated permission, recheck window/server/runtime authority before dispatch and response, and accept only Observe/Retry/Skip. Go owns existing vault reads and joined cancellation. Never expose credential bytes, accept account/path selectors, retry terminal failures automatically or weaken original 35-second shutdown. Follow the desktop/credential contracts.

Restore only untouched permitted fields by exact resource ID, retaining disconnected registered runners and Local proof precedence. Preference failures never repeat CreateSession.

Never mount Desktop/Connect/device controllers, refresh product observations on panel interaction, reset freshness, pool quotas, infer services/IDs, or log account/native content. External child views have no preference access. Failed/uncertain writes require explicit inspection; category disposal never cancels admitted native storage. Preserve fixed product/editing reservations and log classifications/revisions only, never keys/chords or text. Preserve exact revisions, invalid/newer/linked files, atomic writes, uncertain recovery and authorized-window publication. Presentation changes preserve mounted drafts/focus/request identities, original observations and authenticated Worker image bytes/cleanup; renderer toggles stay unavailable until independently implemented support exists. The marked set covers Claude compaction pre/post/dropped tokens and duration, Claude Task usage `total_tokens` and `duration_ms`, Claude estimated thinking tokens, Claude tool-progress elapsed seconds, Claude Task update reported end time and total paused time, Codex/OpenCode current context tokens, the Session Context current, latest native-reported and used-of-capacity context token lines plus the capacity progress bar whose `aria-valuetext` carries the token count, Grok tool context tokens, and Grok tools-terminal token totals and elapsed time. Trigger, `tool_uses`, retry delay settings, disclosures, history controls, identity text and the turn-timing line stay visible, each toggle works independently, and turning one On restores the unchanged original values with no request or history mutation.

Count only actual client-generated raw transport failures after a matching success baseline; cache only acknowledged scoped preferences, reserve a private immutable local edge before OS submission, share observation across original windows and join reads/presentation on Quit. Missing cache, denied/failed/uncertain OS results and ledger bounds suppress rather than retry. A transient or unconfirmed native observation under still-valid original authority is retried on the next 30-second tick without disposing the connection's native scopes; scopes are disposed only on verified authority loss, stopping/Quit, cancellation or a local state error, each logged with a closed disposal reason. Never fabricate server Inbox IDs, prompt automatically or acquire execution authority.

B remains a fixed product shortcut reservation, not an editable override.

Keep both URL-authorizing commands asynchronous, checksum/bounds and original instance/connection guards, one process-owned pending operation, replay receipts and joined Quit publication. Unknown/positive status keeps Cancel available; cancellation grants no cleanup or mutation authority. Confirm joins the existing shutdown once off the UI loop, preserving close-to-tray,35-second original-child grace, borrowed/remote lifetime and mandatory updater/crash behavior. ### apps/delidev/src constraints

- Project first-prompt history follows the sessions/storage/desktop/protocol/client contracts for the feature. Preserve immutable project-owned text with empty session IDs, atomic 100-entry acceptance order, actor-bound confirmed clear receipts, scoped byte-bounded reads and text-only boundary recall. System 48 / EntityKind 35 add no Worker capability or migration. Session deletion preserves history; project deletion removes it, managed backups capture it and portable exports exclude it. Never log prompt text.

- `session-tabs.tsx`, `session-tab-bar.tsx`, `session-activity.tsx` and `session.tsx` own connection-scoped typed session presentation tabs. Keep Conversation pinned first, exactly one active content pane and persistent original Info. Files/comparisons use original repository/path/kind identities and discard inactive bytes; terminals/pages/Sidechats use original resource IDs. Retain authoring and accepted/uncertain controllers, suspend inactive observations, and never create, delete or retry from presentation close/reopen. Sidechat actions/Info bind the child and retained navigation routes its original parent. Terminal attachments retain unsent-discard guidance and independent process ownership. Browser departure retains original Hide cleanup before replacement.

- Files Back retains original inner and enclosing Session scroll owner snapshots under the same controller/repository identity; restore selected focus with preventScroll and restore only connected original ancestors containing the returned tree. Replacement repositories/connections cannot receive old scroll state.

- `entrance-motion.ts`/`.css` own the shared 160ms Y4 entrance primitive and replay-safe `useEntranceActivation` hook under `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md#shared-restrained-entrance-motion-and-appearance`. Keep keyframes static, add no inline style or dependency, and let each Settings category opt in through the `entranceCategories` map (category to `EntranceTarget`) with its own contract text; see the Settings category entrance section.

- Image composers follow `cmds-delidev-image-input-contract.md` and `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md#image-inputs`. `image-input.ts` owns bounded original-byte validation and complete reference/receipt verification; `image-drafts.tsx` owns connection-identity drafts, exact staging/recovery and original Runner cleanup. Preserve independent first-message/General Chat/Session drafts across navigation, Settings and reconnect; dispose bytes/object URLs on identity change. Keep typed references separate from document JSON, require READY and matching ordered admission receipts, restage changed Runner/operation selections, and retain uncertain requests without edits. `image-attachments.tsx` owns ordered accessible previews and authenticated digest-verified history readback with explicit retry; queued edits retain immutable refs and image-bound Steer remains disabled. System 45/Worker 25 and the original execution harness are advisory frontend gates; native modality proof remains backend-owned. `useImageRoute` admits Codex Agents and OpenCode Agents whose every source route model declares the `image` input modality and whose System and Runner Device report the independent OpenCode image pair (System 105 / Worker 70); queued follow-ups use the frozen execution harness plus `image_input_declared` for OpenCode, and Sidechat, Claude Code and Grok Build stay unsupported. The en/ko creation guidance states the OpenCode 384 KiB combined limit and its required message text. The isolated image browser fixture grants no native/account acceptance and must stay outside product bundles.

- `runner-observation.ts` owns bounded closed presentation evidence, without changing the original Runner eligibility predicate. The shared Runner provider retains one exact machine controller across presenter close and same-identity readiness changes; full Settings inspection preserves Updates and network tools. Exact-machine pending or uncertain inspection retains consuming-flow gates. SessionTools likewise retains one original controller; the owning conversation failure exposes its eligible recovery action and original confirmation within the same session, including Info for constrained layouts. Account reads older than retained acknowledgments cannot enable fresh lifecycle actions, while original uncertain retries and durable cleanup retain their own authority.

- `account-remediation-layout.fixture.tsx` and `session-remediation-layout.fixture.tsx` are isolated synthetic entries for inline failure/confirmation/recheck geometry and focus. Keep fixtures out of the product bundle; their counters prove no fixture mutation, never real native/account acceptance. Original task, controller, query and draft lifetimes remain authoritative.

- Inline workflow problems follow `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md#inline-workflow-remediation-issue-1699` and the diagnostics/subscription contracts. Keep typed safe guidance and supported original actions visible beside the owning failure. `ui.tsx` is presentation only; `local-connection-presentation.tsx` moves original views without native reads or repair authority. Share exact controller/request/busy/confirmation state, distinguish loading/error/empty/current-page/continuation/stale/malformed evidence, and preserve drafts, revisions, native generations, cleanup, Stop and disposal. Do not add automatic Doctor reads, duplicate recovery controllers, new repair authority, account-storage UI or the removed Search shortcut. External installation/OS/remote remedies use concrete manual steps plus existing rechecks.

- Sidebar session actions are owned by `session-row-actions.tsx` under one sidebar opening. Read the exact Session and budget only while open; never infer action eligibility from navigation outcomes. `session-control.tsx` shares detail/menu eligibility and `control:<id>` retained request locks, and holds accepted original acknowledgments in a connection-owned cache bounded to 1,000 entries/8 MiB of exact wire bytes. Protect active detail/open-menu snapshots during eviction; keep original pending/uncertain requests in the independent mutation registry. Reject invalid revisions and unreadable/unsupported Session documents before enabling row actions. Reuse the connection Fork provider with Fork-only menu presentation. Preserve selection/drafts, original revision/retry authority, independent archive/terminal lifetimes, hover exclusion and keyboard/drawer focus.

- OAuth format selection activates only the main-established the originating change ProviderInventory capability 8 and Start/attempt fields 4/7. Follow `cmds-delidev-account-oauth-contract.md#oauth-api-format-selection-reservations`: bind the original explicit Bearer profile without changing the authentication adapter, retain omitted legacy receipt bytes and original recovery/cleanup authority, and keep unaccepted provider registrations disabled. Common manual/OAuth UI explicitly selects multiple formats or displays a sole profile; no migration or native change.

- All app-owned dialogs and compact modal navigation use the shared approximately 12% black `--backdrop: f` token under `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md#modal-background-visibility`. Keep underlying content visible and category headings, column geometry and scroll stable while preserving `showModal`, Settings inert/disabled boundaries, focus containment/restoration and task lifetimes. Do not hide inventories, local Worker controls or pairing presentation solely for a modal, or add viewport-sized shadows, blur or a separate overlay manager. Preserve native per-modal backdrop stacking, undimmed wide nonmodal navigation, inactive-surface, disclosure and same-window task-step hiding; OS-owned dialogs are separate.

Preserve request bytes, fresh confirmation after terminal retention and disposed-callback fencing. Auto cleanup includes fully disconnected subscriptions across services; account selection and cleanup proof stay server-owned. Follow the subscription Settings contract.

- Capability-9 API format generations follow `cmds-delidev-accounts-contract.md#connected-api-format-changes` after main reservation the originating change. Resolve immutable execution connection IDs against server-owned retained profiles, share the original protected key reference, and keep current validation separate. Preserve actor-bound atomic retries, all-generation confirmed cleanup, old-client protection and portable/restore exclusions. Ordered-route reconfiguration markers block new routing only. No SQLite migration or native change.

- `desktop-runtime.ts` owns Local transport proof. Validate the exact native origin, server ID, generation and private key before constructing transport; verify a bounded HMAC challenge without bearer before every Connect request. Keep proof material in memory, reject stale/foreign origins and preserve connection drafts across generation replacement. Saved transports retain their explicit addresses. Never log/persist proof keys.

- `execution-startup.tsx` owns closed startup-failure projection, corrective copy, eligibility and safe metadata copying under `cmds-delidev-execution-startup-contract.md`. It grants no native or RPC authority. SessionView uses the existing Info drawer and Resume mutation; explicit setup presents the original exact Runner controls locally; Runner Devices remains optional. Keep ordinary welcome free of prerequisites, unknown metadata unavailable, original recovery separate, and current keyboard/focus/responsive behavior intact. Pause borrowed Runner presentation when the owning session surface is inactive; retain its original controller. Positive no-send and confirmed cleanup proof remain required for startup retry.

- Repository verification rechecks observe the original local Worker proof and server status without automatic inspection, cloning or saving. Require the same previously verified machine, preserve folder/path/drafts, redact private native errors and fence callbacks to the active original Settings opening. Inline local connection help releases its presentation claim when the owning task becomes inactive; original controllers and admitted effects remain mounted.

- Screen shortcuts follow `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md#screen-shortcuts-and-help`. `shortcuts.ts` owns typed registration/matching and `shortcut-provider.tsx` owns connection-local keydown/keyup, blur/visibility listeners and read-only help. Keyboard Help retains its accepted original code (logical-key fallback) until release; blur/hiding/disposal retire held ownership. Early dismissal blocks reopening during the same press and later release cannot restore stale focus. The button retains persistent Help; effective committed bindings and locale changes preserve the original lifetime. Search has no global entry shortcut or primary+K guidance; retain sidebar Search entry, screen primary+I and native Enter search. Keep dispatch, help and aria-keyshortcuts derived from the same declarations; exclude hidden/inactive surfaces, IME/repeated/handled events, terminal passthrough (except the fixed `SessionCloseTab` and numeric tab actions) and visible modals (including compact navigation), except eligible non-input-target actions from the owned help dialog. Close help before an accepted callback and suppress opener restoration for action dismissal; Escape/Close retain restoration, and help never grants background input-target authority. Preserve existing form guards, native newline/search defaults, focus-local panel Escape, draft/reconnect lifetimes and the primary-key platform of the renderer. Do not log key events or content, persist bindings, add OS-global authority or use help rows as action launchers.

- Main-window local Worker controls observe native automatic registration/start/recovery; component mounts, polling and Settings navigation cannot initiate it. Preserve the metadata-only automatic presentation hint through category lifetime wrappers before the first native read. Render optional management metadata with explicit paused/blocked states, original-generation Stop retries and concrete inline permission/service/uncertain-exit guidance with the existing status recheck. Blocked Runner Devices opens a read-only Local Worker problem Modal over the same controller; opening/closing adds no reads or actions, and safe unknown-failure fallback, opener focus and category disposal remain mandatory. Connections keeps its stable category and persistent Connection controls, with localized information when native controls are unavailable; never mount Doctor there. Standalone Doctor retains its original query and report boundaries. Preserve saved/retained connection manual controls, machine IDs, readiness distinctions, localization and visit disposal.

- `agent-worker-wizard.tsx` and its stylesheet own the Harness card picker: Codex/Claude Code/OpenCode/Grok Build, 48px decorative official local images, 16px gaps, 24px padding, 176px minimum height and 8px corners. Preserve original colors, proportions and transparency with contain scaling; select supplied OpenCode/Grok variants through resolved `data-theme` and the initial OS fallback. Keep `public/harness-marks` notices/licenses separate from unchanged subscription assets. Use a button radiogroup with one Tab entry, wrapping arrows, Home/End, native Space/Enter and visible button focus; unknown saved values use the first card for validation focus. At available form widths below 640px stack the cards. Preserve supported/mutation guards and current-harness reselection: arrows/Home/End only select/focus, confirmation opens Accounts, Harness has no Next/form-submit advancement, and later steps retain Next. Only a changed harness clears source/accounts/model. Preserve the brand license/notices and other Settings ownership.

- Home New project/Create a project opens the existing Project editor directly over Sessions or New Session without selecting or mounting Settings. `project-creation.tsx` owns the independent scoped lifetime and mutation registry, original pending/uncertain task reopening, exact retries and active-query invalidation; App owns admission and disposal on another surface/conversation or connection identity. Preserve drafts, Home pages/filter/scroll, shared dialog geometry and visible opener/compact Home fallback focus. Keep Settings-internal creation unchanged and follow `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md#project-creation-outside-settings`.

- `language.tsx` and `language.css` own the Appearance language search combobox. Keep System pinned first and sort actual languages by stable English names; display English/native self-names independently of UI language. Search and keyboard navigation are local and never save; click/Enter confirms an existing enum, while cancellation, IME input and reselection cannot write. Preserve the device controller, revision/uncertainty locks, Settings disposal, mounted input focus and native interfaces. Use bundled catalog guidance, static semantic CSS and the shared input focus treatment under the localization contract.

- `sidebar.tsx` owns the session hover card content; `session-hover-card.tsx` owns its sidebar-local timers, single-card subscription and measured placement. Preserve the full name, separate workspace/execution/archive observations, safe title state/reason and complete accessible description from existing navigation metadata only. Use the approved 320px theme surface, 16px padding, 8px corners, neutral badges and no arrow/actions. Hover opens after 300ms, focus immediately, and source/card departure has a 150ms grace period. Escape suppresses reopening until a new entry; activation, external scrolling, resize, hidden/inactive navigation and source removal dispose presentation and pending timers. Card scrolling remains independent. Compact cards stay descendants of the open drawer and use the manual popover top layer to escape clipping without moving focus or changing modal authority. Keep listener ownership singular and row subscriptions boolean; add no RPC, durable state, logging of content or native execution authority. Follow the desktop and localization contracts.

- `repository-list.tsx` and its static stylesheet own only Repositories inventory presentation. Keep the shared Settings anchor, saved server order, complete wrapping IDs/paths and page-scoped counts. Keep 16px gaps between card border boxes within and across pagination pages through the outer list and measurable one-column payload-wrapper grids. Preserve wrapper measurement, eviction/restoration and focused-page protection; do not flatten wrappers or add double page-boundary margins. Source labels and GitHub configuration badges use saved metadata only; never expose raw remote URLs, infer permission or perform discovery. Keep explicit GitHub read controllers, original schema/action gates, edit/delete task ownership and Settings visit disposal unchanged. Successful initial empty, continuation empty and retained refresh failure remain separate; scope responsive/theme styles to the repository body.

- OAuth credential-runtime recovery uses typed closed causes and localized explicit server Stop/Start guidance. Preserve original receipt/callback clearing, read-only inspection and original cancellation authority; never render native error content or repeat authorization/exchange to repair code identity. Follow the desktop development-signing and credential contracts.

- `reasoning-effort-field.tsx` and its stylesheet own the shared Agent Reasoning effort/Subagent effort combobox. Keep harness hints advisory, exact direct input and omitted defaults unchanged, Codex child capability gates and inherited form locks intact, and keyboard/IME/accessibility state local to the editor. Opening/filtering/selecting hints performs no RPC or native discovery; follow the desktop contract.

- `pull-requests-layout.fixture.tsx` is an isolated synthetic browser entry for the real App/PR sidebar. Keep its fixed repository identities and read counters outside the product entry, use no native/account authority or external RPC, and retain normal connection/controller ownership. The script-owned layout check covers localized themes, responsive wrapping, disclosures and native keyboard behavior; it does not prove packaged CEF acceptance.

- Repository addition uses generated Connect Query profile/page reads and durable Clone jobs. Select profile/repository explicitly, clear the selected profile and repository page when outer profile pagination changes, retain an association only for the same GitHub identity, and discard scoped reads/exact uncertain presentation requests on dialog disposal. Failed Worker verification exposes the original paired proof/Status recheck and local connection controls without losing the selected folder or draft; a later different machine cannot inherit earlier proof. Fresh local proof/capability precedes Clone; the server alone completes registration. Show published paths after failure and retain existing-folder registration on older peers under the desktop/workspace/integration contracts.

- Transient in-app toasts are owned by `toast-notifications.tsx`, `toast-store.ts` and their static stylesheet under the desktop contract. Keep one provider per connection, viewport-only subscriptions, bounded FIFO retention, remaining-time pauses and disposal/late-publication guards. Preserve the approved webview-centered 80px placement, theme/CSP/accessibility behavior and Settings save authority. Jobs and uncertain results never imply immediate save completion; OS notifications and Inbox reservations retain their independent owners. Do not persist or log toast content.

- Add repository uses a native child dialog over the mounted Repositories inventory. Give each dialog its own Settings lifetime and mutation registry so Cancel, close and Escape discard drafts, scoped reads and exact pending presentation requests without canceling accepted business jobs. Preserve the connected Add repository opener and restore focus on dismissal. Keep 640px/24px dialog geometry and responsive scroll/actions scoped to repository registration; other dialogs retain their geometry. The atomic originating-Worker Clone action is available only before the repository name or optional settings are edited because its existing request cannot carry those fields; edited drafts must use Add repository.

- `repository-clone-fields.tsx` owns the pure URL/destination presentation and derived editable folder name. Its URL/path checks are advisory; preserve original submitted bytes for Go authority. Show existing-folder selection and Clone inputs together, preserve explicit folder-name edits and handle parent picker cancellation without Worker verification. Keep Clone disabled with update guidance until the negotiated server/Worker flow is available; a UI fixture grants no Clone capability.

- Shared and category-specific focus styles exclude every `input`, `textarea` and `select`, including checkboxes and radios, for both pointer and keyboard focus. Suppress browser focus rings while preserving ordinary control boundaries, static checkbox outlines, selected states, insertion carets, autofocus and keyboard behavior. Keep visible focus on buttons, navigation, disclosures and other focusable content; follow `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md`.

- `subscription-onboarding.tsx` and its stylesheet own the pure login-first account body under the subscription Settings contract. Supply confirmed progress from the owning controller; render performs no login, account creation or browser opening. Preserve once-only name focus, edited values, the UTF-8 name bound, existing Settings tokens and departure callbacks without business cancellation.

- Workspace storage and permanent deletion use the connection-owned controller in `session-storage.tsx`. Retain original requests and jobs through navigation/uncertainty, pin exact successful previews and snapshot selections for confirmation, observe deletion independently of removed resources and preserve decimal/nullable byte measurements. Use separate negotiated capabilities and follow `cmds-delidev-storage-contract.md`.

- New schedule creation presentation is owned by `src/schedule-creation.tsx` and `src/schedule-creation.css` (relative to `apps/delidev`) and follows the previous feature section in `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md`: creation-only Task/Execution/Repeat/Review wizard with a centered 720px column, noninteractive status indicator, step count and persistent footer and an unobscured main-content action row, mounted collapsed overrides, native radios, explicit catalog states and once-only name focus. Inactive authoring steps stay mounted/hidden/unfocusable and outside native validation, with inventory reads suspended but pagination retained. Next validates/focuses its first invalid control; Back and distinct Review Edit actions preserve drafts without saves. Only Review invokes the original create path after all-step validation/reveal, including collapsed invalid references. Preserve full exact identities, available labels, prompt/reference text, raw cron/timezone and paused/enabled state; review is configuration, not readiness. Lock all navigation while proof/save/uncertain and preserve exact retry. User step changes focus the heading without refetch/reconnect focus theft. Step/frequency/time/weekday/disclosure stay in connection memory, emit only canonical existing Cron fields, preserve raw Custom transitions and invalid Time drafts, and never replace server calendar authority. Preserve strict schema-v1 writes, limits, fresh Local proof, exact uncertain retry and all existing edit/list/detail/history/sidebar behavior. Keep native viewport/zoom evidence separate from component checks.

- Sidechat actions require negotiated server/native Worker support and a completed original parent. Retain creation/findings requests across navigation and uncertainty, offer complete own assistant replies from the selected answer generation only (superseded same-question retry answers remain read-only history) and transfer full selected content under exact revisions. Explain dependent permanent cleanup and keep workspace/terminal mutation outside Sidechat authority; follow `cmds-delidev-sidechat-contract.md`.

- Backup job observation uses owner/client `GetBackupCreation` and `GetBackupDeletion` independently of bounded history pages. Keep accepted IDs and exact revisions through navigation, refresh inventory after observed completion, and never replay a mutation to poll status. Follow `cmds-delidev-storage-contract.md`.

- Keep managed Backups in the full-window Settings System group and dispose its local workflow on category departure while accepted durable jobs continue. Ordinary session welcome has no prerequisite checklist; preserve Inbox and connection-memory drafts.

- New session is a mounted `Surface.NewSession` chat-first page. Keep the first message, execution selections, Options and exact uncertain create identity in connection memory across navigation, Settings and same-identity reconnect; clear them when connection identity changes. Preserve first-message autofocus and its insertion caret without a focus ring, and disable Project selection while Local proof or session creation is pending or uncertain. Gate creation on `AUTOMATIC_TITLES_V1`, omit `name`, and preserve backend title state and safe reason in session details and loaded sidebar rows. Follow `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md` and `cmds-delidev-session-titles-contract.md`.

- General Chat creation is `Surface.NewGeneralChat` with `NewSessionKind.GeneralChat`, entered through the 36px **New Chat** action (English; Korean remains **새 일반 대화**) below New session. Keep each controller mounted after first entry, separate drafts/options/budgets, activation counters, HTML IDs and retained mutation keys (`create-session`/`create-general-chat`). General Chat always submits projectless `general-chat` through the existing Session RPC with no Git/Local controls, references or credential proof. Preserve explicit Agent Worker/Runs on choices, automatic-title/execution gates, late-result navigation guards and English/Korean/theme behavior; ordinary Agent tools/permissions remain unchanged.

- Durable backup creation uses `SystemService.RequestBackup` and existing actor/server-bound jobs, with separate acceptance and publication. Keep original image/job IDs across client loss and restart, recheck the original actor, join maintenance before stopped logs, honor lock-wait cancellation, and let external deletion obligations win. The current protocol-2 reset retires synchronous `CreateBackup`; preserve its numeric ownership only and return Unsupported without fallback. CLI `backup create [--wait]` and desktop use durable status. Follow `cmds-delidev-storage-contract.md`.

- Managed backup deletion uses existing durable jobs/receipts and schema-24 indexing, plus immutable synchronized `backup-deletions/` intents outside SQLite before unlink. Bind fresh deletion confirmation to the exact inspection object, clear it on deactivation/refetch/replacement, and preserve already submitted uncertain request bytes independently. Preserve exact inspected revision/metadata/hash, original actor/request identity, startup obligation reconstruction, creation-replay suppression, bounded pending retries and source preservation on mismatch. Never evict deletion obligations or equate logical image bytes with reclaimed disk space; follow `cmds-delidev-storage-contract.md`.

- Optional diagnostics use authenticated status and explicitly requested doctor/configuration reads only; ordinary welcome and execution never mount the legacy checklist. Keep retained Worker handshakes, connected/enabled Workers, saved account health and Agent configuration as separate observations, never a combined execution-readiness grant. Validate the complete schema-v2 report, storage, credential and Worker shapes, required platform/version/time fields, four harness entries, closed states and protocol/problem relationships before accepting any report-derived observation. Reject foreign/malformed reports, preserve incomplete inventory and failed refresh states, and do not run discovery, login, provider validation or inference from the check.

- DeliDev managed backup operations follow `cmds-delidev-storage-contract.md`. Keep owner/client-only authorization, bounded metadata pagination, exact creation retries and source-preserving integrity inspection. Inspection must read an identity-checked private copy, reject sidecars/foreign server identity, recheck authorization after I/O and never imply restoration or credential/Worker recovery. Preserve exact byte counts and clear stale success after failed reinspection.

- Settings presentation follows `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md`: use the shared application-screen sidebar layout with 20 grouped categories (Tailscale is listed only in the original local desktop window) and mount only the selected category, with AI Subscription, AI API Keys, API Providers, Agent Workers and Instructions under AI; Project defaults, Projects, Repositories and Git Profiles under Coding; Runner Devices and Paired devices under Device management; and Appearance, Browser, Keyboard shortcuts, Server preferences, Connections, Notifications, Import / Export, Backups and App information under System. Keep responsive selection, mutation locks, empty/error/pagination distinctions, focus handling and exact draft/retry preservation within the active category. Ordinary entry starts at SubscriptionAccounts; Settings-internal New Project and explicit Repositories entries retain their destinations. Changing categories disposes category-local state; leaving Settings also disposes its selection, while page-level Escape preserves it. Disposal clears deferred entry markers, supported client waits and scoped query/mutation caches without save/replay, recovery UI, server/native cancellation or rollback. Guard late RPC/native callbacks and follow-up work, preserve sibling workflows and the shared QueryClient, and create a fresh un-aborted generation on Strict Mode replay. Retain the current opening across same-identity reconnects. Scope the presentation styles to Settings and leave all other modal geometry and native window behavior unchanged.

- The Schedules pane uses a Schedules-only root class, horizontal All schedules/Enabled/Paused segments, an All projects empty selector choice, Saved schedules with icon-and-text Refresh and wrapped complete UTC rows. The feature removes the sidebar Retained history lookup and its hidden DOM, state, focus targets and standalone destination without a spacer or replacement. Preserve bounded detail occurrence history and original-session navigation after confirmed configuration deletion, independent cursors, connection-memory filters/selection and protected replacement locks. Sidebar refresh and filters cannot request occurrence history. ResourceChoice emptyLabel defaults remain exact for every other caller. Keep shared rail/pane/footer/drawer geometry, CSP and server/mutation/retention authority unchanged; follow `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md`.

- Agent Workers alone follows the desktop contract's centered 1040px column, exact title/summary/scope and success-only empty-panel copy, below-1100px toolbar exception and divided rows with inert safe identity labels and name-scoped actions. Keep schema gates and the common Settings-opening disposal/late-continuation policy; the category may share exact Model metadata reads solely for ordered row summaries. Use one four-slot queue across all mounted pages, deduplicate within the opening, read additional routes only when expanded and retain only bounded native ID/name projections for mounted requested references. Collapse or unmount releases unshared queued work and projections. Validate original requested ID/kind/schema/positive revision and native identity; unavailable first metadata never substitutes another route. Explicit Refresh settings renews displayed summaries; pause/disposal cancels reads and fences late results. Unsupported Agent schemas read nothing. Presentation creates no mutation, polling or execution eligibility.

- Unsupported-schema Agent name/alias projection enforces the existing 256-byte UTF-8 Agent name limit before reuse in headings or accessible labels. Check code-unit length before encoding; oversized values retain Unnamed and disabled actions with the original full resource ID. Never truncate a name into a different actionable identity.

- Settings > Projects follows the shared the feature 1040px category column, semantic theme, 40px controls and 8px radii, superseding the previous feature presentation exception. Retain grouped project rows and the four mounted General/Repositories/Execution/Access tabs for edits, styled by the shared tab strip presentation. Keep exact empty-state text exclusive to a successful final empty first page; preserve server order, complete wrapped identities, pagination, cached refresh results, typed failures and original creation gates. Existing edits preserve every field/help string and explicit primary selection. New Project defaults the primary only when its ordered repository selection changes from empty to nonempty; preserve valid automatic/manual choices through additions and reorder, and require manual correction after removal while survivors remain. Preserve configured-empty restrictions, document bounds, revision guards, mutation locks and immutable retries. Use static scoped CSS with AA text/control/focus contrast; retain the shared application sidebar, other category appearance and discard-on-close semantics. Browser/component evidence cannot establish native desktop keyboard/geometry acceptance.

- Sidebar Inbox/Search actions render only on Sessions (welcome/detail), NewSession and NewGeneralChat, independent of read state. Other surfaces contain no header action group. Preserve the static left-aligned heading, 32px Home header/targets, 16px decorative icons, existing styling/rail/pane geometry and mounted connection state. Only header-origin navigation consumes a pending destination in a synchronous parent layout effect after destination commit/drawer close: focus main with preventScroll on wide viewports and the persistent destination opener below 760px, checking the current media query. Preserve Search first-entry autofocus, discard superseded/Settings intent and never schedule a competing focus frame or change tray/notification focus. Follow `apps-delidev-desktop-contract.md`.

- Agent Worker create/edit presentation is owned by `agent-configuration.tsx` and its scoped stylesheet for this feature. Keep the max-800px Core panel, always-visible permissions, four independently collapsed optional disclosures, truthful read/problem summaries and Name/Model-only required markers. Disclosure toggles keep children/queries/cursors mounted without RPCs; invalid hidden controls reveal their section before focus. Preserve complete documents, unknown options, ordering and original revision/request bytes. Settings disposal still clears every editor/disclosure/retry under ; accountless configuration is saveable and never proves execution readiness. Leave other Settings forms and native geometry unchanged.

- Every desktop destination has its own context pane. Search keeps drafts separate from applied requests and submits explicitly. Inbox uses one applied filter state, accepts exact Project/Session selections immediately without cascading, and remounts only its selectors across Reset to fence earlier callbacks. Preserve its compact drawer/focus and independent detail/response owners. Schedule list filters apply immediately, and an editor/confirmation/in-flight/uncertain operation protects the current schedule workflow from sidebar replacement while global navigation remains available. Inbox response drafts and notification activation retain their inbox-specific source/revision guards.

- Pull requests is a standalone surface. Selecting an exact repository automatically reads page one only after its current metadata validates the supported schema, profile and mapping. State/page size apply immediately; valid trimmed search applies after a 300 ms IME-aware debounce. Same selection, equivalent terms, Details, locale and layout changes do not reload. Invalid search cancels pending application. Automatic activation preserves drawer/focus. Detail, observation, refresh and existing history actions retain their original scope. Repositories Settings owns saved configuration/management and its separate deferred entry, with no GitHub content browser or automatic content reads. Preserve shared strict decoding, standalone PR observation/history/disposal, session associations, profile registration and the repository registration chooser. Leaving Pull requests cancels and drops disposable reads; connection-scoped pending PR operations remain visible with their exact retry identity before the automatic return read. Do not aggregate repositories or add query syntax, writes, or execution capabilities.

- Pull requests sidebar presentation follows the desktop contract and the approved name-only redesign of the feature's presentation. Apply only an active `Surface.PullRequests` root style scope without remounting controllers or query owners. Keep existing rail/pane/drawer geometry and independent list scrolling above normal bottom padding. Repository rows show the decorative glyph and name with separate selection and Details buttons. One connection-memory UUID controls the expanded Details region; show only the already-loaded configured GitHub owner/name there and never display or announce the internal local UUID, with no selection, extra read, raw URL/path or persistence on expansion. Use original-name accessible labels with stable presentation numbers for equal names, and retain page-scoped empty states and divided Query options that end after PR page size without automatic-load helper copy. State uses native Open/Closed/All radios with neutral segments and a surface-colored selected segment; omit the Load button. Preserve the 17/13/12px hierarchy, 16px horizontal inset, 8px corners, pale-blue row selection, 40px minimum row/control targets and independent Connections control geometry. Preserve task/recovery dialog geometry and ownership, including inside the outer drawer dialog. Preserve neighboring visibility contracts, exact pending identities and the current Settings opening lifecycle; never restore closed Settings-local drafts.
