The feature changes navigation and supersedes the modality from while retaining the disposal safeguards. Changing categories unmounts the category-owned tree and discards filters/cursors, details, editors, wizard steps, drafts, confirmations, secrets/disclosures, pending category entry, pending client waits and uncertain retry presentation. Leaving Settings also discards category selection. It never restores a former modal opener. There is no discard confirmation, recovery banner, implicit save, abandoned replay, server/native cancellation or rollback. The device-owned Appearance controller remains above connection state; its committed selection and pending native saves survive Settings presentation disposal and connection changes. Persisted settings, accepted server/native effects and receipts, authorization, selected conversation/composer, New session drafts and sibling workflows remain authoritative and intact.

Each selected category owns a fresh mounted component tree, mutation registry and authenticated transport wrapper. Supported RPC requests receive a linked category abort signal; disposal rejects late outcomes and blocks follow-up RPC/native work even when the underlying operation ignores cancellation. Native Worker and notification permission completions cannot update a replacement category. Keep the connection QueryClient and successful-save invalidation; cancel/remove only queries keyed by the disposed transport or category and remove its tagged mutation cache entries. Same-identity reconnects retain the current editor and route subsequent requests through the replacement authenticated transport. Strict Mode setup/cleanup replay creates a fresh un-aborted generation before mounting its readers. Fresh reads may reveal committed changes or pending server jobs; this is authoritative state, never restoration of an abandoned workflow. The feature presents the persistent desktop controllers inline in Connections. Leaving Settings or moving their views to an owning failure flow retains their original lifecycle, registration, saved-profile and updater requests, drafts and confirmations.

Menu selection lives outside the category lifetime. Only the selected category body mounts. Settings-internal New Project, explicit Repositories entry and API Providers account management/creation use one transition path; non-secret typed entry information initializes the target once. OAuth begins only after the target category lifetime mounts. Category departure disposes local native callback/listener authority without business cancellation, automatic completion, save or replay. Returning reads current server state and never restores abandoned input, confirmations, filters or uncertain retries.

Every category has one visible category title and its existing scope/help description above its content. Configuration list toolbars keep Refresh settings and any eligible existing New action together at the upper right; detailed editors retain their existing explicit save/cancel/back actions. Devices and Runner Devices do not gain a generic create action, and Project defaults remains the revision-bound policy singleton. Server preferences owns only independent Network operations without policy reads, editor or Save/Discard. API Providers keeps the capability-gated Custom provider action and its successful final-first-page custom-provider empty region. Initial loading and initial read errors do not render successful emptiness or grant new create eligibility. A cached result remains visible during refresh; a refresh error shows its sanitized correlated failure and a stale-results notice. Pagination is hidden only for a successful empty first page with no continuation token; an empty later page still offers First page. Query staleness alone is not a read failure.

The former Models Settings category and independent model editor are removed.
The Agent Worker wizard owns model selection; Usage owns model details and Token
pricing. CLI/RPC model configuration remains compatible. Internal canonical
models retain their original IDs, discovery provenance, display settings and
historical attribution. Source-scoped server catalog queries supply autocomplete.

### Agent Worker wizard

Creation and editing use the same four steps: Harness, Accounts, Model, Configure.
Fill existing values on edit. Stage navigation never saves. Choose a supported
harness, then ordered subscription service/API provider groups, each with at least
one same-source account. Keep their explicit order and relative
weights (1–1,000), all six routing policies and the inherited server default.
Fixed routing permits exactly one account per group. A source change clears only
that group's model/accounts; a harness change clears incompatible groups. Both
require explicit selection; ordinary Back
and disclosure changes retain values. Legacy accountless Workers remain readable
through existing APIs, but need an account before wizard resaving. Retired models
remain inert; affected Workers require explicit current account and model
reconfiguration without rewriting historical executions.

#### Worker wizard step indicator

The four-item step indicator (Harness, Accounts, Model, Configure) is also
navigation among steps the user has already reached. The wizard keeps one
`visited` limit, the highest step reached in the current opened wizard session.
It starts at Harness (an edit also starts there and reaches later steps through
Next), only grows when a step is selected, and is never persisted or saved.

- A visited or current item is one `button type=button` holding the number and
  label together, with a 36px minimum hit area, a pale selected-surface hover and
  a visible `focus-visible` ring. The current item's button carries
  `aria-current="step"`. Items after the visited limit are plain non-focusable
  content with no hover or focus affordance.
- Selection never saves, submits the form or starts login, connection
  verification, endpoint model discovery or inference work. It starts only the
  read-only reads that reaching the target step with footer Back or Next starts
  (see the read table below), and nothing for a step it jumps over.
  Back/Next, harness confirmation, the final Save and Settings dismissal are
  unchanged.
- English and Korean labels, the four-item layout and wrapping on narrow widths
  are unchanged. The styles are scoped to `.worker-steps`; other wizards keep
  the shared `wizard-progress` presentation.

Atomic step labels. Each step's number and label form one unbreakable group.
The label is `white-space: nowrap` and never breaks inside a word, for example
Harness or Accounts in English and the equivalent Korean labels. When the
available width cannot hold all four groups on one row, whole groups wrap to the
next row in source order (the strip is `flex-wrap: wrap`) and no label is
hidden, truncated or clipped, and the page or dialog gains no horizontal
overflow. The shared control rules of every host (wizard, Settings task dialog,
Settings page) cap a button at `max-width: 100%` of its list item at different
selector specificities. That cap excludes the 16px of padding the negative
margins give back, which squeezed the label and let it break inside words. The
step button therefore declares `min-width: max-content`, which overrides the cap
in every host without an `!important` or a change to shared control sizing; the
28px circle, 14px/20px label, 8px number-to-label gap, 24px group gap and the
thin divider are unchanged.

`scripts/test-worker-steps-layout.mjs` (`pnpm test:worker-steps-layout`) mounts
the committed stylesheets and step markup in a Settings task dialog host and a
Settings page host with a host-supplied Playwright/Chrome
(`DELIDEV_QA_PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE`, optional `DELIDEV_QA_BROWSER_CHANNEL`). It
measures real line boxes in English and Korean, light and dark: every
current/visited combination at the 720px wizard bound stays on one row with
one-line labels and 28px circles; viewports of 320, 640, 641, 760 and 761px at
100% and effective 200% zoom, plus a 1px sweep across the wrapped-row boundary,
keep groups whole and ordered with no overlapping hit targets or horizontal
overflow; the focus ring, hover surface, `aria-current="step"` and non-focusable
future steps are unchanged. Effective 200% zoom uses the halved CSS viewport and
skips only the 320px case (160 CSS px, below the 960px native window minimum).
It is a synthetic browser fixture outside `pnpm test` and CI; it does not
establish mounted-app, actual browser zoom or packaged CEF acceptance.

Step strip hit areas. The strip never lets two adjacent step hit areas overlap,
so the visible edge of a step always activates that step. Step spacing is owned
by the shared `wizard-progress` rule (24px between steps at every width) and the
worker stylesheet declares no gap, because the shared rule's higher specificity
would silently override one. Each button reaches 8px past its item on both
sides horizontally and 4px vertically, and keeps a 36px minimum height. Overlap
is the facing reaches minus the gap; a negative value is the clearance left
between the hit areas.

| Viewport width  | Placement              | Gap  | Reach of each facing pair | Overlap | Minimum hit height |
| --------------- | ---------------------- | ---- | ------------------------- | ------- | ------------------ |
| 761px and wider | Same row               | 24px | 8px + 8px                 | -8px    | 36px               |
| 761px and wider | Wrapped onto a new row | 24px | 4px + 4px                 | -16px   | 36px               |
| 641px to 760px  | Same row               | 24px | 8px + 8px                 | -8px    | 36px               |
| 641px to 760px  | Wrapped onto a new row | 24px | 4px + 4px                 | -16px   | 36px               |
| 640px and below | Same row               | 24px | 8px + 8px                 | -8px    | 36px               |
| 640px and below | Wrapped onto a new row | 24px | 4px + 4px                 | -16px   | 36px               |

`step-hit-area-css.test.ts` evaluates the committed stylesheets (media
conditions, specificity and load order) at every width threshold and fails when
any row's overlap is zero or positive, when the worker sheet declares a gap on
the strip, or when a rule the evaluator skips targets the strip. Other control
strips keep adjacent targets non-overlapping the same way: the shared tab strip
has no gap and no negative margins, and the only other negative inline margin
in the desktop stylesheets is the sole dismiss button of an inline error row,
which has no neighbouring control. The same test fails on any new negative
inline margin or pseudo-element offset until it is documented there.

| Target item                                     | Wizard state                                                              | Result                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| After the visited limit                         | any                                                                       | Not a button, not focusable, click does nothing.                                                                                                      |
| Any item                                        | pending save, uncertain save, pending account evidence or inactive wizard | Button is disabled; no step change, no second write.                                                                                                  |
| Current step                                    | idle                                                                      | Enabled. Focuses the step heading; no entrance motion; drafts and any shown error stay.                                                               |
| Before the current step                         | idle                                                                      | Enabled. Selects it with the entrance motion, focuses the heading, clears the error and retains compatible drafts.                                    |
| After the current step, up to the visited limit | idle, preceding stages valid                                              | Enabled. Selects it with the entrance motion and focuses the heading.                                                                                 |
| After the current step, up to the visited limit | idle, a preceding stage invalid                                           | Enabled. Does not select the target: it shows the first invalid stage without entrance motion, shows its error and focuses the first invalid control. |

Read table. A step's reads belong to arriving at that step, whichever control
caused the arrival, so selecting an item and pressing footer Back or Next start
the same requests. Leaving Accounts discards its pages and inventory can change
while another step is shown, so Accounts is read again on every arrival instead
of reusing retained rows. A step the selection jumps over starts no read.

| Target item                             | Earlier state of the target's data                                                              | Requests started by the selection                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Harness                                 | any                                                                                             | None.                                                                                                                      |
| Current step or an item after the limit | any                                                                                             | None.                                                                                                                      |
| Accounts, from Model or Configure       | pages loaded, or the last read failed                                                           | One provider inventory read per source group and one account read per source group that has a source, as Back starts them. |
| Model, API source                       | any                                                                                             | None. Endpoint models are read only by the explicit Refresh models from endpoint action.                                   |
| Model, subscription source              | known catalog loaded and fresh in the shared query cache                                        | None.                                                                                                                      |
| Model, subscription source              | known catalog not loaded, stale (older than the cache freshness window) or its last read failed | One known catalog read for that source, as Next starts it.                                                                 |
| Configure                               | any                                                                                             | The one Configure field read that Next starts. No Accounts or Model read and no save.                                      |
| Any item blocked by forward validation  | any                                                                                             | Those of the first invalid stage it routes to, from the rows above.                                                        |
| Any item while disabled                 | pending save, uncertain save, pending evidence, inactive wizard                                 | None.                                                                                                                      |

`agent-worker-wizard.test.tsx` records every request through the transport and
covers each row, including a multi-source draft, a failed earlier read and equality
with the Back/Next arrival.

Clamping: choosing a different harness clamps the limit to Harness (confirming
then reopens Accounts). Committing a different source for a group, or adding a
source group, clamps it to Accounts, so Model and Configure become inactive until
reached again with Next. Reselecting the same harness or source, reordering,
removing a group and editing accounts, the model or the name keep the limit;
the forward validation above covers those drafts. `agent-worker-wizard.test.tsx`
covers every row and clamp, and `agent-worker-wizard-steps-css.test.ts` covers the
markup-dependent geometry, hover and focus rules.

The Model step uses source-scoped server catalog autocomplete and permits exact
native ID input after loading, empty, failed or unsupported discovery results.
Both wizard generations reserve an always-mounted 280 CSS-pixel result area
beneath each model input. Keep suggestions, initial/additional/loading/error/empty
and catalog-result messages inside its bounded scroll owner even while the
suggestion list is closed. At fixed viewport and body scroll, result transitions
must keep the dialog, model input, Reload, footer and later source inputs within
one CSS pixel. Keyboard highlighting scrolls only this result area, including
options nested in retained payload pages; focus within it retains the popup.
Closed/hidden/inert ancestors never admit continuation reads. Preserve original
source, query, account/model revision, drafts, exact-ID, retry and mutation
ownership. Shared dialog sizing and other steps remain unchanged.
`scripts/test-worker-model-layout.mjs` owns the bounded synthetic geometry
fixture with committed product styles and host-supplied Playwright. Component
checks retain real catalog/query/pagination adapters; synthetic browser evidence
grants no packaged CEF or installed-platform acceptance.
Typing never contacts a provider endpoint. Endpoint refresh uses the deliberate
existing discovery RPC and original account revision. Codex native observation
retains explicit selected-account/Runner Device/installation scope, accepted jobs,
immutable pages and original uncertain retries. Subscription native model lookup
remains unsupported. Connection and saved health observations remain separate
from execution eligibility; mount, navigation and save never start login,
connection, validation or inference. Saving declares configured harness/model
compatibility; execution still rechecks current authority and native support.

Configure retains name, permission, reasoning, instructions and native options,
including mounted collapsed values, and reviews every ordered source/model/account group.
The single-source wizard retains capability 33 compatibility. Capability 36 enables
ordered source groups with Add/Remove and keyboard-operable Move up/down controls.
Accounts retains server-filtered per-source pagination, routing policies and weights;
Model displays the same group order with a source-scoped autocomplete/exact ID for
each. Both wizard generations retain English/Korean presentation and the independent
capability-35 known-model catalog. Known candidates remain advisory, while saved
models retain exact revisions and take precedence over duplicate known IDs after
all saved pages are read. New account choices require a connected Ready or
Unverified account; retained selections stay visible independently of that filter. New groups default to Priority. Configure saves all typed model choices and
the Worker once under the original revision and UUID-v7 receipt. Schema-3 editors
require capability 36; unsupported servers show update guidance. Stage navigation
never starts login, validation, discovery or inference. New sessions advance only
after complete confirmed quota exhaustion; observed recovery restores preference
for future sessions. Existing executed sessions keep their original selection.
Keep exact uncertain request bytes, current-revision conflicts, visit disposal,
late-response fencing and same-identity reconnect/Strict Mode behavior.

Use the shared 1040px left column and 960px workflow task shell with fixed header/footer, flat rows/dividers, semantic themes, 40px controls and 8px corners. Harness, Model and Configure retain the 720px form cap. Accounts uses the available body width. Accounts presents one vertical ordered list of inline source accordions at every width; no detached source list, detail panel or repeated source heading remains. Each source is a bordered 8px-corner card whose header shows a separate reorder grip, the one-based position, the source name (or "Choose account source"), the selected-account count and a disclosure chevron (down when collapsed, up when expanded). Existing semantic light/dark tokens apply: dividers use the border token and the expanded header uses the selected-surface tokens. Long names wrap without covering the grip or chevron and controls fit narrow widths without horizontal scrolling. Only the shared task body scrolls. The header uses the shared `DisclosureButton`/`DisclosureContent` primitives. The grip and the trigger are sibling controls; a grip or Remove is never nested in the trigger. The trigger exposes `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` and supports Enter/Space with visible focus. The source picker, account rows, current provider/account failure, retry, stale/invalid/empty/loading presentation, routing and weight/order controls and Remove live in the expanded card body; Remove is disabled for the last group. Add account source sits below the list.

Disclosure state is a single expanded source key owned by the wizard. On first Accounts entry the first group is expanded. Opening another group closes the previous one, and activating the expanded header closes it so every group may be collapsed. Returning to Accounts keeps the disclosure choice (including all-collapsed) while that group still exists; changing the harness resets it. Disclosure never changes drafts. Add appends an empty group, expands it and focuses its source picker. Removing the expanded group expands and focuses the next remaining position's trigger, or the preceding final group's trigger. Validation (Next, a visited forward step or save) expands the first invalid source before focusing its invalid control and never saves. The Model step is unchanged: it renders the same mounted source groups with their model editors and plain headings, without accordion controls or grips.

Keep stable-key group controllers and route identities mounted while collapsed, including their cursors and routing controls. Collapsed bodies are hidden and absent from keyboard and accessibility interaction and run no visible-only continuation; first-page reads for every group still start on Accounts entry. Separate always-visible grips in each header preview source order without changing draft objects, the expanded identity or reads; the list shows live positions while moving. Pointer movement hit-tests card headers only (the insertion index counts the other headers the pointer has passed, by header midpoint) and the moving source's body is collapsed while it moves, so an expanded body never stretches a slot or makes the grip appear stuck. Pointer drop or Space/Enter commits once and retains grip focus and the expanded group; a collapsed-all list stays collapsed. Arrow keys preview and Escape cancels movement before dialog dismissal. Pointer cancellation, lost capture, step/category departure, hidden/inert/disposed openings, connection replacement and membership/order changes cancel without saving. Singleton and pending/uncertain grips remain visible but disabled. `WorkerSourceOrder` owns the ordered list element, the movement state machine and the announcement region, and renders each item's card around the grip it supplies. Do not sort by source type.

Selected account rows lead eligible choices and remain visible outside current pages. Failed-read display retention keeps only selected identity/name/status metadata; current independent reads remain the only account proof, and complete visited Resource documents are never retained for labels. The source picker is always visible; only a committed different source resets that group's accounts/model/cursors. Account choices are directly available without Choose accounts. Required selected-provider failures and their exact read-only retry remain visible in the expanded card beside the source picker. Retry reads that provider without changing the source, account selection or draft, and admits no mutation. Remove Change source, Refresh accounts and source Move up/down buttons. Preserve exact explicit failed-read retry/reload, complete server filtering, invalid/stale/empty states and selected-account counts. Routing stays visible with an empty helper and all original account weight/order controls. Only a complete valid exhausted empty inventory shows Add account in AI API Keys for its selected provider, or Add account in AI Subscription for its selected service. These links use ordinary Settings navigation, dispose the wizard draft and start no login, discovery, save or native operation. Partial, failed, incompatible, malformed or hidden-only nonempty pages never establish empty inventory. Pagination follows the shared continuation contract and never changes account authority. Validation expands the affected source and reveals/focuses its invalid control. Collapsed bodies expose no keyboard/accessibility controls. Language changes and reflow never remount controllers or steal focus.

Both wizard generations place Back/Next/final Save in the Settings task footer, associated with the original form. The header owns the create/edit title and top-level dismissal; omit duplicate title and Cancel in a task, retaining standalone page cancellation. Harness has no Next action. X/Escape and original opener restoration retain their existing ownership. The Accounts step shows the selected harness name as plain text without a change control; footer Back and the visited Harness stepper item are the routes back to Harness. Either focuses the step heading, confirming the same harness returns to Accounts with the draft kept, and choosing a different harness applies the harness-change reset above.

The Harness step replaces its select with
four equal selectable cards in Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Grok Build order.
Show their decorative 48px local brand marks, 16px names and 12px origin labels
OpenAI, Anthropic, Open source and xAI. Use 16px grid gaps, 24px card padding,
176px minimum card height and 8px corners. Two columns fit at available form
widths of at least 640px; below that width use one column. The selected card uses
the semantic selected background, accent border and a checked circular indicator;
unselected cards use the ordinary surface, border and empty circular indicator.
Keep the existing Harness heading/helper and footer guidance. Cards use a
button-based single-selection radiogroup with one selected Tab entry, wrapping
Arrow Up/Down/Left/Right selection, Home/End and native Space/Enter activation.
With an unsupported saved harness, select no card and use the first card as the
Tab entry and validation focus target. Preserve the new Codex default and saved
edit selection. Arrows and Home/End only change selection/focus; click or native
Space/Enter confirmation opens Accounts and focuses its heading, including
current-card reselection. Harness has no Next button or form-submit advancement.
Reselecting the current harness preserves account/model choices, while an actual
change retains the existing explicit reset. Later steps retain Next. Buttons
retain visible keyboard focus
and disabled server-support/mutation guards. Harness cards contain decorative
official local images in the existing 48px boxes, preserving original colors,
proportions and transparency without network access, inline styles or additional
dependencies. OpenCode and Grok use the supplied light/dark variants selected by
the resolved `data-theme`, with the OS color scheme as the first-paint fallback
before that attribute exists. Keep these assets and their source/version/hash,
usage conditions and separate license in `public/harness-marks`; retain the
subscription provider assets and notices independently. Follow the repository
license contract for vendor trademark conditions and distribution notices.
Input/select focus preserves ordinary
boundaries; buttons/disclosures retain visible focus. The combobox supports
Arrow Up/Down, Enter and Escape with active-descendant semantics. Stage changes
focus their heading; invalid configuration returns to its stage and input. Narrow
windows use one column and compact stage labels. Footer Cancel/Back/Next and the
final Save remain in normal document flow. Verify 1280×800, 960×640, 640×480,
effective zoom and light/dark browser fixtures separately from actual browser
zoom, packaged native platforms and real-account acceptance. Usage model details
provide current revision-bound Token pricing, including models without usage;
retired historical model attribution remains read-only.

Agent Workers uses the shared left-aligned `width: 100%`, `max-width: 1040px` column inside the shared 32px/24px/16px content padding. Its single 26px title is followed by the 14px summary **Reusable configurations for your agents.** and 12px scope **Saved on the selected server.** Keep Refresh settings and the single eligible **+ New Agent Worker** action together at the upper right in list mode, hiding that toolbar during existing parent workflows. Below 1100 CSS pixels, the Agent toolbar moves below the title; every category uses this shared toolbar breakpoint. A subtle divider ends the heading, with content 24px below it. Controls retain 40px minimum height, 8px corners and visible focus.

After a successful empty first page without a continuation token, Agent Workers shows one semantic-themed region with thin neutral rules and 160px minimum height. Place a decorative, accessibility-hidden 32px outline icon at the left, with the 16px heading **No agent workers yet**, and 14px copy **Define a harness, model, accounts, and instructions, then reuse them in new sessions.** No second creation action appears in this panel. Loading, initial permission/read errors and failed cached-empty refreshes never satisfy that success-only predicate. Empty continuation or later pages preserve accepted rows and distinguish reached-range emptiness from complete exhaustion. Shared continuation retains the original kind, page size and opaque server tokens.

Loaded Agent configurations occupy one flat list with divided rows. Preserve exact inert names and safe original-ID presentation labels, existing Status text and a visible harness product name. Known harnesses reuse the licensed decorative 32px marks from the wizard; unknown harnesses have plain text without a mark. No health, readiness or execution eligibility is inferred. Supported legacy configurations show their configured model; schema-3 source routes show the first saved model and a localized `+N more` disclosure. Expansion preserves every saved route in numbered order, including repeated model references. Show exact validated native IDs as neutral chips and distinct model display names as supporting text. Keep 40px disclosure controls, visible keyboard focus, semantic themes and wrapping actions below 640px available row width. One category-owned four-slot reader serves all mounted payload pages with exact Model requests, opening-local deduplication and bounded native-ID/name projections retained only for mounted requested references across the three 50-item payload pages. Read the first route only until expansion; never enumerate models or read accounts. Require requested ID, Model kind, supported schema, positive revision and readable native ID/name within their 256-byte limits. Missing, denied, malformed and unsupported responses show localized unavailable metadata without substituting a later model or altering actions. Additional routes read only while expanded; collapse or unmount removes their unshared queued work and retained projections. Only the explicit header Refresh settings action renews settled displayed metadata, without independent polling. Ordinary inventory refetch, Close/Cancel and accepted task completion retain settled model projections and failed-first unavailability; changed mounted model references receive their own exact reads. Suspension, disposal, replacement identity and late responses retain the common opening cancellation fences; same-identity reconnect preserves its owner. Unsupported Agent schemas trigger zero model reads. Unsupported schemas expose only inert name/alias text within the existing 256-byte UTF-8 Agent name limit and safe identity labels; oversized projected names retain the Unnamed fallback, and all existing unsupported-schema action gates remain enforced. Check code-unit length before allocating a UTF-8 validation buffer. Visible actions appear in Edit, Preview routing, Delete order; each accessible action name includes the configuration name. Rows, long text and controls wrap without clipping. Use the creation/edit wizard above, existing read-only routing and explicit revision-bound deletion confirmation, ordered account/template/options validation and exact uncertain requests. Reflow and same-identity reconnect retain these only within the same visit. The common disposal/default-category policy above remains authoritative for navigation away, including late outcomes and already accepted server effects.

Agent Worker configured-model metadata shares four category-owned transport permits across all mounted pages and response generations. A started original read holds its permit until its transport await settles, including abort-ignoring reads after Refresh or disposal. Same-identity authentication transport replacement retains the original category reader, accepted projections and unsettled reads; later explicit reads use the replacement transport. Identity replacement retains its independent disposal boundary. Remove obsolete queued references before dispatch and retain the existing late-publication fences.

Git Profiles uses the approved the feature content hierarchy within this shell. Its description is “Manage GitHub profiles for repository access. AI accounts are configured separately.” One left-aligned GitHub panel, at most 1040 CSS pixels wide, contains the provider heading, Refresh, bounded profile rows and exactly one New GitHub profile action. Keep that action in the category header; a successful empty first page without a continuation or read failure shows first-profile guidance with three static informational steps and no second action. Loading, initial failure, cached refresh/failure and empty continuation/later pages remain distinct; create keeps its original eligibility before read success and paging keeps its original opaque cursor and 50-resource size.

Rows and Manage display Token storage and Identity validation separately, including pending denial, unsupported versions, unknown observations and original check time/identity when provided. Neither identity verification nor token storage claims repository capability. Create/rename forms are bounded to720 CSS pixels, focus the name only on first visible entry, and keep token type/owner immutable after creation. Manage separates explicit token connection, identity validation and confirmed deletion. Its empty password field disables submission and never reveals stored tokens. Full official-form guidance remains mounted inside a native disclosure; toggling alone cannot query or open a form. Existing exact uncertain identities, decimal revisions, PAT clearing and operation guards and the common Settings visit lifecycle remain authoritative. See the [integration contract](cmds-delidev-integrations-contract.md) for authority and operation ordering.

Settings-specific colors and system fonts are scoped to this Settings screen and remain CSP-compatible: white content, pale-gray navigation, 8px control radii, flat empty regions, 40px minimum controls, decorative outline icons and non-color selected-state semantics. Do not add a route, native window, dependency, external asset, inline-style exception, public API, persisted schema, storage, authorization, credential, polling or migration change. Component tests do not establish native geometry or keyboard containment; record native desktop smoke evidence separately, including platform and viewport, and report unsupported/unavailable platforms without claiming acceptance.

#### Device appearance

Appearance is the first category in the System group, with the scope description
“Saved on this computer.” Existing category IDs/order, the ordinary AI Subscription
entry and Settings-internal New Project and targeted Repositories entries remain unchanged. The desktop
shared context pane and compact navigation drawer expose the same category. Theme is a native
radio group with System, Light and Dark; System is the fresh-install default.
Selection saves automatically, with pending and visible failure states and no Save
button. System observes `prefers-color-scheme` changes while running; explicit Light
and Dark ignore later OS changes.

`appearance.tsx` mounts above local/saved connection application state. Appearance
changes update static root selectors without remounting sessions, composer drafts,
Settings openings or other workflows. Leaving Settings disposes its visit as
before while the device controller and already submitted appearance save remain
alive. This preference is shared by every live local/saved-server window and loaded
by newly opened windows, independent of selected server or connectivity.

Native owns bounded, strictly validated `appearance.json` in `app_config_dir`,
using version 2 with the complete mode and preference snapshot, bounded to 256 KiB.
Valid version-1 mode documents retain compatibility defaults and upgrade only on
a successful explicit user change. It contains no
server identifier, secret or conversation content. Custom names and colors are
device preference metadata. It stays outside server configuration,
pairing, backups and configuration transfer. The narrow `read_appearance` and
`update_appearance` commands authorize the trusted `main` or registered `server-*`
document using the existing URL/binding checks; no generic path/filesystem or
Connect/protobuf capability is introduced. URL checks and disk I/O stay off CEF's
UI loop. One native process store serializes reads/atomic writes; update checks
the expected process revision and reinspects the stored document before replacement.
Writes synchronize a same-directory temporary file before atomic replacement, then
synchronize the Unix parent directory or use Windows write-through replacement.
Committed changes emit `appearance-changed` only to authorized live webviews.
Snapshots have non-wrapping unsigned process revisions; delayed reads, replies and
events cannot restore older state. Equal unchanged inspections retain the revision.
Brief saved-window binding contention receives bounded event-admission retries.
A healthy retained window reinspects when focused or made visible to reconcile a
missed event; an error or uncertain save still requires explicit Reload appearance.
The failure text and the Reload action live only in the Appearance settings
category. The provider renders no window-level alert, so the product window
reserves no space for an Appearance problem. The same rule applies to the Language
provider: its failure text and Reload action live only in the Language settings.

The original native controller inspects `appearance.json` once during startup
setup, before any product window or the tray is created or admitted, using the
same read semantics as `read_appearance` (missing file: System and default
palette; invalid, newer, linked or unreadable file: default presentation, the
problem recorded and no write authority). The auxiliary tray view never
inspects the file. `read_tray_status` projects only that retained snapshot and
fails with `StorageUnavailable` when the store has never been inspected (process
revision 0), so placeholder defaults are never reported as a saved palette. The
first product read of an unchanged document keeps the startup revision, and a
later `update_appearance` publication still refreshes the tray.

Read/write failures are visible with stable typed messages, without raw OS errors
or paths. Failed writes retain the prior committed selection. An uncertain IPC or
post-publication synchronization outcome disables another write until a deliberate
fresh inspection; it never blindly repeats the mutation. Invalid, oversized, linked,
unknown-field or unsupported-version files remain untouched, with System fallback
and visible recovery guidance rather than silent replacement. Logging records only
the operation and stable outcome/problem, never file bytes or configuration paths.

`themes.css` owns shared semantic light/dark colors for initial connection/loading/
error presentation, the shell, conversations, forms, dialogs and every Settings
category, including the scoped Projects, Agent, schedule, Diagnostics and
Import / Export treatments. A static OS media-query fallback covers initial paint
before IPC. The fixed light color descriptions in presentation sections describe their light
baseline; the feature extends them through semantic dark equivalents. Preserve all
layout/content/state semantics, selected/disabled/hover/focus states, strict CSP,
native geometry and decorations. The feature extends application colors and
text/layout preferences through the device-owned boundary below. Transparency,
blur, external fonts/assets, feature flags, database migrations and server
synchronization remain outside this preference. Record component/build and temporary storage evidence separately
from actual supported-platform CEF OS/theme/restart/multiwindow, keyboard containment
and 200% zoom acceptance in PRs/issues/CI, retaining unavailable targets explicitly.

#### Device styling and custom themes

Appearance uses five flat sections: Theme, Composer, Session status, Display and
Images, followed by Language and Date format under their independent controllers.
Its left-aligned body alone is capped at 720px; other forms retain their existing
widths and the shared desktop/medium/compact padding. Separate flat sections with
thin semantic rules and 24px gaps. Keep 26px/32px category titles, 16px/24px section
headings, 14px/20px labels and 12px/18px explanations. Place section help 6px below
its heading and leave 12px before the first row. Show the computer-local scope
and automatic-save explanation while retaining actual Reading/Saving/Saved and
failure states. Ordinary rows have a 56px minimum, 8px vertical padding, 24px gap
and 200px control column, with associated descriptions and native controls.
Checkboxes remain native checkboxes: an 18px indicator is centered in a
transparent target of at least 40px aligned at the control-column start, and label
click, target click and Space keep native behavior. The Language label is top-anchored in its row and vertically centered on the
40px combobox (its global block margin reset to 0) at Appearance body widths of 640px or more; opening, filtering,
showing the empty result and closing the in-flow option list never move the label
or the combobox, and below 640px the stacked label sits above the picker. Three independent
Tool/Reasoning/Compaction selectors share one wider grouped row without merging
values or accessible names. At body widths below 640px, the Appearance-scoped
container stacks row labels/controls, radio tiles and grouped selectors; actions
wrap and content scrolls vertically. Retain every labelled disabled renderer,
longer behavior/recovery explanation and custom-theme management action.
Language and Date format retain their existing ownership. Ordinary selections
save automatically. Theme mode retains System/Light/Dark, with independent light
and dark palette references for Default, Titanium, Nord, Dracula and Solarized.
Default preserves the original colors. Custom libraries hold at most 32 UUID-v7
identities, with names of at most 80 Unicode scalar values. Bundled themes are
immutable; duplication creates a separate editable identity. Each palette row has
its own localized Duplicate action beside its selector. The action resolves that
row's selected bundled or custom family independently of theme mode and clones
its original name and complete light/dark maps into the existing editor with a
fresh UUID-v7 identity. Opening or cancelling performs no preference write.
Explicit Save adds only the new custom identity and preserves both selected
references. Retain custom-library row actions, the 32-theme limit, revision and
recovery guards, modal focus restoration and narrow wrapping.

Titanium, Nord, Dracula and Solarized each provide complete light/dark semantic
maps in the shared bundled JSON. Their surfaces, text, borders, links, focus,
selected states, inverse surfaces and conversation colors follow each family.
The stored values use the approved encoded-sRGB channel blends with rounded
opaque uppercase hex output; no runtime palette generator is used. Corresponding
Default warning, danger and success values retain their meaning. Dark running
status retains Default teal; light running status uses the darker teal variant.
Default maps remain unchanged. Saved bundled references adopt updated bundled
values; existing custom maps and earlier duplicates retain their stored values.
Frontend distributions and the native host must rebuild from the shared JSON;
tray projections use that same embedded source. Geometry, independent mode
selection, mounted drafts and excluded terminal/backdrop/shadow/native surfaces
retain their existing ownership.

A custom editor owns its name and complete light/dark opaque semantic color maps.
Its synthetic preview contains no conversation content. Save and import require
explicit confirmation. Import accepts one version-1 JSON theme of at most 32 KiB,
with name and complete light/dark token maps, and always creates a new identity.
Unknown fields/tokens, non-#RRGGBB colors and failing text/control contrast reject
adoption. Exact token-set checks compare the key count and each required key
instead of a delimiter-joined key list, so a key containing a comma cannot
stand in for several tokens. The frontend and native validators require the same
contrast rows for each light/dark map: `text`, `text-secondary`, `muted`,
`text-subtle` and `link` against `surface`; `success-text` against
`surface-subtle`; `conversation-text` against `warning-background`;
`on-accent` against `accent` and `accent-hover`; `selected-text` against
`selected-background`; `warning-text` and `danger-text` against their
backgrounds; `on-inverse` against `inverse-surface`, each at least 4.5:1; and
`control-border` and `focus` against `surface`, plus `focus` against
`surface-selected`, each at least 3:1. A saved custom theme that fails these
rows makes the appearance document invalid (the file is preserved), the same as
any other failing contrast row. Terminal colors, backdrop, shadows and native OS surfaces are excluded.
Validated tokens use an application-owned constructed CSS stylesheet without raw
CSS injection or a CSP exception. The selected root palette must outrank built-in
theme rules in main and retained tray windows for explicit Light/Dark and resolved
System mode. Replace or dispose only the exact owned sheet; preserve independent
light/dark choices, default colors and scoped custom previews. Export captures one
committed custom theme.
Deletion requires confirmation and atomically returns all selected references to
Default. Cancel discards only the editor/import draft. Concurrent revisions keep
dirty drafts visible and block save until explicit discard/reload.
The editor preview validates the identity-bearing custom theme draft (UUIDv7 `id`
plus version, name and both color maps); the strict no-ID shape applies only to
theme file import and export. An invalid id, token or contrast row installs no
preview sheet. Submitting freezes the name and every color input while the save is
pending and records the exact submitted theme. Acknowledged success closes the
editor by comparing the persisted custom theme with that submitted snapshot, never
with later draft state. Failure or an uncertain outcome keeps the original draft
and the existing Reload recovery; Cancel and disposal behave as before.

When session accent is disabled, focused content inside a user message keeps an
outline with at least 3:1 contrast against `surface-selected`. Use the semantic
`focus` token when it meets this threshold. Otherwise, compute the higher-contrast
opaque black or white value and expose it through the render-only
`--focus-on-selected` variable. This fallback does not change stored theme tokens.
Stored maps must already meet the `focus` to `surface-selected` 3:1 row above, so
the fallback is only a render-time safeguard.

Composer and Display retain Regular/Compact layouts and explicit 12/14/16/18px
text choices. Project and General Chat creation retain the 210px Regular minimum.
Compact removes only that container floor; its five-row textarea, 12px padding,
64px textarea minimum and wrapping toolbar determine natural height. Supported
12px/14px content may fit below 210px, while larger text or wrapped controls can
grow beyond it. Preserve manual vertical resizing, creation placement, scrolling
and reachable controls at narrow widths and effective 200% zoom. Switching layout
retains the same mounted input, draft, selection, focus, attachments, skill bindings,
resource/mode choices and original pending/uncertain request; it never submits.
Default text size preserves the original per-component size;
Original disclosure defaults preserve each component’s original expansion. Explicit
Expanded/Collapsed overrides apply only to newly mounted supported content. Changes preserve mounted drafts, focus, attachments and business
request identities. Session Default/Minimal presentation and accent controls
preserve all approval/error/recovery controls and Session information. Token/time
visibility changes only already validated observations; omitted observations
remain unavailable. Color-vision assistance adds non-color state cues. Animation
Off disables application motion; system reduced-motion preference always wins.
Tool, reasoning and compaction-history defaults initialize newly mounted
supported disclosures without replacing explicit choices on mounted content.
Markdown, Mermaid, SVG and automatic table charts retain enabled preferences but
remain visibly unavailable until their independently owned renderers exist.

Inline images Off retains an explicit labeled reveal action. Fit preserves the
bounded existing presentation; Original uses a bounded scrollable viewport.
Styling cannot change original authenticated Worker bytes, retained-image digest
validation, immutable attachments or independent cleanup. Preferences remain
native-owned across trusted windows and restart, outside server backups/portable
transfer. Complete snapshots share original revision, atomic persistence and
uncertain-save recovery. Product/browser/native validation retains the repository
policy; report actual performed evidence separately from skipped acceptance.

The appearance context exposes `ready` (`useAppearanceReady()`), which is false
only until the initial native read settles. A failed initial read also settles,
with compatibility defaults (Original disclosures, images shown). Before
readiness, tool groups and entries render collapsed without recording a choice,
so a delayed saved Expanded default applies exactly once to untouched groups and
entries; an explicit toggle made earlier is kept, and later preference changes
never replace mounted choices. Before readiness, retained images make no
authenticated attachment byte request and show no image (a loading status), and
draft images show no preview, unless the user explicitly reveals. After
readiness, saved Off keeps the labeled reveal action and saved On or default
preserves the original bounded readback and cleanup behavior.

#### Shared restrained entrance motion and Appearance

Desktop only. `entrance-motion.ts` and `entrance-motion.css` (relative to `apps/delidev/src`) own one shared, statically scoped 160ms entrance primitive: `translateY(4px)` to `none` with `ease-out`, keyframe `entrance-y4`, selected by the activation-scoped attribute `data-entrance="y4"` (`EntranceMotion.Y4`). It never changes opacity, scale, height or geometry, has no bounce, stagger, fill mode, exit animation, dependency, inline style, CSP exception, telemetry or per-frame/content logging, and its resting transform is `none` with fully opaque surfaces. The 120ms `translateY(2px)` (`entrance-y2`, `EntranceMotion.Y2`), 120ms `translateX(4px)` (`entrance-x4`, `EntranceMotion.X4`) and 120ms `translateY(4px)` (`entrance-y4-short`, `EntranceMotion.Y4Short`, owned by Search) siblings live in the same stylesheet with the same rules; any further primitive is added by the screen that first needs it. The primitive excludes native, fixed and portal positioning hosts and their ancestors. A native dialog that mounts beneath an animated surface (`Modal` calls `settleEnclosingEntrances` before `showModal`) settles that surface's in-flight entrance in the same commit, so no dialog host ever has an animated ancestor; the dialog's own inner block still plays its single entrance and focus never waits. A top-layer host that asks `settleEnclosingEntrances` to settle an enclosing entrance clears its `data-entrance` attribute synchronously, before React applies the matching state update, so the host measures an untransformed anchor. A retained surface that opts in with `clearWhenDisabled` (the Usage tab content) settles its in-flight entrance at once when it stops being enabled, and re-enabling never replays it; every other surface treats `enabled` only as the condition read when an activation starts, so a one-render request such as the Settings Map or Review stage keeps its entrance running. Every fixed-position popup, tooltip and hover card beneath an animated destination (the Home session hover card, the New project tooltip, the Pull requests Refresh and repository-details popups, Settings action tooltips and every `ScrollPicker`) settles the enclosing entrance before it first measures its anchor.

`useEntranceActivation(activation, enabled)` owns one explicit activation. A new activation key plays the motion once (a key that arrives while the previous entrance is still running resets and re-declares the attribute, forcing a style flush, so the animation restarts instead of continuing the old timeline), only when the surface opted in, Animation is not Off (`data-animation` is not `false`) and OS reduced motion is not requested. The attribute clears on the element's own `animationend`/`animationcancel` (descendant animations are ignored; an `animationcancel` queued by the intentional restart reset is ignored while an animation of the same name is still running, checked through `getAnimations()`) or, as a generation-fenced fallback, after 240ms. Switching Animation Off or enabling OS reduced motion mid-flight clears it immediately through the existing global `animation: none !important` suppression in `themes.css`; re-enabling never replays the current activation. Rendering, reads, refetch, polling, pagination, typing/streaming, async progress, errors, permission changes, same-category reselection and Strict Mode replay never restart it. Rapid departure and re-entry replace the keyed surface, so a stale completion cannot affect the new activation or retain an inactive surface. Focus, navigation, dismissal, disposal, RPC, draft/selection/scroll ownership and mounted controller identity never wait for animation completion.

Settings opts categories in through `entranceCategories` in `settings.tsx`; the activation key is the category opening (`selection.key`) held by `SettingsVisit`, and the attribute lands on the category content column (heading and body) inside `SettingsWorkspace`. Appearance is the first opted-in category: its explicit category opening and its custom-theme editor (`Modal` with the `entrance` prop, one activation per explicit open) use the primitive. `Modal` applies the attribute to an inner block that wraps the dialog header and body, never to the native `<dialog>` host, so the top-layer modal host and its geometry stay stable. Theme, language and date selectors, autosave, import, deletion and every save keep their immediate behavior, and an open editor keeps its dialog, draft, focus and controller identity. Each additional category or task opts in only with its own approved contract text.

#### Settings category and task entrance

Desktop only. `entranceCategories` in `settings.tsx` maps each opted-in `SettingsCategory` to an `EntranceTarget` (`entrance-motion.ts`). Every opted-in surface uses the shared 160ms `translateY(4px)` Y4 primitive and the replay-safe rules above. The activation is the category opening (`selection.key`) and, for tasks, one mounted task window. Opted-in categories with target `Surface`: Appearance, Keyboard shortcuts, Server preferences, Paired devices, Notifications, Import / Export, Backups, Agent Workers, AI API Keys, AI Subscription, API Providers, Instructions, Project defaults, Projects, Repositories and Git Profiles (`SettingsCategory.Integrations`). Opted-in categories with target `Heading`: Runner Devices (`SettingsCategory.ExecutionWorkers`), Tailscale (`SettingsCategory.Tailscale`), Connections and App information.

- `Surface` moves the category content column, which holds the heading and body. `SettingsTaskWindow` also plays one entrance for every Settings task opened inside any opted-in category, through `SettingsTaskEntranceContext` provided by `SettingsWorkspace`. The task entrance moves only the task `header`, never the native task `<dialog>` host or its body: a transform would make the dialog the containing block of fixed descendants (for example portaled tooltips) and the contract above excludes native positioning hosts. Tasks outside an opted-in category never animate. Opening, editing, saving, cancelling, refresh, polling, pagination, async progress, errors, permission changes and job or history updates never restart it, dismissal is immediate with no exit animation, and focus return, dismissal, disposal and request ownership never wait for it.
- `Heading` moves only the static `.settings-category-heading`; tasks always move only their own task heading. Runner Devices, Tailscale, Connections and App information contain persistent portal hosts, native controllers and update or connection callbacks (Tailscale hosts the This computer, Devices on your tailnet and Connection requests portals); no ancestor of those hosts receives a transform, and their controllers, original version evidence, pending update checks, connect, re-pair and retry requests keep their identity. `Modal` takes `headingEntrance` for desktop-owned Connections and Runner Devices tasks (Saved server add, rename and removal presentation, Tailscale enable and device selection, and local re-registration). It plays one entrance on the dialog `header` and never on the dialog. The owner supplies `presentationRequest` for retained tasks: a Modal that mounts visible is one presentation, and afterwards only a changed request that becomes visible (a user action that opens the task, Continue after a dismissal, or a new Add generation) adds one. Visibility changes without a new request, such as a Connections host slot appearing or the page becoming active again, stay immediate. Incoming Tailscale approval prompts and slot-driven Saved servers presentation never animate.
- Import / Export (`configuration-transfer.tsx`) additionally animates the Map fieldset and the Review preview section once when the user explicitly requests that stage (Load configuration document, Preview configuration changes). `requestedStage` records only that request and is cleared by edits, invalidation and stage arrival. The Map activation is an explicit Load request counter, not the `loaded` visibility: loading again while a document is already mapped replaces it in one event batch and still plays one entrance (the shared hook restarts a running animation for the new key). Stage changes that are derived from asynchronous results (apply progress, uncertain-request recovery, import result) stay immediate. Exact transfer bytes, mappings, original request IDs and protected state are untouched.
- Agent Workers animates the category and both owned task windows (Worker wizard create and edit, and Preview routing), each once per opened window through the `Surface` rules above. Inside the Worker wizard (`agent-worker-source-wizard.tsx`) the static step `h3` heading additionally plays one entrance per user-selected step change: harness confirmation, Next, Back and selecting a different step in the step indicator. `stepRequests` counts only those handlers and is the activation key through `selectStep`; the first step shown when the task opens and automatic routing through `fail()` (validation failures that return the user to Harness, Accounts, Model or Configure) never animate. The entrance moves only the heading, never the form, fieldset, step sections, model combobox popup or scroll-picker popovers. Model refresh, endpoint or subscription discovery, account inspection, typing, polling, refetch and pagination never replay it and never advance a step. Chosen sources, permission settings, exact model IDs, request counts and the original uncertain save request are untouched. `agent-worker-wizard.test.tsx` and `settings.test.tsx` cover this with synthetic fixtures.
- Keyboard shortcuts animates the category only. Key capture, shortcut dispatch, typing and validation never restart it. The category has no separate task dialog at present, and any future owned task must opt in with its own contract text.
- Paired devices animates the category, the pairing task and the revocation confirmation. Disclosures such as Details stay instantaneous. Pairing codes, device credentials and confirmed-revocation state are not read or logged by the motion.
- AI API Keys (`SettingsCategory.ApiAccounts`) animates the category and every owned task window: Add account, Manage connection (format and details) and Edit preferences. `AccountSettings` renders its own heading, so `Surface` moves the content column that holds it. Each opened task window plays one entrance on its task header only; stage advance inside the wizard (provider choice, key entry), typing, format selection, validation requests and replies, retries, status or health changes, inventory refetches and pagination never restart it. The key, format and source drafts, the original save and connection requests and their request identities, and the clear-on-dismiss credential lifecycle are untouched, and the secret input, its mask and its value are never inside an animated element or read, logged or stored by the motion. A new Add account window opens with an empty key and plays a fresh entrance. `settings-credential-motion.test.tsx` covers this with a synthetic credential and a held connection reply; it grants no account or native acceptance.
- AI Subscription (`SettingsCategory.SubscriptionAccounts`) is the default Settings landing category, so opening Settings plays its category entrance once like any other category opening. It animates the category and every owned task window: the Connect subscription and Claude login window, the Manage subscription window and OpenCode Go windows. Step navigation does not open another window, so the logout confirmation is a step of its Manage window and never replays the window entrance. Failed-login cleanup is an inline status disclosure, not a task window, and never animates. A hidden retained Claude login mounts a new window (and one entrance) only when the user explicitly chooses View original operation; login responses, progress polling, native OAuth callbacks, refetches and spinners never open, restore or replay a window, and Escape hides or disposes the task immediately with the existing native OAuth Dispose. The exact paid-credit balance overlay is a fixed positioning host: it settles any in-flight enclosing entrance through `settleEnclosingEntrances` before placing and measures its anchor again once the untransformed layout commits. See `apps-delidev-subscription-settings-contract.md#settings-entrance-motion`. `settings-subscription-motion.test.tsx` covers this with synthetic fixtures; it grants no native or account acceptance.
- API Providers animates the category and the custom-provider editor window (one header entrance per opened window). An identical or held provider refresh, retry, activation switch or editor close never replays the category entrance, accepted provider rows keep their positions, and the motion starts no inventory read, automatic endpoint discovery or switch. Focus returns to the opener without waiting for the motion.
- Instructions animates the category, the instruction editor and the deletion confirmation, each window once. Typing, saved or failed state, refetch and dismissal never restart it, and the exact instruction content and original save and delete revisions are untouched.
- Project defaults animates the category only, on explicit opening. The singleton revision, read and create guards, inherited, default and unknown values, the draft lifecycle (a draft is still discarded on category departure) and the disclosure groups are unchanged: expanding a disclosure has instant geometry and never replays the entrance or reads policy. A return to the category is a new explicit opening and plays once.
- Projects animates the category and the New Project, edit and delete windows, each once per opened window. Switching an editor tab (General, Access, Repositories), authoring a draft, saving, retrying and opener fallback never restart it. No project is created or deleted on animation completion, and the tooltip portal and the Scroll picker popups stay outside the transformed header.
- Repositories animates the category and its owned task windows, each once per opened window: Add repository, editing an existing repository and the delete confirmation. A targeted entry from Pull requests (`SettingsEntryDestination.Repositories`) is an explicit opening and plays once. Clone job, save job and inspection progress states are async-derived and never replay it, and the motion starts no clone, inspection, save, delete or extra repository read. The GitHub child chooser (`GitHubRepositoryDialog` in `repository-github-picker.tsx`) is a portal dialog outside the task window, so it plays its own single header-only entrance per opening through `useEntranceActivation` on its static `.repository-github-header`; the native `dialog` host and the scrolling body never carry the attribute, the heading ref and initial focus are unchanged, and choosing a row, Escape or Close dismisses only the child without waiting for the motion. The parent draft (clone URL, name, integration and profile selection), original source identity and local or cloned checkout boundaries are untouched.
- Git Profiles animates the category and its owned task windows, each once per opened window: New GitHub profile (`GitHubOnboarding`), Rename GitHub profile and Manage (wide). The Delete profile confirmation is a step inside the Manage window, so it is not another window and never replays the window entrance; likewise the Verify to Confirm stage and the Confirm to Token return in the onboarding task are async-derived or a back path and never replay it. A targeted entry from Pull requests (`SettingsEntryDestination.GitProfiles`) plays once. Token entry, the existing token-type shortcut that opens GitHub in the browser, verification, accepted request authority and the original scope fence stay click-driven and unchanged, the token is cleared on dismissal exactly as before, and no token value is ever read, logged or placed in an animated element. System status, token inspection, replacement, validation, deletion and external-open counts equal a no-motion baseline.
- Runner Devices (target `Heading`) animates the category heading and both owned task windows, each once per opened window: the per-device settings task (`MachineSettings`) and the SSH setup task (`SSHSetup`). A targeted entry (`SettingsEntryDestination.RunnerDevices`) plays once. Inventory inspect, refetch, pagination and Local Worker status polling never replay it. `LocalWorkerControls` (the native-backed Start and Stop controller and its generation fence) and the SSH setup section stay mounted under the same controller identity, the motion adds no Local Worker read, Start, Stop, SSH connection, inspection or reconnect, and dismissal is immediate with focus returned to the original opener. Portal and tooltip hosts are never inside a transformed ancestor when shown; only the static category heading moves. Runner Devices hosts no Tailscale portal.
- Tailscale (target `Heading`) animates only the static category heading, once per explicit opening (navigation, search selection or re-opening after leaving). Its three portal hosts (This computer, Devices on your tailnet, Connection requests) are never inside a transformed ancestor. Refresh, access polling, discovery, per-peer checks, request refetches, locale switches and re-selecting the current category never replay it and send no enable, disable, begin, decide, resume or cancel request. The enable and device-selection confirmations keep `headingEntrance` and the incoming approval prompt never animates. `settings-runner-devices-entrance.test.tsx` covers the heading and host placement.
- Animation Off (`data-animation=false`) and OS reduced motion prevent the motion and clear an in-flight entrance immediately, and re-enabling never replays the current visit. `settings-motion.test.tsx`, `settings-entrance.test.tsx` and `settings-configuration-entrance.test.tsx` (API Providers, Instructions, Project defaults, Projects), `settings-repositories-entrance.test.tsx` and the Add repository and GitHub chooser tests in `repository-registration.test.tsx`, `settings-git-profiles-entrance.test.tsx` and `settings-runner-devices-entrance.test.tsx` cover this with synthetic fixtures; the shared no-entrance baseline category is `unoptedSettingsCategory` in `entrance-test-support.ts` (currently Browser) and moves when that category opts in; they grant no native or account acceptance.

#### Conversation entrance motion

Desktop only. `SessionView` (`session.tsx`) opts the shared Session/General Chat surface into two entrances from `entrance-motion.ts`. Neither transforms the transcript, composer, progress, approvals, live message content or any scroll root, and neither waits on focus, navigation, disposal, RPC or draft/selection/scroll ownership.

- Session heading and toolbar: the `div.session-header-entrance` wrapper inside `header.session-header` plays the 120ms `translateY(2px)` Y2 entrance once per explicit session activation. The header itself becomes a scroll root in compact widths and heights, so it never carries the transform; the wrapper mirrors the header's flex layout through inherited properties. `useActivationCount(active)` counts rising edges of the existing `active` prop (selection, or returning to a retained session), and the activation key is that count with the session ID. Renders, reads, refetch, polling, pagination, typing/streaming, async progress, errors, permission changes and startup projection never restart it. Inactive sessions never animate. The same wrapper inside a retained, published Sidechat's embedded `SessionView` (heading, connection status and Stop/Resume/Actions toolbar) plays the same entrance once per explicit activation of that Sidechat tab, the rising edge of its pane `active` prop after mount; `useActivationCount(active, activateOnMount)` counts an embedded pane's mount only when `SidechatPane` marks it explicit: `SessionTabsStore.automaticSidechat(id)` is true after `publishSidechat` and cleared by `open`, so a Sidechat that mounts selected because `publishSidechat` promoted its pending tab, one published or updated in the background, and one that mounts inactive never animate and the first later explicit selection plays once, while a Sidechat the user opens (`open`, for example from a Search result, including a never-visited parent) that mounts selected plays once. `PendingSidechatPane` renders no heading or toolbar (status, recovery actions and composer only), so a pending Sidechat has no entrance and gains no header or controls. The transcript, composer, draft, held late replies, child identity and independent lifetime are untouched, and motion never creates, sends or cancels a Sidechat. Opening the Session actions popup (`SessionActions`) settles any in-flight enclosing entrance in the same commit through `settleEnclosingEntrances`, so the transformed wrapper never caps the popup's z-index beneath the later navigation siblings; focus moves to the first action without waiting for the motion.
- Session Info heading: the persistent Info card never animates when it merely appears, including when startup presentation reveals it. Only an explicit opening (`showInfo`: Show details and the recovery or budget entries) increments an opening counter and plays the 120ms `translateX(4px)` X4 entrance on the `header` inside `aside.session-information`. A later explicit opening plays again; there is no exit animation, and Info keeps its controllers, disclosures and focus.

Animation Off (`data-animation=false`) and OS reduced motion prevent the motion and clear an in-flight entrance immediately; re-enabling never replays the current activation. Rapid leave and re-entry replace the activation key, so a stale completion cannot affect a new activation. Shared 160ms Y4 rules in the section above (no inline style, dependency, CSP exception, telemetry or per-frame logging) apply unchanged. `session-entrance.test.tsx` and `session-sidechat-entrance.test.tsx` cover activation-only play, no replay, Sidechat promotion and background publication, preference changes and controller identity with synthetic fixtures; it grants no native or account acceptance.

#### Session tool entrance motion

Desktop only. The Session tools opt their static heading and toolbar into the shared 120ms `translateY(2px)` Y2 entrance from `entrance-motion.ts` (`EntranceMotion.Y2`, keyframe `entrance-y2`). Every tool follows the same rules: the `data-entrance="y2"` attribute lands on the tool's own `header` element only, once per explicit activation of the tool, through `useActivationCount` (or the tool mount, where the tool is mounted only while it is open) plus `useEntranceActivation`. The tool body, its scroll roots, native, fixed and portal hosts and their ancestors never carry the attribute. Reads, refetch, polling, pagination, typing/streaming, async progress, errors and permission changes never restart it; Animation Off (`data-animation=false`) and OS reduced motion prevent it and clear an in-flight entrance immediately, and re-enabling never replays the current visit. Rapid leave and re-entry replace the activation key, so a stale completion or late reply cannot affect the new activation. Focus, Escape or Close dismissal, disposal, request ownership, controller identity and draft/selection/scroll ownership never wait for animation completion. The shared Y2 rules (no opacity, scale, height, bounce, stagger, fill mode, exit animation, inline style, dependency, CSP exception, telemetry or per-frame logging) apply unchanged. `session-tool-entrance-helpers.ts` holds the shared test helpers; each tool's `*-entrance.test.tsx` covers its rules with synthetic fixtures and grants no native or account acceptance.

- Diagnostics: `RequestDiagnostics` (`request-diagnostics.tsx`) is mounted only while the Diagnostics panel is open, so each explicit open plays one entrance on the panel `header` (Model request diagnostics title and Close). Validated diagnostic values, complete identities, unavailable and error states and disclosures render immediately. The motion starts no read and logs no model content. The pagination chain, the execution filter draft, the execution ID and the focus granted to the execution input are unchanged, and neither the diagnostics portal target nor the retained job portal sits inside the animated header. A reread that resolves after the panel closed cannot replay, focus or navigate. `request-diagnostics-entrance.test.tsx` covers this.
- Files: the `header` (title plus Refresh and Close actions) of `SessionFiles` (`session-files.tsx`) plays one entrance each time the Files tool becomes the active panel: `useActivationCount` counts the rising edges of the existing `active` prop, including the first open that sets `filesOpened`. The retained hidden, inert panel keeps its `FilesController`, expanded directories, scroll and selection, and an in-flight entrance settles when the panel stops being active (`clearWhenDisabled`). The `header` of `SessionFilePreview` plays one entrance per explicit preview open: mounting the preview panel (opening or re-selecting its tab) or opening a different file, keyed by session, repository and path. Directory reads, refresh and retry, expansion, tree rows, preview bytes and the heading focus never animate or wait for the motion, and read `AbortController` cancellation, bounded coverage and the serialized read owner are unchanged. A directory reply that arrives after the user left cannot replay, focus or navigate. `session-files-entrance.test.tsx` covers this.

#### Destination screen entrance motion

Desktop only. Home, Pull requests, Usage and Schedules opt their retained destination content into the shared 160ms `translateY(4px)` Y4 entrance from `entrance-motion.ts` (`EntranceMotion.Y4`). Each surface counts explicit activations with `useActivationCount(active)` (the rising edges of its existing active flag, including a first mount that starts active) and derives the `useEntranceActivation` key from that count, so the entrance plays once per explicit activation or return and never for renders, reads, refetch, polling, pagination, typing, streaming, async progress, errors, permission changes or saves. The attribute lands only on an inner content element that is neither a native dialog, a fixed or portal positioning host, nor a scroll root, and no ancestor of such a host carries it; a `Modal` or popup that mounts beneath an animated element settles it first through `settleEnclosingEntrances`. The compact drawer opening or closing alone is not an activation. The welcome content (`section.welcome` in `App.tsx`, shown when no session is selected) plays one Y4 entrance per rising edge of `Surface.Sessions`, owned by the shell so the section mounting later never replays it; selecting a session, status reads and Retry never restart it. The Project and conversation options dialog settles the Home entrance from its opener before it mounts, so the popup never animates with the wrapper.
