#### Tailscale category presentation

The `tailscale` Settings category (`SettingsCategory.Tailscale`, label **Tailscale**, listed after Paired devices in Device management, icon path in `settingsIcons`, entrance target `Heading`) exists only in the original local desktop window, where `Desktop` supplies the optional `runnerTailscale` publisher prop to `App`, which forwards it to `Settings`. `TailscaleConnections` (`tailscale-connections.tsx`) stays mounted in its original desktop owner (`desktop.tsx` controls) and owns every access, discovery, check, begin, decide, resume and cancel request, request ID, retained mutation and approval prompt. Access polling and discovery run only while their slots exist (`DeviceInventory` mounts only with the devices or requests slot and keeps the existing on-mount discovery), and the unsupported state (no `TAILSCALE_CONNECTIONS_V1`) shows the existing unsupported guidance in **This computer** without discovery or mutation requests. A failed capability read is not the unsupported state: **This computer** shows **Unavailable or blocked** with the sanitized problem. **Connection requests** shows **No connection requests.** only after a successful list read; before that it shows the loading line, and after a failed first read it shows **Connection requests could not be read. The enable confirmation, incoming approval prompt, uncertain access, decision, resume and cancel retained input, and the exact-original-request retries live in the owner and survive leaving and returning. They reflow at 960x640, narrow widths and 200% zoom, and each is a static search target (`tailscale-computer`, `tailscale-devices`, `tailscale-requests`).

- **This computer** separates the stored access intent (Enabled or Disabled) from the observed status. Only the `ready` state reads **Ready**; `off` reads **Off**. Enabled intent with `setup-required` or `cleanup-required` reads **Action needed** with the guidance line "Check Tailscale sign-in and HTTPS setup, then refresh devices." and never claims readiness; Disabled intent with a non-Off, non-Ready state keeps "Setup or cleanup required". The Enable or Disable action follows the intent (Enable keeps its confirmation), and the original-request inspection control appears only while a retained access or decision request is uncertain. Login-required guidance and sanitized problems are unchanged.
- **Devices on your tailnet** shows the installed-client state, Refresh and the peer rows (ownership, Online state, the independent DeliDev check state, the explicit Check action, Connect and Register Worker only after a successful check under the existing eligibility, and the SSH path). Online status alone never enables a connection.

Automatic availability checks (visit queue): each mount of `DeviceInventory` is one visit of the devices presentation. After the first successful `running` discovery of the visit settles, it snapshots the peers whose manual Check control is enabled (online and not shared to) and sends one `CheckTailscale` read per snapshot peer, in discovery order, with the exact peer ID and at most one automatic read in flight (a serial queue; the backend takes a non-blocking lock on every status read). The active row reads `DeliDev: Checking…` in its `role="status"` line with a subtle decorative `.tailscale-progress` indicator (static under `prefers-reduced-motion`) and a disabled Check button; queued rows keep `Not checked`. A settled row shows the existing **Accepting requests** or **Unavailable or blocked** state and the sanitized Problem detail, then the queue advances; a failure never blocks later peers. Offline and shared-to peers, an unsupported server (no `TAILSCALE_CONNECTIONS_V1`, no `DeviceInventory`) and saved-server windows (no controller) send no Tailscale request. Connect and Register Worker still require the verified `identity.approval` plus the existing online and `workerEnabled` predicates. Check stays available after completion or failure and re-checks only its own peer (a manual Check on a queued peer is its read; the queue then treats it as settled without a second read). The queue is the single owner of whether a peer was already checked automatically in this visit: it records each peer as claimed when its automatic read is handed out and as settled when that read ended, in the `DeviceInventory` state, independent of row mounting, the gcTime 0 check cache and the live or active flags. A claimed peer keeps its automatic check enabled and its read running while a failed discovery refresh or access read hides or changes the surrounding presentation, a read that ends while the rows are hidden is recorded as settled (success or failure), and no recovery, Refresh, access change or peer metadata round trip re-enables, restarts or repeats it; the queue starts a later peer only after every claimed read ended. Rerender, Strict Mode effect replay, window focus, reconnect (`refetchOnWindowFocus` and `refetchOnReconnect` stay false) and Refresh never duplicate or restart it, and peers first seen after Refresh are only manually checkable until the next visit; a queued peer whose host changes, or that goes offline or vanishes, is dropped from the visit queue for good (recorded in the `DeviceInventory` state, settled or not), so a later Refresh that restores it never re-enters the queue or shows an automatic result for it and it is only manually checkable for the rest of the visit, and the queue starts the next peer only after the dropped entry's own read in flight has ended so two automatic reads never overlap. A check result (success or failure, automatic or manual) belongs to the host, online state and sharing the peer had when it was read: when any of them changes, the row hides the result and its Problem detail at once, clears its manual opt-in and resets the cached read for that peer ID, and a read still in flight is allowed to finish and is then discarded, so a restored peer reads **Not checked**, shows no Connect or Register Worker, and its next manual Check always sends a fresh read. Leaving the category unmounts the controller's presentation, which drops the queue and cancels the active read, so a late response cannot update a later visit; reopening starts a fresh visit. Page entry sends no enable, disable, begin, decide, resume, cancel, pairing, Worker registration or SSH request. A manual Check or Refresh during an automatic read may fail with the backend Conflict; it is the ordinary per-peer or discovery failure and is retried manually.

- **Connection requests** lists the retained requests with the Approval pending, Approved, Denied, Expired, Completed and Outcome unconfirmed states, preserves exact-request resume, cancel and retry with the same request ID and bytes, shows loading and empty states, and keeps the incoming approval modal in the owner.

`settings-runner-tailscale.test.tsx` covers placement, absence from Runner Devices and Connections, unsupported and saved-window fixtures, intent versus Ready, retained confirmation and uncertain requests, incoming approvals, `onPaired`, search and Korean copy; `tailscale-connections.test.tsx` covers the controller retries and login guidance. `settings-runner-tailscale.test.tsx` also covers the automatic check queue: serial order and exact peer IDs, eligibility, failure with single-peer manual retry, leave and reopen, and Strict Mode, focus, reconnect and Refresh, and peers that go offline, change host or vanish before or during their turn, plus discarded automatic, manual, failed and in-flight results of peers that changed and fresh reads on the next manual Check. A table-driven matrix there crosses the automatic check states (in flight, in flight then failing, settled success, settled failure, never started) with discovery error and recovery (single, repeated, with the read ending while hidden), access error and recovery, peer metadata change, category re-entry and Refresh, and asserts exactly one automatic read per peer per visit.

Each device row maps a proved Check failure cause (`FailureCause` `tailscale_connection_refused`, `tailscale_timeout`, `tailscale_certificate_invalid`, `tailscale_unexpected_http` or `tailscale_invalid_identity`, each with its exact code; the unnamespaced generic values never map) to a localized `InlineRemediation` alert that interpolates the device name. The cause display changes only what a failed row shows, never when checks run: it applies identically to the failure of an automatic visit-queue check and of a manual Check, and the queue, its eligibility and its serial order stay as described above. A refused connection changes the row status to **DeliDev: Could not connect** and shows **Could not connect to DeliDev on {device}.** with **On {device}, start DeliDev and enable Tailscale access, then select Check again.**; it never claims the process is stopped. Other causes show only their own heading and guidance and keep the **Unavailable or blocked** row status. The summary stays outside the closed Technical details disclosure, which keeps the original safe message, guidance, code and correlation ID. Generic, unknown or mismatched failures keep the existing Problem. Check, SSH setup, query lifetime, the absence of automatic retries, responsive layout (the alert takes the full row width and wraps at narrow widths and 200% zoom), keyboard behavior, the **Accepting requests** success state and offline or shared-to rows are unchanged. The latest query result always controls the row: when a re-check, a discovery refresh or an access read fails after an earlier success, TanStack Query keeps the previous data next to the new error, and the controller ignores that cached data. A failed re-check removes the **Accepting requests** status and the Connect and Register Worker actions (a refused retry shows **Could not connect**); a failed refresh removes the cached inventory status and hides its peer rows (the rows and their check queries stay mounted, so a settled automatic check or failure is never discarded and no automatic check is issued again when a later Refresh recovers; the user retries manually) and shows **Unavailable or blocked**; a failed access read treats the access status and the Disable or Register Worker actions as unknown. While the access state is unknown (the first read is pending or the latest read failed), the access Enable or Disable button and the open Enable confirmation are disabled, so no fresh request that could clean up a working ingress is sent; a retained uncertain request keeps its original retry control, and a later successful read restores the action. A later successful result restores them. A check result still belongs to the peer observation it was read for: when discovery changes the host, online state or sharing, the row hides the cause guidance, failure, identity and actions together with the earlier result, as described for the visit queue above. `tailscale-connections.test.tsx` covers each cause for automatic and manual checks, locale switching, the generic fallbacks, these latest-failure overrides and the host or online invalidation of a cause.

#### Projects grouped presentation

The feature replaces the Projects-only the feature presentation exception with the shared white/semantic-theme surface, left-aligned 1040px category column, 26px title, 14px body, 40px controls and 8px radii. Refresh settings and the single + New Project remain in the shared header, stacking below 1100px. The exact scope, read states, server order, IDs, grouped form fields and behavior below remain authoritative. Decorative vectors are accessibility-hidden, styles remain static CSP-compatible and focus/control boundaries retain AA contrast.

Only a successful empty first page with no continuation token and no read failure shows the shared 160px-minimum empty region, 24px after the heading. Place a 32px decorative folder at the left of the 16px semibold “No projects yet” title. Its left-aligned secondary copy is exactly “Group repositories and choose which Agent Workers and AI accounts a project can use.” followed by “Choose New Project to get started.” There is no second create action. Initial loading/failure never claims emptiness. Successful cached results remain during refresh; failed refreshes retain rows with their sanitized error, guidance, correlation and “Refresh failed. Showing the last successfully loaded results.” Failed cached emptiness does not show the definitive empty panel. Empty later/continuation pages show “No projects on this page.” and retain First page/Next page. Hide pagination only for successful final first-page emptiness.

Loaded Projects use one flat divided panel, preserve server order and tokens, and retain project-specific accessible Edit/Delete actions. The feature presents complete wrapping project names and configured source URLs in saved order. The feature uses compact divided rows with 16px vertical padding, 16px semibold project headings and 14px body text. Derive cardinality from saved repository IDs. Exactly one saved repository omits its count and Primary badge; omit its secondary name only when validated Ready metadata exactly matches the project name. Retain different names and all loading, unavailable, missing-URL, stale and sanitized failure guidance. Multi-repository and zero-repository counts remain visible beside the project heading when space permits. URLs are inert selectable text; they provide no navigation, clipboard or execution authority. Only the saved primary repository receives the Primary badge. Show the first three repositories and retain order, primary identity and button focus across Show all/Show fewer. Project details is an initially collapsed, Projects-scoped borderless native disclosure with no enclosing padding, a 40px summary target and visible focus. It retains the complete project UUID and associated repository UUIDs, including IDs whose metadata cannot be read. No sorting or automatic page traversal is added. Unsupported schemas disable Edit/Delete. New Project remains available during list loading/read failure; server authorization remains authoritative. Existing resource-read failures and revision mismatch block a new edit Save without discarding the draft.

One Projects-category metadata owner resolves only exact repository IDs referenced by all mounted Project payload pages through the existing authenticated generated GetResource query. Deduplicate across those pages and limit the entire category to eight concurrent transport reads. Share permits across response generations; a started read retains its permit until the original transport wait settles, even after disposal, Refresh, page changes or same-identity reconnect. Remove disposed queued references before dispatch. Retain only validated bounded display projections; remove transient full Resource responses from the query cache. Validate the exact requested kind/ID, supported schema, positive uint64 revision, bounded safe name and configured URL with the existing repository Clone URL validator. Preserve the original configured URL bytes; never use inspected remotes or derive a replacement source. Reject malformed responses and revision regression without replacing accepted projections. Distinguish loading, URL not configured and unavailable details. Explicit Refresh starts a new batch while retaining prior successful details as visibly stale until a valid replacement arrives. Failures preserve project rows and action eligibility, show only sanitized shared guidance/correlation references, and never poll or retry automatically. Prune references outside the mounted payload window; category exit, connection identity replacement and unmount abort/fence reads and follow-up work. Same-identity authentication reconnects retain accepted projections and do not retry settled reads; explicit Refresh uses the replacement transport. This adds no RPC, schema, migration, capability, dependency or native authority.

Existing project edits retain every existing field and explanation in four mounted tabs: General, Repositories, Execution and Access. Repositories retain ordered selectors, shared repository drag handles, Remove controls and explicit required Primary repository. Removing the primary clears it without replacement. Each restriction retains configured-empty “permits none” semantics; turning it off clears selected IDs and permits otherwise eligible entries. Keep full serialized documents, byte limits, captured revisions, busy/uncertain locks and Save/Cancel/original request retries beneath the form. Deletion uses the same scoped flat section while retaining confirmation, session/history consequences, future schedule effects and the original revision/retry. No autosave or replay is added.

New Project selected rows and Edit Project repository rows share one repository-only reorder controller. Each editable row starts with a focusable 40px grip, then position/name and Remove. Unique resolved names hide secondary IDs; duplicate or unavailable names expose exact wrapping, selectable inert UUIDs. Selected rows and creation summaries contain no Repository details disclosure. Catalog candidates and unrelated Accounts, Instructions and restrictions retain their original controls.

Pointer movement starts only from the grip, captures the original pointer and previews destination order locally. The moving row's accent border identifies its destination; edge movement scrolls the existing dialog body. Drop commits the preview to the draft; a same-position drop is a no-op. Space/Enter picks up the focused UUID, Arrow Up/Down moves within bounds, Space/Enter commits and Escape cancels before dialog dismissal. Keep UUID focus and localized pickup/position/completion/cancellation status. Pointer cancellation restores the original snapshot without changing the draft. Disable singleton movement. No movement sends Save or changes the primary UUID.

Admission checks current active/visible/editable state, original transport, connected DOM, Settings lifetime and native disabled/inert/hidden ancestor locks. Capture an immutable starting UUID sequence. Cancel on changed gates, connection replacement, source order, disposal or document hiding; reject late callbacks. Busy/uncertain request owners remain outside this view. Creation's untouched name follows the first committed selected repository; manual names remain unchanged. Metadata arrivals do not reset movement, order or focus. Explicit Save retains original revision, full document extensions, byte/count bounds and exact uncertain retry ownership. These presentation controls add no backend, RPC, protocol allocation, migration or native authority.

New Project alone uses a three-step creation wizard in the shared 768px form dialog with fixed header/footer, scrolling body, 40px controls, existing semantic themes and wrapping actions at narrow widths. Step 1 searches repository names and narrows a native checkbox list; users select multiple repositories, then reorder or remove the ordered selection. Step 2 retains Name and an editable Primary repository selector from those repositories. New Project defaults the primary to the first selected UUID only when its previous repository selection was empty. Step 3 retains Agent Workers and AI accounts restrictions and shows the project name, ordered repository names and primary repository before Save. Step indicators are non-interactive; Previous/Next preserve the draft and selection, and only step 3 exposes Save. No autosave is introduced.

Creation reads the authenticated existing repository catalog sequentially in 50-record Connect Query pages, searches the complete accepted inventory and displays candidates in groups of 50. Accumulate only ID/name metadata, never original resource documents. Retain successful metadata and selections after a failed page; Retry reads that exact cursor and Reload begins a fresh catalog chain without replacing selection identity. Separate initial loading, partial loading, read failure, final registered-empty and final no-match states. Reject malformed/repeated page cursors without claiming complete inventory. Leaving or hiding the task cancels its client catalog waits; late results cannot publish or start another page. Settings disposal retains its existing authoritative-effect boundary.

Candidate labels, ordered selections, primary options, summaries and existing edit repository fields display names while document values and selection keys retain original UUIDs. Resolve existing edit names by their exact IDs, including IDs outside selector pages. Missing or unsupported names show explicit unavailability, never another repository's name or a UUID as the display label; failed name reads support retry. Duplicate names remain distinct selectable identities and expose their original ID as inert secondary text in selected rows. Names and details render as inert text.

Until the user edits Name, it follows the first currently selected repository after selection, removal or reordering; removing all repositories clears the automatic name. A manually edited name survives later selection changes. Creation preserves a valid automatic or manual primary through additions and reordering. Removing the primary clears its selection without choosing a replacement while any repositories remain; later additions cannot refill that blank selection. Clearing all repositories and selecting a new first repository establishes a fresh creation default. Existing edits continue to require explicit selection. No background repair changes arbitrary empty or invalid primary values. Step 1 requires at least one unique repository within the existing 1,000-entry bound; step 2 requires a nonblank name within 256 UTF-8 bytes and a primary from the selection. Final submission rechecks every required value and returns focus to the invalid step/control. Preserve complete document bounds, configured-empty restrictions, captured revision rules, duplicate-submit guards, exact uncertain original requests, pending dismissal and Settings lifetime behavior through the existing ConfigurationEditor controller. This adds no public API, protobuf, database, dependency or execution authority.

Fresh creation focuses repository search once after the modal captures its opener; explicit step 2 focuses Name and step 3 focuses its heading. Catalog completion, language changes and reflow cannot steal focus. Search and native checkboxes have accessible names and retain Tab/Shift+Tab/Space behavior. Input controls retain the shared no-focus-decoration contract; buttons retain visible focus. Native-dialog Escape, Close, Cancel, contained focus and opener restoration remain owned by the shared task host. On accepted completion its delayed restoration rechecks pending child signals after their cleanup, while hidden retained operations keep their focus boundary. Validate all three steps in English/Korean and light/dark themes at the listed sizes and effective 200% layout; distinguish browser checks from actual packaged CEF keyboard/platform/zoom acceptance.

The feature own the visit lifetime: navigation away discards Projects drafts, editors, confirmations, cursors, waits and uncertain presentation. Home creation uses its independent dialog lifetime; Settings-internal New Project and targeted Repositories entry use the Settings visit. Protected/deferred navigation, same-identity reconnect and successful-save invalidation remain unchanged within the applicable visit. Preserve sibling session/composer/query state and late-result/cache-disposal guards. Native decorations, maximization, 1280×820 restored and 960×640 minimum sizes remain unchanged. Validate empty/list/create/edit/delete at 1440×900, 1280×820, 960×640, 640×480 and 200% zoom, preserving the below-760px shared navigation drawer, scrolling to all actions and full identities. Child-dialog and shared-drawer background inertness, keyboard containment, Escape and opener restoration require separate actual desktop evidence; browser and component checks alone cannot establish them.

Account metadata editing is separate from credential connection, validation, catalog refresh and disconnection. API-key input is password-masked, limited to the server's printable ASCII contract, and cleared on submission or hiding the form. Its wire bytes can remain only in the bounded visit-scoped exact pending request after uncertainty; completed React Query mutation variables are released. Keys never enter read keys, logs or browser persistence. Keyless connection requires the selected provider's explicit keyless configuration. Service-native subscription configuration uses its independent managed login capability and never inherits system credentials.

The 35 canonical Provider presets retain one server/CLI/desktop order with 32
hosted defaults and three explicit local defaults. Account key guidance exposes
explicit official-key and documentation actions on the native desktop. Rust
accepts only a canonical preset/action and uses the Go-generated compiled public
HTTPS allowlist; server-supplied URLs cannot expand OS opener authority. Regional
key separation, ordinary API versus subscription/coding-plan guidance, Hugging
Face inference permissions and Baseten personal keys remain explicit. Opening
help never validates a key, creates an account or sends inference; unconfirmed
OS opening retains a sanitized status without automatic replay. See the
[provider contract](cmds-delidev-providers-contract.md).

The build app manifest declares `open_provider_guidance`. Its dedicated
`provider-guidance` permission allows only that command and is granted through
the trusted `main` and `server-*` webview capabilities, never through their
containing windows or remote origins. Regression tests resolve the generated
build manifests and capabilities with Tauri's authority resolver across the
desktop targets, checking trusted access and external-child/remote denial.
These permission checks do not establish OS browser dispatch or page access;
actual native browser opening requires separate platform verification.
After preparing the native assets and sidecar, run these permission tests with
`cargo test -p delidev-desktop --features desktop-host,custom-protocol --lib permission_tests`
from the repository root; the default library feature set excludes native ACL
generation.

Account settings separate **AI Subscription** and **AI API Keys** presentation sections while continuing to query the existing Account resource. Each section sends the server-side account-type selector; provider-row links add the exact provider ID. Filtering must happen before pagination, and cursors must remain scoped to the exact account type and provider. The desktop requires the provider activation, active-model filter, account-provider filter and explicit account-type-filter capability markers before enabling split lists or the guided API account flow. It must never fall back to a mixed list, client-page filtering or an inferred all-enabled provider inventory. The wizard rechecks the fresh provider identity, authentication, protocol, endpoint and enabled state before saving account metadata and before an explicit credential connection; it never validates or discovers models automatically. API connection, validation, health, quota, exhaustion and credential cleanup remain distinct states. Category navigation stays locked during account creation, settings and connection workflows; application navigation remains available, with exact uncertain requests retained for deliberate retry. Independent server capability 30 enables ChatGPT browser login followed by editable account naming under the subscription Settings contract; Claude follows its independently negotiated selected-Runner flow; Grok follows the independent System capability 39 browser flow under the subscription Settings contract (its explicit `Use a device code` action shares capability 39 and the same Settings contract). The feature replaces the creation picker’s search, radios, selected markers, numbered steps and Continue with native provider action buttons. Choose an API provider / Select a provider to connect your entry. precedes server-ordered enabled saved API entries reached through shared scroll continuation. The picker requests `query: ""`, `enabledOnly: true`, `pageSize: 50` and its own cursor, independent of AI API Keys’ unsearched account-provider inventory and API Providers’ search. Both account and picker inventories must retain all four capability gates; no generic resource page or credential inference can supply eligibility. Direct-entry details remain disabled while either inventory lacks the gates, and become unavailable again if those capabilities are lost. The clicked UUID and complete summary/Resource are retained as one bounded hint even when the account-filter page does not contain that provider. The clicked snapshot remains authoritative across unrelated inventory refreshes; the existing fresh provider checks validate or reject its contract before writes.

The feature supersedes the prior API creation-card geometry. API list and child workflows use one left-aligned fluid column at most1040 CSS px wide, provider choices at most 720px and entry/preferences forms at most 720px. Remove the outer creation card. Preserve the shared 32px content padding, 24px below 1100px and existing narrow-screen padding. The picker is always one full-width column with 10px gaps at every viewport and zoom level, and never a multi-column grid; the page wrappers created by shared scroll continuation use the same single-column stack and gap, so providers on later or retained pages are full-width rows too. A retained (evicted) page wrapper keeps its measured height as `min-height` with `align-content` and `align-items` set to `start`, so its Restore control stays content height. Neutral native `button type="button"` actions have 64px minimum height, 12px padding and 8px corners, exact provider names, muted API key or Local endpoint methods and decorative chevrons. No selected/pressed semantics, invented logos or inferred OAuth availability are used. System fonts, white content, primary ``, secondary `b6577`, accent/focus `d8` and panel border `#d8dee8` remain scoped to API Account documents/workflows. Use a 26px semibold main title, 16px step headings, 14px body and 12px metadata, 40px minimum controls, 8px control corners and flat groups with AA contrast. Other Settings categories share these body defaults; Settings-external callers retain their appearance.

A deliberate click, Enter or Space opens the existing entry form immediately and focuses its step heading. Back/Change retains the picker page and restores the original provider-button focus. The feature replaces First/Next page controls with shared scroll continuation and an accessible Load more fallback. Reached display identities accumulate in server order while at most three complete provider response pages remain resident; older ranges restore from accepted opaque tokens. Back/Change preserves the reached range and selected identity. Explicit retry preserves the failed query/cursor; cursor expiry requires explicit reload. Loading, typed permission denial, read failure/Retry and stale cached results remain explicit. Open API Providers is offered only for a successful empty first page without continuation; empty pages with continuation keep continuation and cannot imply globally empty inventory. Restoration, rerender, Strict Mode replay and provider navigation cannot create/connect/validate/discover or start authentication. Leaving follows the visit-disposal policy above.

Entry-name/key validation, password masking and transient key clearing, collapsed preferences (`enabled=true`, `exclude_automatic=false`, `recovery_notifications=true`), explicit keyless connection and server-relative localhost guidance remain unchanged. Fresh provider checks precede metadata save and connection; one save is followed by one deliberate connection, with saved-account retention on connection failure, unverified health, separate validation/discovery, original request/revision retries, navigation locks and late-continuation guards. Record browser/component fixtures separately from native/provider acceptance in the feature, its pull requests and CI runs.

The feature simplifies AI API Keys for a few saved entries. List mode owns one **AI API Keys** title, one top-right **Add AI API key** action, the description **Manage AI API keys and keyless local connections. Connection and health are separate states.**, the scope **Saved on the selected server.** and a subtle divider. Saved results, Manage connection, Edit preferences and Delete entry use one clear heading, full inert entry identity, the scope line and existing Back/Cancel actions.

Remove API Search providers, Filter entries by provider and More provider filters entirely, with no hidden filter equivalent, totals, sorting or bulk operations. Its account-provider inventory always sends `query: ""`, `enabledOnly: false`, `pageSize: 50` and an API-owned bounded cursor. Display that provider’s exact label or complete inert ID with **Clear provider filter**, which clears the scope/hint and returns account pagination to its first page. Saved entries retain server order in flat divided semantic rows with the shared 16px padding. The approved usage body adds **Your API keys**, **DeliDev usage · Last 30 days** and **Refresh usage**. Each row presents the full wrapping alias/provider identity, separate connection and health states, historical **Estimated cost**, **Observed tokens** with observed-response counts, and saved **Quota** observations. Confirmed exhaustion remains authoritative; missing observations are **Not reported**, never measured zero. Costs remain separate by currency and native accounting unit; unavailable native totals are never computed from categories. A successful empty usage interval shows **$0** estimated cost and **0** observed tokens, both with **No usage in this period**. Empty presentation requires returned native accounting support, present response totals, zero response and all returned accounting-unit counts, present native summary totals, and no accepted executions or native context actions without response usage. Loading, failed reads, absent totals, unreported usage or prices, and older accounting profiles cannot become zero. Refresh failures retain the last successful values with the existing stale notice. This empty display is independent of connection/health and quota and does not establish actual charges or alter ledger/budget evidence. **More actions → Details** opens one read-only 768px Form Settings task with heading focus, a localized Details title and the full entry alias as its subtitle. Details is first, before **Edit preferences** and **Delete entry**. Close the disclosure and focus its permanent More actions button before mounting the dialog; X/Escape restores that opener when available, otherwise the shared category fallback. Remove the inline Details trigger and keep only **View usage** in the row footer. Retain API format, Entry Enabled/Disabled, Provider Enabled/Off/Unavailable, safe Account identity labels, every disclaimer, exact half-open range, incomplete/measured/unavailable usage, separate estimates/native accounting and full quota observations/timestamps. The mounted row retains its original usage query, loading/error/stale state, quota clock and verification/management controllers; dialog open/close/reopen/language changes add no read, write, verification or discovery. Category departure disposes only its presentation. **Manage connection** stays visible. Unknown schemas retain More actions and read-only Details while Edit/Delete, Manage connection and View usage keep their original strict gates. Preserve shared modal background inertness, keyboard containment, body scrolling, wrapping identifiers and semantic theme tokens. **View usage** deliberately opens the original account and exact returned half-open range in the existing Usage page. Unknown schemas retain inert safe identity labels and disabled business/navigation actions; read-only Details grants no authority. No stored-key masking/readback/reveal/copy is added.

The list uses generated account-scoped GetUsageSummary reads only for its current bounded page, with the server-default last 30 days and independent native accounting profile. It never traverses inventory, sums groups in React, queries provider billing or polls usage. Refresh usage refetches the current Account page and active scoped summary reads without connection, validation, discovery or native quota operations. Usage read failure is independent of entry management; retained values are marked stale, and deliberate retry reads only that exact account. The shared Settings opening owns summary caches and cancellation. View usage carries an in-memory unique event key and original account/range; it applies once and subsequent navigation/reconnect cannot overwrite Usage filter drafts. These reads grant no credential or execution capability. Below the list retain **Known usage may be incomplete. Estimates are not billed amounts.** and the existing secure-storage note. Example values and preview notices are fixture-only.

At 900px of available body width, usage metrics move beneath identity/actions; below 640px the metrics and actions stack. The existing 1040px cap, typography, semantic light/dark tokens, 40px controls, 8px corners and below-760px shared category drawer remain authoritative. Reflow, refresh and disclosures retain focus and the existing Settings disposal policy.

Only a successful unscoped final empty first page shows the approximately 260px-high `#fafbfc` neutral panel with a decorative key, **No AI API key entries**, **Add an entry for an enabled API provider.** and **Keyless local providers do not require a key.** It has no second Add action. A provider-scoped final empty first page says **No entries for this provider.** Empty continuation or later pages say **No entries on this page.** the feature uses shared scroll continuation and an accessible Load more fallback with opaque cursors; retain fetching guards and render at most three complete resource pages. Only complete chain emptiness grants the unscoped or provider-scoped empty state. Below results keep **Credentials are stored securely on the selected server.**

Initial capability loading, permission denial, missing capability markers and sanitized read failures cannot claim successful emptiness. Failed refresh retains cached rows and the stale notice; cached empty failure suppresses definitive current-empty copy. Each failed inventory/account read has a deliberate Retry disabled while fetching that refetches only its current request/query/cursor, never writes, traverses pages or grants eligibility. All four account and picker capability markers remain required, including capability loss after direct provider entry.

The Provider → Details flow remains immediate. Keep **Only enabled API providers appear here.** and arbitrary supported saved providers in server order; preview names are examples. Deliberate provider activation focuses the step heading; Change restores the exact provider-button focus on its retained page. Details uses **Connect your entry**, a slim provider/method summary and **Change**, Entry name, a transient password-masked API key only when required, collapsed **Where to get an API key** with every existing guidance/documentation string, and collapsed **Advanced preferences** with all existing fields/defaults. Preserve **Use a separate entry for each API key.**, **Stored securely on the selected server.** and **New connections remain unverified until you explicitly validate the connection.** Keep one **Add and connect** submit and the top list-return action; remove the duplicate footer Back to provider. Explicitly keyless providers omit key input/key-creation guidance, retain server-relative localhost/local-endpoint explanation and never ask for key reentry after local failure.

Name/key byte limits, fresh provider checks before save/connection, one metadata save followed by one intended connection, retained saved entries after connection failure, distinct connection/health/validation outcomes, exact original request/revision retries, busy/uncertain locks, secret clearing and late-continuation guards remain authoritative. Management retains active-only five-second status reads and explicit Connect, Validate connection, Refresh models and Disconnect eligibility, separate validation/catalog observations with original times and sanitized problems, exact original cleanup retry and all disconnection consequences. Preferences retain immutable provider/type, complete fields/observations, captured revisions and guarded Save/Cancel/retry; they cannot mark an entry ready. Deletion retains explicit confirmation, disconnection/cleanup and relationship checks, sessions/history and original uncertain requests. No automatic validation, discovery, secret persistence or replay is introduced.

Use static CSP-compatible CSS, semantic headings/articles/navigation, explicit labels, visible focus, text alongside status colors and decorative aria-hidden vectors. Keep the existing below-760px shared category drawer and independent shell scrolling. Child dialogs and the shared drawer retain their own inertness, Tab containment, Escape and opener restoration; Settings has no outer modal or Close action. Long UTF-8 aliases, provider names and safe identity labels wrap at 200% zoom; actions and forms stack without clipping. Fetching/reflow cannot steal focus. The common Settings-visit disposal policy continues to own drafts, cursors/scope, confirmations, secrets, waits/retry presentation, ordinary Subscription reopening, targeted entry and same-identity reconnect; preserve sibling caches and Strict Mode guards. Record revision, commands, actual results and native geometry/keyboard/zoom limits in the feature, its PR and CI artifacts under the current repository validation policy. Component/browser/build/package checks cannot establish native/provider acceptance. This ships in the ordinary frontend build without backend/native/API/schema/migration, dependency/asset, logging, credential-storage, flag or deployment changes.

API entry creation is a content-level Provider → Details flow inside Settings. Only the provider inventory's enabled API entries may be selected. The Details step keeps alias, a masked transient key only when required, and collapsed existing account preferences; keyless entries require an explicit connect action and retain server-relative localhost meaning. Creation is followed by a fresh provider read immediately before one explicit connection attempt, with the created account retained after connection failure. Manage/Done navigation stays disabled while that provider check is in flight. The registered Local-role (`main`/`local-*`) `local_worker_proof` command is read-only infrastructure. It accepts no renderer path, command or chosen machine. Missing, foreign or malformed registration fails without pairing, starting or replacing a Worker; Worker bootstrap/lifecycle uses its separate explicit native control boundary.

Selecting Local identifies this computer's paired machine, clears starting overrides and disables arbitrary Worker selection. Submission reads proof again and requires the same selected machine and still-selected connection. The server revalidates actual authorization/revocation at the product commit boundary. Existing Local schedule edits can retain their original authenticated machine without new proof. Proof tokens do not enter form state, read caches, documents or logs; only the bounded immutable pending RPC can retain them after uncertainty, and exact retries cannot silently change to a replacement credential. Connection disposal prevents a late native read from submitting a mutation.

### Automatic main-window local Worker management

A fresh trusted main desktop process owns one joined Worker supervision task in addition to server supervision. A retained reserved admission or readiness wait remains on its original generation; native observation of original child exit, or fresh-launch durable original-controller proof, and Go admission gates are required for replacement of incomplete controller evidence. The surviving Worker uses its existing Local transport to reconnect to later proved desktop generations; update polling and original update-outcome reporting use that same protected outbound boundary. Preparation failures log only the bounded stage and safe error code.

Existing repository editing/additional checkout inspection preserve explicit saved values and remain separate from primary replacement.

GitHub choice appears only for a current connected schema-v1 GitHub.com PAT profile without a pending change and without a registration/Clone mutation in progress. Profile inventory and repository inventory are bounded independent pages; profile selection never defaults to the first account. Explicit profile/repository selection fills its constructed HTTPS URL and exact revision/identity metadata. A same-repository SSH edit retains that association; another or invalid URL clears it. Show name, Public/Private and Archived, Filter this page, shared cumulative continuation and explicit refresh. Loading, current successful empty pages, no filter matches, restricted/authentication/malformed reads, stale cached rows and changed profile generations remain separate. Only a currently verified page can select a repository. Older servers explain the update requirement while retaining existing-folder registration.

Clone requires valid URL, existing absolute parent and portable editable folder name. Immediately before submission, reread this computer's native proof/status and server Worker capability; no remote machine selector can grant new Clone authority. Retain the exact accepted request through transport uncertainty, with only identical retry or original job observation. Observe the durable Clone job independently: its server completion performs registration. Closing or category departure discards inputs, reads and guarded continuations while the accepted job continues. Authentication uses existing computer Git/SSH credentials; the PAT reads metadata only. The atomic Clone action is available only before the repository name or optional settings are edited because its existing request carries only clone inputs; edited drafts use Add repository so their settings are not silently replaced by server defaults. Failed registration displays the preserved checkout path for existing-folder registration; ownership or process uncertainty blocks a new Clone.

Successful existing-folder selection clears repository-bound overrides and reinspects with no inherited preferred remote before new inference; canceled selection retains the draft. Pending/uncertain inspection or save blocks source replacement/new requests. Original jobs are observed without replay, and uncertain requests retry only their retained exact bytes. Only confirmed successful save publication returns to the repository list; failed/canceled saves may return to the current draft. Leaving Settings/disposal drops the entire registration presentation and guarded picker/proof/inspection/save continuations, initiates no follow-up request and cannot steal focus. Already accepted native/server operations remain authoritative and can appear in fresh inventory reads without wizard restoration. This composes 's disposal guards with 's application-screen visit. Settings has no page-level Close/Escape dismissal; page-level Escape preserves the visit. Actual child dialogs retain their dismissal semantics. A fresh ordinary visit starts at AI Subscription; explicit Repositories entry remains supported.

The creation column is limited to 760px, retaining Settings white/gray/blue tokens, current category naming, 40px targets, disclosure state and progress/error announcements. Summary rows/actions stack on narrow layouts; existing Settings scrolling, shared compact category drawer and destination focus apply at 960×640 and 200% zoom. Native picker/webview authorization and keyboard/geometry evidence must be recorded independently for macOS, Windows and Linux; component/compile evidence alone does not establish those runtime outcomes. No new feature flag is required; optional result enrichment uses protocol capability negotiation.

Saving repository configuration acknowledges a durable asynchronous job. The UI retains and polls that exact job, shows queued/claimed/uncertain/failed/canceled/succeeded independently, and reports configuration publication only after success. Failed/canceled saves permit an explicit return to the retained draft; uncertainty cannot submit another save. Read refresh never resubmits a Worker operation. Confirmed configuration deletion uses the captured revision, preserves retained sessions and explains affected future schedules/account cleanup; uncertain retries retain their original identity. API entry deletion uses a dedicated confirmed cleanup sequence: a fresh exact-version account read, original `DisconnectAccount` cleanup (including disconnected staged intents or an exact pending-removal retry), a fresh cleared-account read, and one latest-bigint-revision configuration deletion. The existing 480px Settings confirmation dialog is titled `Delete entry`, with `Delete {alias}?`, neutral `Keep entry` and outlined destructive `Disconnect and delete entry`. It explains active execution cancellation, protected credential removal, retained history/reference restrictions and independently continuing browser cleanup. Keep receives initial focus; fixed header/footer and scrollable body preserve narrow-width wrapping, theme tokens and 40px controls. Progress announces checking, disconnection/credential cleanup and deletion without percentages. Cleanup failures keep the entry, display safe original server reasons/guidance and offer only original cleanup retry. Unconfirmed mutation replies retain original IDs/bytes; after-cleanup read failures retry only inspection. Changed state requires fresh confirmation. Success closes and refreshes once, with deleted-row opener retirement and no browser-cleanup count read. Closing a task disposes its local controller and shows no hidden operation or opener; category departure blocks late follow-up deletion. Accepted server/native work remains authoritative and can appear in fresh reads. English/Korean presentation changes never replay work. This reuses existing RPCs and server protection without a protocol allocation, migration or subscription-flow change. ChatGPT account deletion additionally composes the confirmed original server logout and cleanup before configuration removal, using a fresh bigint revision after cleanup while preserving confirmed preferences. Its category-owned controller stops follow-up deletion on departure and keeps independent device/browser cleanup visible; see the [subscription Settings contract](apps-delidev-subscription-settings-contract.md). Agent routing previews show the server's candidates, eligibility, selected account, nullable quota evidence and fallback without consuming routing state or granting execution readiness.

### Worker discovery and schedules

Execution-Worker settings show platform, last observation, exact selected/resolved harness paths, version and native-protocol outcomes. Refreshing without path edits retains current selections; explicit editing replaces all four paths, with empty paths meaning Worker PATH. Original revisions and uncertain requests are retained. A checkbox separately authorizes native protocol validation without login/inference. Track the accepted discovery job before reporting completion; never install a harness or turn detection into execution readiness.

Schedules have a dedicated desktop surface that remains mounted across navigation. Creation/editing sends only the strict editable definition: prompt, project, Agent, Worker, input mode, cron, explicit IANA timezone, overlap policy and optional per-repository starting overrides. Fresh desktop schedules enable future runs by default and use Worktree. Existing saved schedules retain their enabled or paused state during editing. The server alone computes next UTC due times, skips offline instants, applies overlap/skip/FIFO wait and resolves execution authority. Existing Local definitions can be edited with their unchanged authenticated Worker; new/relocated Local schedules require fresh private proof from this computer's paired Worker through the native boundary. The UI never accepts a supplied UUID as origin proof.

Pause/resume changes future scheduling only. Run now explicitly confirms one independent occurrence, works while paused under ordinary server eligibility, and retains the original request after uncertain acknowledgment without enabling the future timer. Accepted occurrences are shown independently from native execution and current session state. Each occurrence history row labels its own identity with the Occurrence presentation kind (Scheduled run / 예약 실행 with an occurrence-scoped number), while schedule details keep the Schedule kind for the real schedule ID; numbers are assigned per kind. Delete confirms future configuration removal, while the independent paginated history remains visible, refreshable and accessible by retained schedule ID. Every configuration/control mutation uses its captured revision, and stale edits preserve their draft. History and status reads do not replay side effects.

### New schedule creation

The creation presentation owns `apps/delidev/src/schedule-creation.tsx` and
`apps/delidev/src/schedule-creation.css`; shared schedule state and mutations
remain in the existing schedule editor.

Only creation without an initial resource uses the Task → Execution → Repeat → Review wizard in one centered column capped at 720px. Editing, list/detail/history, the icon rail, context pane and scheduling operations retain their existing contracts. A noninteractive wrapped indicator announces completed/current/future steps. Keep authoring steps mounted, hidden, unfocusable and excluded from native constraint validation while inactive. Suspend their inventory reads while retaining pagination; the original parent Runner preference remains independent. Step and all existing drafts remain connection-owned across Back/Next, navigation and same-identity reconnect; replacement starts fresh.

Step 1 has Cancel/Next, steps 2–3 Cancel/Back/Next, and Review Cancel/Back/Create schedule, with a step count. Next validates only its step and focuses the first invalid control; Back and distinctly named Review Edit controls retain drafts without writes. User changes focus the step heading; fresh entry focuses Name once, and refresh/reconnect never steals focus. Enter in single-line inputs follows Next; prompt Enter remains newline. Only Review submits. Final creation validates all authoring steps, reveals the first invalid step/disclosure and focuses correction before calling the original save path. Local proof/save/uncertain states lock editing and all navigation/dismissal, with the original identical-request retry retained. Escape in the idle creation wizard, from any step, calls the same cancel callback as Cancel (the editor unmounts, the protected workflow clears, the Schedules sidebar re-enables and no save is issued). It does nothing while the wizard is locked (pending or uncertain save, pending Local proof, runner remediation or pending resource selection), when the event is already default-prevented (an open custom picker consumes its own Escape first, so a second Escape closes the wizard), when the event originates from a native picker control (a select such as Frequency, Weekday or overlap, or a time, date, color, file or list-backed input) because the platform picker closes on the Escape default action that runs after the keydown dispatch without setting defaultPrevented (move focus to a non-picker control or use Cancel to dismiss), during IME composition, or for repeated or modified keys. After dismissal by Cancel or Escape, focus returns to the enabled New schedule opener; when that opener is not connected or sits in a hidden or inert compact drawer, focus falls back to the visible compact Schedules opener, then to main content, and never overrides focus the user already moved. A fallback candidate counts as available only when it is connected, enabled, outside any hidden or inert ancestor and rendered (no `display: none` on itself or an ancestor and no `visibility: hidden`), so the compact opener that the stylesheet hides outside the compact breakpoint is skipped, and a candidate that does not actually take focus falls through to the next one. This restoration applies only to dismissing the creation wizard; cancelling the edit of an existing schedule keeps its previous focus behavior. Editing an existing schedule, details and other dialogs keep their current Escape behavior, and no global shortcut is registered.

Review displays three separate Task, Execution and Repeat cards with 16px gaps, 24px padding, 12px corners, decorative outline icons and distinctly named Edit actions. Definition rows use a 160px label column and wrapping values; below 600px of available content width they stack. The complete prompt uses a lightly tinted inset with preserved whitespace and no nested fixed-height scroll area.

Review displays only the exact cached Project/Agent Worker/Runner Device names, using the existing name/alias/Unnamed behavior. Missing or mismatched cached identities show bundled English/Korean Name unavailable without new reads or selection changes. System resource IDs are absent from Review text, attributes, accessibility descriptions and disclosures. Keep exact IDs internally in query inputs, definitions, validation, Local proofs and outgoing requests; equal names never merge selections. Starting overrides are ordered localized Repository 1/2 rows with complete reference type, name and optional remote. Their original repository identities remain internal; Review performs no repository reads. Preserve UUID-shaped user prompt/reference text and the existing no-overrides guidance. Review retains workspace/mode, recurrence/raw cron/timezone, overlap and enabled/paused state. It reports configured selections rather than execution readiness, preserves server next-run authority and never truncates prompts or explicit references. Safe server failures remain visible without invented field attribution.

The main-content creation form owns a
scrolling body and a separate white, top-bordered persistent action row; its

Frequency is an internal enum, never a definition field: Daily, Weekdays,
Weekly, Custom cron. Fresh creation defaults are enabled, Worktree, Execute, Overlap,
Weekdays 09:00, `0 9 * * 1-5` and explicit `UTC`. Preset Time is required
minute-resolution `HH:mm`; Weekly additionally selects exactly one weekday,

Daily emits `m h * * *`, Weekdays `m h * * 1-5`, Weekly `m h * * d` (Sunday 0,
Monday 1), with decimal numbers without leading zeros. Preset switches retain

No general parser, browser timezone substitution or client calendar validation
is introduced. Empty/invalid Time remains a visible draft, blocks submission and

Retain Overlap independent sessions, Skip new occurrences while prior work is

Settings and same-identity reconnect. Cancel performs no save; the next fresh

scheduling after desktop closure and skipped offline due instants without a

Cancel; uncertainty also disables Create and exposes **Retry the same schedule**
using its original retained definition bytes, token, request ID and revision.
Definite errors permit draft correction. Preserve 1 MiB definition, 256 KiB UTF-8
prompt and existing field bounds, retaining the previous valid draft on overflow.
Every save remains strict schema-v1 editable definition only, empty resource ID
and revision `0n` for creation, with one mutation identity and existing owner/client
authorization. Frequency, time, weekday, disclosure and resolved/server-owned

Preserve all creation authoring state, including raw Custom input, time/weekday
and disclosure, across global navigation, Settings and same-identity reconnect;

replacement locks remain active while editing/in-flight/uncertain. Focus Schedule
name once on the first active fresh entry; retained entry, refetch and responsive

state, visible focus, status/error announcements and Task -> Execution -> Repeat
-> actions focus order stay accessible. The existing compact native drawer keeps
focus containment, Escape/Close and opener restoration without remounting drafts.
The only motion is the single 160ms Y4 page entrance described in

Recovery never sends input or invokes Resume; successful reconciliation leaves the server's paused state intact.

### Session Info summaries

The Session information header shows compact, noninteractive saved model and reasoning-effort chips from the immutable initial execution configuration. Their accessible names identify saved selections. Omit unspecified effort; missing, incomplete or unsupported snapshots show unavailable model evidence and retain detailed guidance in Diagnostics. The chips and the Diagnostics saved-configuration section share one validation result: schema version 1, canonical UUID v7 initial execution and Agent identities, a source-scoped model key, positive integer Agent and model revisions no larger than the uint64 envelope (unsafe integers up to 2^64 stay admissible and display as unavailable; larger values could never be server revisions and make the snapshot unavailable), a harness from the closed supported set (`codex`, `claude-code`, `opencode`, `grok-build`), a native model ID that satisfies the server's native model ID bound (well-formed UTF-8, no NUL, not blank under Go `strings.TrimSpace` whitespace and at most 256 UTF-8 bytes), an absent or string effort (exact direct input, never checked against a value list), an options object, accounts and templates arrays, a supported routing policy and an instructions string. The model key is never a resource UUID: it is `source:` followed by the unpadded base64url JSON of the exact source (one API provider ID or one subscription service) and native model ID, and it must agree with the snapshot's own provider or subscription service and native model. A subscription service must be a known service whose native harness equals the saved harness (`chatgpt` with `codex`, `claude` with `claude-code`, `grok` with `grok-build`, `opencode_go` with `opencode`), like the server's `SubscriptionService.Harness()` check. The key must also equal the server's canonical encoding of that identity (fixed field order, compact JSON with Go HTML-safe escaping, unpadded base64url); reordered or duplicate fields, whitespace and non-canonical base64 trailing bits are rejected like the server's `ParseModelKey`. Each failed requirement independently produces the unavailable outcome for the chips and shows incomplete-snapshot guidance in place of the saved-configuration section only; native observations and applied instructions keep their original independent gate (a retained initial execution with its Agent and native model identity) and stay visible when only the strict requirements fail. No value is inferred from the current Agent, resumed executions or native observations. Current Agent edits, resumed executions and native observations cannot replace these saved chips.

Keep the principal Info groups ordered Pull requests, Subagents, Context, then Usage and budget. Hide only successfully empty PR and Subagent sections. The Subagents section is hidden only for a confirmed complete empty result: a supported owner with an accepted, current, single-page empty snapshot, no continuation token, no read error and no unrecovered failure latch. A healthy revision-triggered background Refresh over that snapshot keeps the section hidden while pending and after it settles, so Context and Usage and budget do not move; the refresh read itself is never suppressed. Initial, Reload, Retry and Additional reads, missing capability, malformed or foreign pages, continuation pages (including a chain whose last page is empty, which is no longer a single-page snapshot) and any failed read stay visible, and a pending Retry or Reload stays visible (honoring the `unrecovered` latch, not only `error`) until a successful accepted result. An accepted child reveals the section and a later complete empty result hides it again. Disposing or replacing the session or transport owner (the conversation pagination chain scope includes a stable transport owner identity, so a replacement transport that keeps the QueryClient also drops the retained snapshot) resets the section to visible so earlier emptiness or a stale response from the old owner cannot hide the new owner's initial state. The routine Status and recovery heading and Workspace/Result/Archive summary do not appear in Info. The original SessionTools portal and recovery controllers remain mounted, with applicable failures, correction guidance, confirmations, accepted/uncertain/failed jobs and exact retries in Info. Healthy empty hosts reserve no section padding or divider. Native read-only settings and usage observations, source references and safe technical snapshot details appear in Diagnostics. Original interactive native prompts, terminal/stop controls, applied instruction disclosures and storage actions remain below the principal groups, with unchanged source ownership and guards.

Usage and budget starts with a full-width input/output row: only In and Out labels are chips; exact locale-formatted integers remain plain text at opposite ends. Read the original session's response-only lifetime summary through the existing authenticated GetUsageSummary RPC. Validate creation metadata, returned bounds, profile, coverage and measures; pin the first server-default upper bound, then read older disjoint half-open ranges of at most 366 days sequentially through session creation. Add only input/output known subtotals and their measured/unavailable counts with BigInt. Missing evidence stays unavailable and measured zero remains zero. Publish only complete collections; retain the last complete result (totals and per-range Diagnostics evidence) as stale after a failed refresh with read-only Retry, including when the failed read is for a newer `execution.latest_response_usage_id` generation. The retained collection belongs to one exact owner (Session ID, the exact validated RFC 3339 creation timestamp including sub-millisecond digits, and authenticated transport); changing any of them clears it, even when the millisecond read bound is unchanged, and a successful read replaces the whole collection at once. A first read with no prior collection shows unavailable totals and the read-failed text. Default Info shows no routine coverage paragraph (including the former known-responses-only text); independent per-range evidence stays in Diagnostics. No native, child, cache or reasoning counts are added. Missing execution/compaction coverage counts remain per range, and separate reads do not establish an atomic ledger snapshot. Refresh on active entry, original usage invalidation and authenticated reconnect; cancellation and original-owner disposal fence delayed results.

Session Info is concise by default. Context leads with the prominent “Context used” metric and its progress bar. Usage and budget keeps the In/Out row and budget controls; an unconfigured estimated-cost budget reads “Estimated-cost budget · Not set” with Edit session budget, and reached-budget, failed-read, stale, edit and revision-recovery states are unchanged. Applied DeliDev instructions shows “None selected” when no additional instructions exist and otherwise preserves the actual selected content, template order and existing access boundary. No routine snapshot, coverage, budget or instruction explanatory paragraph and no Details disclosure appears in default Info; Compact context keeps its eligibility, pending, failure, uncertain-retry and ineligible-reason behavior. English and Korean strings cover the new presentation, and it adds no RPC, storage migration or observation read.

Each visible original PR row shows the standard PR icon with a lower-right dot: green (`--success-text`) for open, purple for merged and red (`--danger-text`) for closed without merge. Merged uses the fixed `--pr-merged` token defined only in the bundled light, dark and OS-dark blocks of `themes.css`; it is independent of `--accent` and is not a customizable palette token, so accent palettes and saved themes never override it. There is no textual state badge. A localized accessible name and tooltip identify state; Diagnostics retains the current observation timestamp and read-only Retry. Existing titles, Open, unlink and original failure/recovery controls remain independent. Read only active visible associations, with at most four concurrent detail reads and no polling or inventory scan. Validate the original configured repository, authenticated detail envelope and exact remote repository/PR IDs and node IDs before coloring. Merged requires a closed observation; contradictory, unavailable, failed, stale or mismatched evidence is neutral gray. Association invalidation, authenticated reconnect and session reactivation (hidden to active) each refresh these observations exactly once without mutation or expanded authority. A successful observation stays fresh while its row remains mounted, so scrolling a row out of and back into the viewport with unchanged association, row revision and connection issues no repository or PR detail request; explicit Diagnostics Retry still refetches.

Keep the existing 360px rail, compact upper band/drawer, bounded scrolling and semantic light/dark tokens. Narrow and effective 200% layouts wrap long values without replacing controllers, drafts or Info focus targets. English and Korean changes affect presentation only and start no new reads or actions.

native child through exact Hide cleanup when a page becomes inactive. Failed or

Profile explanation, address/navigation, explicit resource Close, 16-page gate,

Each Sidechat is a child conversation tab inside its original parent. Its own

Forks keep their separate session and deletion ownership. A selected Sidechat (or

and no blank sibling or horizontal overflow remains at desktop, narrow and 200%
reflow widths. Returning to Conversation restores the same mounted composer, draft
and scroll state while inactive Sidechat panes stay hidden and inert.

### Retained execution configuration and instructions

The session offers a read-only execution configuration view from its original `initial_execution.configuration`, with no current Agent/model/template lookup. Show retained harness/model/revisions, native option selections, routing/account order and weights, original account, and separately selected current execution/account. Later configuration edits or deletions cannot rewrite the displayed snapshot. Missing snapshots, unsupported document versions, additional unknown options and integer values outside exact JavaScript precision remain explicit rather than becoming defaults or reconstructed values.

Display the exact combined DeliDev instructions and each original template's contents/order/revision as inert text. Preserve whitespace and Unicode without Markdown/HTML execution or truncation, and exclude internal harness prompts and arbitrary native configuration fields. The surrounding resource reader retains its 1 MiB document bound. The scroll-bounded disclosure preserves the mounted session and unsent composer; it has no mutation capability. Memoization avoids re-decoding unchanged snapshot resources during unrelated transcript updates.

Native settings remain separate observations attributed to their recorded execution/input. Empty values and unavailable/null values are distinct; never fill a missing observation from the requested setting. Retained preceding-execution observations cannot be labeled as the newly selected execution's settings. Keep Codex sandbox/approval, Claude tool permission, OpenCode Build/Plan primary-agent and Grok initial `default`/`plan` mode observations separate. The Grok field describes its original pre-input observation; it cannot stand in for later current mode or filesystem permissions. Displaying supported observation fields does not enable an unfinished harness dispatcher or establish current account readiness.

### Retained native reasoning

The transcript renders original `reasoning-text` artifacts in a collapsed, keyboard-accessible Reasoning disclosure, separately from assistant answers and indexed summaries. Combine the initial text and strictly ordered, exactly representable index-free delta sequence once. Enforce the 256 KiB UTF-8 and 10,000-delta bounds, valid Unicode and closed state/kind shapes; complete content must equal that exact stream. Inconsistent or missing evidence displays Unavailable without partial output. Preserve empty text, whitespace and Unicode as inert text. Memoized transcript rows avoid reparsing unchanged records on unrelated stream updates. This read-only display cannot enable unfinished harness dispatch or infer a reasoning capability.

### Retained native Read operations

The transcript gives `opencode-read` its own collapsed disclosure with Pending, Running, Completed and Failed states. Validate original call identity, ordered exact sequences, immutable applied inputs/start time, content bounds and the recorded message state before presenting the retained operation. A pending proposal cannot imply a successful read; contradictory or missing evidence remains Unavailable. Preserve explicitly empty output, zero requested offsets/limits and original Unicode/whitespace. Display paths as inert text, never local file links or access authority. Original proposal/state history, native preview, loaded instruction paths and native truncation/interruption evidence stay separately inspectable. A tool error is neither an assistant answer nor an execution outcome. This read-only surface does not enable unfinished native dispatch or attachment presentation.

### Retained native Shell operations

The transcript gives `opencode-shell` a collapsed Shell disclosure with original Pending/Running/Completed/Failed state. Validate original call, immutable applied command/workdir/timeout/start, exact ordered sequences, safe integer/Unicode/content bounds and independent message closure. Inconsistent or unknown evidence stays Unavailable without partial display. Preserve omitted options without inventing defaults and explicit null exit as Unavailable, separately from no exit observation during execution.

Show the final combined output, original native exit, clipping and saved-output reference independently from rolling preview/state history. Do not concatenate previews, infer separate stdout/stderr or equate Completed with exit zero or session success. Preserve native error text and empty result. Render all commands and paths as inert text inside native keyboard-accessible disclosures, with no launch, copy-to-execute, hyperlink or filesystem access. The surface has no execution authority and cannot enable unfinished harness dispatch.

Keep step and finalized-assistant source labels, uncached/cache-read/cache-write/nonreasoning/reasoning categories, nullable reported total and exact currency-unspecified native estimate separate. The shared inbox/session interaction surface renders the separate original OpenCode payload after validating its pinned version, original request namespace, assistant/part/call/event and disjoint content. The separate OpenCode response forms preserve matrix order, native single/multiple/custom behavior, exact empty-string choices and explicitly unanswered rows; questions expose separate explicit rejection, and permissions expose native “Allow once”, session allowance and rejection with optional correction feedback. Explain session-only scope and that plain sibling rejections may stop the native run even when a direct correction is supplied. Block closed/submitted/inconsistent requests, ambiguous duplicate labels, malformed text and oversized complete responses. Protected response profiles remain unavailable; never suggest ordinary input as an answer.
