No polling, transcript reads, mutation retry, query persistence or logging is added. Closing or identity replacement aborts and fences the owner; same-identity reconnect retains query and enumeration. Destinations perform only their ordinary reads. Creation entries open their original forms without submitting or confirming; Search never receives the palette query. Only session-title navigation metadata is permitted as a dynamic palette index; exclude account/project values, URLs, paths, native observations, transcripts and secrets. Accepted sessions invoke the original App.open callback after close, preserving validated Sidechat parent routing.

Use semantic themes, min(520px, viewport minus 32px) width, min(440px, 100dvh minus 32px) outer maximum height, 16px viewport margins and 8px corners. One fixed 56px search row has a decorative 16px glyph, flexible input and 40px icon-only Close target; the localized dialog title is visually hidden. The search row uses 8px vertical and 16px horizontal padding with 12px gaps. The result list has an 8px inset on all sides within the existing maximum height, including empty, loading and recovery states. Group headings use 12px top, 8px horizontal and 8px bottom padding; each subsequent visible nonempty group has 8px separation. Only the result list scrolls and short lists shrink. Rows retain 40px targets, 8px padding, decorative local enum-derived outline glyphs and 8px gaps; the selected outline stays inside the inset row; session titles/project subtitles wrap. Retain native Tab containment and narrow/effective-200% reflow. cmdk and its imported dependencies retain complete MIT notices in public/command-menu-notices. No protocol, migration, RPC, native operation or feature flag is added. Automated component/host-browser evidence remains separate from installed CEF, real account/native and actual platform acceptance.

Require server and original Runner capability plus a settled original root,

request; stale sources and uncertain outcomes cannot submit new input.

The exact connection-owned Revert busy intent also fences the composer, even
when its presenter is reused or remounted and the session row predates job

action identity with that original mutation owner. Acknowledgment alone does
not prove native completion; definitive rejection releases only the matching
original guard. Retain uncertain bytes for explicit original-request replay.
Other sessions and connections remain independent, and disposal grants no

Accepted user text edits synchronously advance a per-session monotonic unsigned
64-bit generation before React rendering, including same-value events, undo and

Keep edited drafts and offer the existing explicit restore action. Bound edit
history to 1000 session owners; reject an edit rather than wrap or discard its
guard. Mutation-owned presentation is limited to 1000 entries and 4 MiB, with a
pending guard reserving the 1 MiB document bound for verified replacement text.
Never evict a busy/uncertain guard or retain it across connection disposal. Starting a later Revert carries the current retained restored-action identity
into its new pending presentation, so a definite rejection of that attempt
releases only its matching pending guard and never offers an already restored
earlier prompt again. When a definite rejection leaves no pending, replacement
or restored-action metadata, the presentation is deleted so its key count and
bytes are freed and mounted readers are notified; meaningful restored
identities, replacements, and busy or uncertain guards stay retained.

Verified completion restores the original prompt text as an unsent draft and
focuses the active composer. Automatic and explicit restoration preserve the
current composer Plan/Execute choice; historical input mode remains validated
evidence and does not select the next input mode. Preserve a draft edited during the operation or
while the view was inactive; offer explicit restoration of the retained prompt
instead of overwriting it. Reopening the conversation can restore that same
verified prompt without a new native mutation. Original image/skill metadata
stays in historical input records; fresh selection/staging owns later input.
Never reuse accepted attachment claims, automatically submit text, reset files
or change historical execution attribution. Earlier-context rows remain visible

not inside a hidden or inert section (the retained session tree is skipped on

`sidebar_preference.json` is an independent computer-local, bounded 4096-byte
version-1 document containing only the Expanded/Collapsed enum and its document
version. Missing storage defaults to Expanded. Keep this file outside server
configuration, pairing, exports and backups, without IDs, credentials or content.
`SidebarProvider` lives above Desktop connection and Settings lifetimes; isolated
non-native fixtures use in-memory state only. Appearance and other preferences
retain independent files, revisions and semantics.

`read_sidebar_preference` and `update_sidebar_preference` use the closed
`device-sidebar` permission only for existing main/local-* and saved server-*
product capabilities. Native admission captures/rechecks original authority,
performs storage work off the UI thread and checks the expected process
revision. Every participating native Read and Update acquires the same private,
persistent `sidebar-preference.lock` sidecar before inspection and keeps its
exclusive lease through publication, owned-scratch cleanup, parent durability
and receipt verification. Never unlink or replace this sidecar. Preserve the
presentation mutex, state mutex and sidecar acquisition order. Nonblocking lease
contention retains the committed selection and requires explicit Reload, with
ReadFailed for Read and WriteFailed for Update.

A successful Read retains private Missing/Present evidence, exact bounded bytes,
decoded version/enum, opened-file identity and link/reparse evidence, and the
original parent identity. It adopts new evidence even when the enum is unchanged.
Update compares that full observation under the lease and rechecks it after
scratch preparation. Opened handles must prove regular, unlinked storage and
original parent/sidecar identity; unsupported metadata or locking fails closed.
Unix uses device/inode identity and owner/link checks. Windows uses handle-based
volume and full 128-bit file identity, link counts and reparse checks.
Publication and cleanup are bound to the exclusively created scratch file
object, never to a bare scratch pathname. After the final destination check, open
the scratch pathname once and prove that handle is the created regular file
(owner, one link, device/inode or Windows volume/128-bit file identity) before
publishing. Missing publication moves that file onto a new target without
clobbering a target that appeared after the final absence check, so no second
scratch link remains. Present publication replaces the observed document with
that file. On Windows both renames go through the verified handle
(`SetFileInformationByHandle` rename) and cleanup deletes through the verified
handle (disposition with POSIX semantics), so a replacement at the scratch
pathname is never published or unlinked. Unix has no handle-bound rename or
unlink, so it uses single-syscall atomic renames (`renamex_np` with
`RENAME_EXCL`/`RENAME_SWAP` on Apple platforms, `renameat2` with
`RENAME_NOREPLACE`/`RENAME_EXCHANGE` on Linux and Android): Missing uses
no-replace and Present exchanges the scratch and destination entries. Immediately
after the syscall, compare entry identities with the verified file. Before an
exchange, refuse with Changed and touch nothing when the destination is already
not the observed document. If the entry that moved into the destination is not
this save's scratch while the displaced entry is the observed document (or a
no-replace move placed a foreign entry), reverse the same atomic rename so the
destination returns to its observed state, keep the foreign entry at the scratch
pathname as evidence and report a safe failure only when that restoration is
verified, otherwise OutcomeUnknown. When this save's file reached the
destination but the entry displaced to the scratch pathname is not the observed
document, a changed destination cannot be told apart from a late replacement of
the displaced entry, so never reverse it into the destination: keep the entry at
the scratch pathname as evidence, leave the destination untouched by any
reversal and report OutcomeUnknown. Foreign bytes may be visible at the
destination pathname for the duration of a verified rollback only. A reversed
rename is not durable until the lease's parent directory is synced: keep the
attempt touched through that sync and map a failed barrier to OutcomeUnknown,
and only then report the safe Changed failure. Unsupported platforms
or filesystems that refuse the atomic variants fail closed with WriteFailed and an
unchanged destination; never fall back to a pathname rename or link.
`SetFileInformationByHandle` rename has no write-through option, so after a
successful Windows publication (Missing or Present destination) and before the
bound handle is released for cleanup, call `FlushFileBuffers` on that verified
write-access handle after proving it is still the created file object by
volume/128-bit file identity. Any identity mismatch or flush failure is
OutcomeUnknown with explicit Reload recovery and no committed-state adoption;
Unix relies on the parent sync below.
On Windows, a Missing-destination first save additionally opens a dedicated
write-access directory handle (backup semantics, reparse objects not followed),
proves it is the leased parent by volume/128-bit file identity and calls
`FlushFileBuffers` on it after cleanup, before the save may be reported as
committed. A volume or ACL that reports directory flushing as unsupported
(Win32 `ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION`, `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`, `ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE`
or `ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED` while opening or flushing that handle) makes this directory barrier a skipped
best-effort step: the file itself was already flushed, a structured warning is
logged and the save is still committed. Any other open or flush failure and any
identity mismatch is OutcomeUnknown with explicit Reload recovery and no
committed-state adoption. Source byte sync, ownership checks and the Unix parent
sync are unchanged. File flush and read-back alone never establish durability,
and power-loss durability of these barriers is untested; automated tests cover
only ordering, identity checking, unsupported-error classification and failure
mapping. The identity check is tested through an injectable directory opener
with a read-only handle, so it does not depend on the host allowing a
`GENERIC_WRITE` directory open.
Adopt the new selection and private receipt only after cleanup, required parent
sync and exact published bytes/new-file identity verification succeed. Any
post-publication failure is OutcomeUnknown and requires Read recovery without
replay. Cleanup can remove only this attempt's exclusively created scratch (or,
after a Unix Present exchange, the observed document it displaced) with matching
file and parent identity; it cannot remove colliding or replaced evidence. A
foreign entry found at the scratch pathname is retained, never reported as a
fully successful save (OutcomeUnknown, explicit Reload), and the published
preference stays available for recovery. Windows deletes through the verified
handle, closes that POSIX-semantics delete handle (the link leaves the visible
namespace only then) and only afterward verifies that the scratch pathname is
gone. Unix cannot unlink by identity, so it first atomically claims the
pathname under a private `.sidebar_preference-*.claim` name, verifies the
claimed entry's identity and unlinks only a verified claim; a foreign claim is
moved back untouched. Documented residual risk: a Unix writer that observes the
private claim name and replaces it in the interval between claim verification and
the unlink can still lose that replacement.

This protocol coordinates processes that preserve the config/sidecar namespace
and use the same lease. The final evidence check detects observed changes by
nonparticipating writers. Scratch-pathname replacement after that check is
detected and reverted as described above (bound on Windows). A writer that
ignores the protocol can still replace an existing destination after the final
check and before the Unix exchange. The pre-exchange identity check refuses a
change it can see, and an exchange that displaces anything but the observed
document is reported as OutcomeUnknown with the displaced entry retained at the
scratch pathname, but the contract does not promise an atomic comparison against
writers that ignore the protocol. Process revisions
and product-window events remain process-local. Publish ordered
`sidebar-preference-changed` snapshots only to authorized product windows;
external, tray and child views have no storage/event authority. Invalid, linked,
oversized and newer documents remain unchanged. Failure retains committed layout;
uncertain writes are never automatically replayed. The product window renders no
sidebar notice, alert or Reload button for any sidebar problem. In this
contract Reload is the controller's recovery inspection: a read of the stored
preference that never saves, queues or replays a change. The only product caller
is the Toggle sidebar shortcut (primary+B, wide layout), which stays enabled
while a problem fences saves. Every problem and event has one result:

| State (idle unless stated)     | Event                               | Result                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No problem                     | toggle shortcut                     | save the opposite committed value                                                           |
| Reading or Saving              | toggle shortcut                     | ignored and never queued; no second read or save starts                                     |
| Any problem                    | toggle shortcut                     | one Reload; the requested change is not saved or queued                                     |
| Any problem                    | Reload returns a healthy snapshot   | clear the fence without replaying the original save; the next press saves                   |
| Any problem                    | Reload returns a problem or rejects | keep the fence (ReadFailed when the revision did not advance); the next press reloads again |
| Any problem, compact layout    | toggle shortcut                     | inactive; no read or save, and the fence waits for the wide layout                          |
| Any problem                    | focus or visibility                 | no inspection                                                                               |
| Any problem except Unavailable | event from another window           | ignored; a later delivery never proves an uncertain write                                   |
| Unavailable                    | event from another window           | accepted                                                                                    |

Unavailable, ReadFailed, InvalidDocument, UnsupportedVersion, WriteFailed,
OutcomeUnknown and Changed all follow the Any problem rows. Each press is
bounded to one read and no timer retries. The controller records only the
`sidebar-read` and `sidebar-save` phases of the diagnostics table above.
Renderer response/events are monotonic, contradictory snapshots are rejected and
pending/failed/uncertain writes remain fenced. A structured problem reply
(Changed, WriteFailed or OutcomeUnknown) to the original save fences the latest
committed presentation even when its revision is older than an already accepted
newer event; the committed revision and selection never regress to the older
reply, ordinary older healthy replies and older inspection classifications
(InvalidDocument, UnsupportedVersion, ReadFailed or Unavailable) stay ignored,
and only a successful Reload clears the fence without replaying the
save. Logs contain only stable operations,
revision and outcome classifications. No business RPC, protocol allocation,
migration, feature flag, dependency or OS-global keyboard bridge is added.

Primary+B works in ordinary editable inputs and consumes an accepted press once, including a press that only performs the recovery Reload.
Preserve handled/repeated/composing/AltGraph/extra-modifier, hidden/inert,
terminal-passthrough (except fixed `SessionCloseTab`) and modal exclusions, including compact navigation. The owned
help dialog retains existing eligible action dismissal. B is a fixed product
reservation in device shortcut validation, not an additional editable override.
Automated fixtures/builds do not establish installed CEF/platform persistence or
native account acceptance.

### Device navigation preference

`navigation_preference.json` is an independent computer-local, bounded 4096-byte
version-1 document containing only the Boolean `usage_pinned` and the document
version (`{"version":1,"usage_pinned":false}`). Missing storage defaults to
`usage_pinned=false`. Unknown fields, a missing or non-Boolean `usage_pinned`,
oversized, invalid, linked and newer-version documents are classified
(InvalidDocument or UnsupportedVersion), preserved unchanged and keep the last
confirmed pin state. The file is separate from `sidebar_preference.json`, server
configuration, pairing, exports and backups and carries no IDs, credentials or
content. `NavigationProvider` lives above Desktop connection and Settings
lifetimes, so the pin survives connection changes and restarts; isolated
non-native fixtures use in-memory state only.

`read_navigation_preference` and `update_navigation_preference` (argument
`usagePinned`, plus the expected process revision) use the closed
`device-navigation` permission only for existing main/local-* and saved server-*
product capabilities. The store is a parallel of the sidebar preference store and
keeps its contracts: authority capture and recheck, off-UI-thread storage work,
the persistent `navigation-preference.lock` sidecar leased from inspection
through publication, full Missing/Present observation comparison, owned scratch
files (`.navigation_preference-*.tmp` and `.claim`), atomic no-clobber or
exchange publication, parent and file durability barriers, receipt verification
and OutcomeUnknown for any uncertain outcome that only an explicit Read can
recover. Committed changes publish ordered `navigation-preference-changed`
snapshots only to authorized product windows, so other windows on the same
computer update; external, tray and child views have no storage or event
authority. The renderer applies the same monotonic, contradiction-rejecting and
save-failure fencing rules as the sidebar preference. Logs contain only stable
operations, revisions and outcome classifications (never paths or content).
Automated fixtures do not establish installed CEF or multi-window platform
persistence; real-app validation is separate.

## Per-turn elapsed presentation

Ordinary Session and General Chat show one compact muted timing line before the first original primary-input user Message, or from matching accepted progress before that Message arrives. Multiple native user parts and accepted Steer share that original line. Before the primary user record arrives, anchor the progress-derived line before the first reached native record with matching original session/execution/thread/turn and positive sequence ownership; foreign executions, turns and inherited history cannot take that anchor. Relocate the same timing observation before the original primary user once it arrives. `In progress · 1m 23s` / `진행 중 · 1분 23초` uses a client estimate from retained server acceptance; completed `Elapsed` presentation freezes the retained terminal-minus-acceptance interval. A genuine zero displays zero. Missing, malformed or inverted observations display `Time unavailable` / `시간 정보 없음`; resource IDs, diagnostics and native/provider latency cannot fill gaps.

One mounted active timer updates only the timing line once per second. Initialize the active estimate from the original Session's server `updated_at` minus retained acceptance, validating both UTC instants at their original precision before reducing to display milliseconds. Retain exact session/owner/input/acceptance identity and resource revision with that anchor. Desktop wall-clock offset or adjustment cannot affect this estimate; advance it only with local monotonic time. Missing or inconsistent server anchors remain unavailable. This is a last-observed estimate, not proof of exact elapsed time: transport delay and stale server updates do not establish the current server instant.

Repeated and older revisions cannot reset the retained estimate or transfer it to a different turn. Reconcile a newer consistent original observation without decreasing already measured time; reject same-revision timestamp conflicts, regressive server timestamps and changed acceptance. Disposal, inactive navigation and document hiding cancel the timer. Preserve the measured value, including its subsecond remainder, and resume the same confirmed observation without adding hidden time. Disconnected, failed-read or uncertain active observations show unconfirmed state and freeze the last displayed value until authoritative reads return; they never invent a terminal end. Only loss of synchronization of the owning Session resource counts: a non-Live stream, stream or message read failure, uncertain control mutation, required recovery or unconfirmed execution responses. A definitive control rejection (for example Conflict) and independent queue or interaction read failures stay visible through their own surfaces and never stop, freeze or relabel a Live synchronized timer. A newly confirmed valid server observation can advance the retained anchor. Completed history remains the immutable server terminal-minus-acceptance interval even if an active anchor is absent. Inherited Fork timing stays labelled and attributed to its original source; a child turn has its own independent interval.

Bounded reached-record timing projections retain only original owner/input identity, timestamps and inherited provenance. Preserve the bounded payload window, exact restore tokens, historical anchors, live bounds, scroll owner, composer draft and focus. Timing wraps semantically at narrow widths and zoom, uses `aria-live="off"`, and never announces every tick. It cannot change execution controls or native/mutation authority.

These fixtures establish error mapping and original-owner preservation, not installed-platform acceptance.

The feature renders ordered original native image-generation artifacts, their actual revised prompts and failure observations, and checksum-verified originals read through authenticated AttachmentService. The native Save dialog chooses the user destination, and the original authority is checked again before writing. A lost response is observed through `read_generated_image_export` using the original operation ID; it never automatically reopens the dialog or replays a write.

Publication uses a synced same-directory temporary file and atomic create-new link. Existing destinations, including symlinks, are never replaced; the user chooses a new filename. Cancellation is terminal and writes nothing. A failure after destination publication reports uncertainty and retains its original receipt. Quit fences new export admission and late dialogs on the UI loop, then joins original disk publication off that loop before native exit. The process owns one pending export and at most 128 immutable receipts; receipts are never evicted into new write authority. A changed request or another window instance cannot replay or read one. Frontend remounts retain the uncertainty fence and can explicitly observe the original receipt. Exported files are user-owned independent copies and session deletion never removes them. Downloads, general file dialogs and navigation remain denied under their existing boundaries. Outside the desktop host (`isTauri()` false) retained generated images render only the verified image: no Save control, anchor, `download` attribute or browser-download fallback is offered, and the original bytes are not retained for export. Only the explicit native Save control may export; loading, failed readback, user image inputs and inactive rendering never show an export action.

Original Save returns a closed operation-bound non-admission result only after the native controller proves that no receipt exists. Busy, stopped and invalid input may receive this proof before dialog admission; a poisoned lock, changed original scope/identity or generic transport failure cannot. The renderer releases only the matching original Save fence and permits a fresh explicit Save. Operation state is one keyed observable store per session/reference/digest: every mounted exporter of that key, including one remounted while Save awaited, receives the settled failed status and re-enabled Save without Check or another remount. Settlement never invokes export, only the retained operation object may settle its own key so an older response cannot settle a newer operation, and different keys stay independent. Check observes retained receipts only and never grants non-admission or opens another dialog. Retained receipt lookup precedes stopped/input classification so lost acknowledgments and admitted writes remain fenced across presentation remounts.

Fresh admission and Quit share one closed atomic lifecycle: running, admission-reserved, stopped and stopped-with-reservation. While holding the receipts lock, admission validates the original bytes and checks pending/capacity limits before atomically reserving the running state. That reservation is the admission linearization point. Quit sets only the stop bit without waiting for receipts, decoding, a dialog or publication. Stop-first requests receive the existing stopped non-admission result with no receipt or dialog. Reservation-first requests complete only their original admitted receipt; reservation release preserves a concurrently published stop bit. Later fresh requests cannot reserve, and late admitted disk publication remains canceled. Retained original lookup stays before stopped/input classification; poisoned locks and changed ownership remain generic failures. Existing structured `generated_image_export` non-admission logs contain only safe phases and typed reasons, never image bytes, raw paths, credentials or request content.

Fixtures cover deterministic stop during validation, both atomic reservation orderings, retained pending/uncertain originals across stop, input/pending/capacity limits, exact bytes, no replacement, cancellation, changed request/scope rejection and lost-acknowledgment observation. Dialog counts in controller fixtures are mocked invocations. Builds and fixtures do not establish actual platform-dialog or account acceptance.

icons and denied OS presentation remain unavailable. Universal Alt+Tab or
app-switcher visibility is not claimed. There is no badge click action,

Unsent choices and selection reads are discarded on repository change or departure; late work cannot change another form or start its PR query. Remote repository capability, backend authorization/revision/checkout validation and normal configured queries remain authoritative. English/Korean semantic forms keep visible focus, 40px controls and wrapping actions.

### Usage filter inline bounds

At the existing 288px and 256px pane widths, Usage filter owners and label grid
tracks shrink to the available inline width. Text, datetime, select and picker
controls fit their label bounds with border-box sizing and retain 40px minimum
height. Preserve native checkbox sizing and calendar appearance. Long labels,
helpers, validation feedback and buttons wrap without hiding required content.
The filter body has no horizontal movement after child geometry is constrained;
its scroll width is at most its client width plus one pixel. Keep independent
vertical scrolling, stable scrollbar gutter, overscroll protection and fixed
Reset. Date precision, invalid drafts, presets, picker selection, query identity
and mounted drafts retain their original owners. English/Korean, light/dark,
compact drawer and effective 200% browser checks are synthetic evidence only.

Queue refresh footer stability: both queue presenters (legacy history-based and negotiated waiting queue) keep a retained complete empty presentation hidden during healthy automatic Refresh/Reload rereads of the same queue identity. Refresh status is announced through a screen-reader-only live region that adds no normal-flow height, so repeated rereads cannot shift the tray, Agent requests, transcript boundary or composer. Initial loading, failures with Retry, incomplete pagination, payload restoration and explicit boundary recovery stay visible. Retained emptiness is cached presentation, not fresh authoritative zero or mutation permission. Populated rows are retained during rereads. No API, protocol, migration or native change.

## Foreground chat Inbox acknowledgment

Ordinary Project and General Chat conversations, including independently selected
Fork sessions, follow the
[foreground session acknowledgment contract](cmds-delidev-inbox-contract.md#foreground-session-acknowledgment).
A connection-owned desktop boundary admits only a visible, focused authenticated
product window. A dedicated visit hook waits for current Session metadata and a
successful initial transcript payload, while preserving the existing interaction,
execution, draft and pagination presentation. Hidden/resource/Sidechat views and
mobile cannot acknowledge. Session snapshot ownership prevents a retained prior
activation or replaced transport from proving fresh loading.

Transcript load evidence is a pagination-chain `observed` flag, not residence of
the first payload page. Only a successful Initial, Refresh or Reload read from the
first page sets it, so evicting that payload (at most the chain's resident-page bound of payload pages stay
resident) never blocks a reselected Session whose refresh succeeded. Suspend,
reset, an in-flight or failed whole-chain read, and Restore or Additional reads
never grant it; Additional reads inside a visit leave it unchanged and never
acknowledge by themselves.

The hook submits once per conversation selection or foreground return. Readiness
changes, reconnects, polling and new alerts do not reset a submitted visit. Exact
failed requests survive navigation in the connection mutation registry and only the
original request can reconcile on a later qualifying activation. The connection's
accepted-result observer invalidates Inbox lists/details and unread aggregates after
sender disposal. Switching connections retires that observer; a late response cannot
change a successor connection. Failed or uncertain outcomes retain authoritative
presentation. Existing manual Inbox controls and native badge fences are unchanged.
No new user control, setting or banner is introduced.

## Configuration name correction

The server owns Project and Repository name availability. Loaded client pages cannot prove global availability; the client adds no catalog scan or availability RPC. Only Conflict with the typed `configuration_name_conflict` cause receives name-specific treatment. Revision, identity, denied and uncertain outcomes retain their existing presentation and request guards.

Show “A project with this name already exists. Choose another name.” beneath the existing Project name field. Repository copy uses “repository”. Korean copy is “이 이름의 프로젝트가 이미 있습니다. 다른 이름을 입력하세요.” and “이 이름의 저장소가 이미 있습니다. 다른 이름을 입력하세요.” Connect the wrapping alert to its input with `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`; use the existing semantic danger color. Preserve field geometry, themes, draft spelling, keyboard flow and opener restoration. A confirmed failure returns to the wizard name step or editor General panel, focuses its field and permits correction with a fresh explicit request. Pending or uncertain requests retain immutable original bytes.

A verified asynchronous repository name collision releases only its original settled request and returns to the retained draft. A completed clone collision retains the reported existing Local checkout and allows corrected registration without cloning or deleting that checkout. The recovered draft restores the exact submitted clone folder spelling as the editable Repository name, shows the localized “This computer” label (not the Repository name) in the summary Computer row, rendered from the locale-independent local-source marker so an application-wide language change updates it immediately, and disables clone mode until registration so the retained checkout is never cloned again. Narrow widths and effective 200% layout retain readable, wrapping guidance.

A definitive Repository name rejection belongs to the draft that submitted it. The still-mounted editor keeps the submitted spelling and guidance until correction. A newly constructed existing-Repository editor shows the saved document and clears a connection-owned definitive name rejection (the typed `configuration_name_conflict` cause) that predates it, because the rejected request document no longer exists. Any other definitive rejection, such as denied, revision, identity or an untyped abort, stays in the registry and in the generic error presentation of the reopened editor. That cleanup never discards busy, uncertain or retained-input state or an accepted job, and a rejection that arrives after the new editor mounted is presented normally.

A newly constructed existing-Repository editor restores a retained connection-owned save instead of the saved document. The submitted draft, including its spelling, is rebuilt from the retained request, and an accepted job and its completion binding (job, Repository and expected revision) return from the same retained entry. The original job stays authoritative: restoration only reads retained state and sends no new save. A job accepted after the editor was constructed, while the original request was still pending, is adopted the same way without another remount: the editor mounts the job observer from the retained request and accepted job of that entry, so the job and its completion binding never come from different sources, and adoption sends or replays no save. A job already released by a name collision, review or completion is not adopted again. A verified deferred name collision, whether it settled while the editor was pending, reopened or absent, returns to the restored draft with the name guidance and editable correction. A successful job still requires its explicit fresh Repository read before completing, and a generic failure keeps the existing read-and-review path back to the draft. An uncertain or busy retained request also restores its draft and keeps retrying only the original request. Restoration is keyed by connection and Repository identity, so another Repository or connection never inherits it.

Home navigation retains only the literal boolean true from the supported

The shared wide pane and compact navigation drawer render one static,
nonfocusable 14px outlined-circle question mark immediately before the existing
execution and archive glyphs. Use the semantic blue link color, preserving its
light/dark theme contrast and the independent execution colors. The decorative
SVG is hidden from assistive technology and has no separate click action or
keyboard stop. Unknown execution/archive question marks retain their meaning.

Append **Waiting for your response** / **응답 대기 중** to the complete row
accessible description and existing hover card. Preserve 32px rows, title
ellipsis before status glyphs, selection, rename, actions, focus outlines and
