### Codex reasoning summary disclosure

Ordinary Session and General Chat retain Codex reasoning in its original resource and
transcript position. Validated indexed `reasoning` records use a text-only disclosure:
a gray left chevron and the first non-whitespace completed summary part, falling
back to the first such initial summary part, then **Thinking** / **생각 과정**.
Preserve the selected string; CSS alone applies single-line ellipsis while its full
accessible text and expanded source remain available. Keep the 36px target, shared
native keyboard behavior and visible focus. The resting row has no background,
border, rounded box, shadow, Artifact label, raw kind or routine completion badge.

Expanded content retains the same summary row and shows exactly one plain inert
text body beneath it, beside one subtle vertical rule with approximately 20px
indentation, an 8px gap below the row, 13px neutral text, about 1.45 line height
and wrapping with no horizontal overflow. It shows no Initial observation,
Streamed observations or Final observation heading, no part-index label and no
raw delta kind or index. The body comes from the first source family with
non-whitespace text, in this order: completed content parts, streamed
`reasoning-content` deltas in sequence order, started content parts, completed
summary parts, streamed `reasoning-summary` deltas in sequence order, started
summary parts. Families are never combined, so a completed content snapshot
replaces the streamed body instead of extending it, and the UI never claims a
snapshot was reconstructed from deltas. The selected parts are joined for display
only: whitespace at a part boundary collapses to one space; a boundary without
whitespace receives one space except before closing punctuation or quotes and
after opening punctuation or quotes (best effort, so a word split across chunks
can be separated). Punctuation roles are fixed by character:

- Closing, attached to the previous part: `. , ; : ! ? ) ] } % …`, `»`, `”`
  (U+201D) and the CJK and Korean closers `、 。 ， ． ： ； ！ ？ ） ］ ｝ 」 』 】
〉 》 〕 〗 ｣ ｡ ､`.
- Opening, attached to the next part: `( [ {`, `«`, `“` (U+201C), `‘`
  (U+2018), `¡ ¿` and the CJK and Korean openers `「 『 【 〈 《 （ ［ ｛ 〔 〖 ｢`.
- Every other character, including dashes, `/` and `・`, gets the normal space.
- Curly double quotes follow the English convention (U+201C opens, U+201D
  closes) and never change the straight double quote state; other quoting
  conventions are not detected. Straight double quotes alternate between
  opening and closing. U+2018 opens a quote unless it starts a word-initial
  elision such as `‘tis`, where it is an apostrophe.

The straight single quote and the curly closing quote U+2019 are both quotes and
apostrophes, so they are classified by joiner state. For a part that starts with
one of them, with `depth` as the number of unclosed single quotes:

| Boundary before the part                                            | Part starts with                                                  | Result                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Whitespace, opening punctuation, an opening quote or the body start | `'` followed by an elision                                        | apostrophe                                         |
| Same                                                                | `'` otherwise                                                     | opens a quote                                      |
| Same                                                                | U+2019 followed by an elision                                     | apostrophe                                         |
| Same                                                                | U+2019 otherwise                                                  | closes a quote when `depth > 0`, else apostrophe   |
| None, after a word or punctuation                                   | `'` or U+2019 followed by an elision                              | apostrophe, one space                              |
| Same                                                                | `'` followed by a contraction suffix (`s t re ve ll d m`)         | no space; closes when `depth > 0`, else apostrophe |
| Same                                                                | `'` with `depth > 0`, not followed by a word or opening character | no space; closes a quote                           |
| Same                                                                | `'` otherwise                                                     | one space; opens a quote                           |
| Same                                                                | U+2019 otherwise                                                  | no space; closes when `depth > 0`, else apostrophe |

Elisions, introduced by `'`, U+2018 or U+2019, are `tis`, `twas`, `em`, `cause` and `til`, each not followed by a letter
or digit, and a two-digit year such as `90s`, not followed by another digit or a
quote, so `He wrote` + `’tis done` reads `He wrote ’tis done` and `called` + `'foo'` reads
`called 'foo'`. Inside a part, an apostrophe between two word characters never
opens or closes a quote. A straight single quote or U+2019 preceded by
whitespace, opening punctuation or an opening quote is an apostrophe for an
elision, an opening quote for `'`, and a closing quote or apostrophe for U+2019.
Elsewhere it closes a quote when `depth > 0` and is an apostrophe otherwise.
Apostrophes never change `depth`.

Whitespace inside a part, every non-whitespace character and
the retained record (families, original indices, sequence numbers and exact
strings) are unchanged. The component never generates summaries, Markdown,
translations or logs of reasoning text. When no family has text the disclosure
shows **No reasoning content was supplied.** / **제공된 생각 과정이 없습니다.**
when expanded. No hidden reasoning recovery is implied.

The original default is collapsed; the existing `reasoning_disclosure` Expanded
and Collapsed preferences govern initial mount. Explicit user choices and focus
survive revisions, completion and locale changes. Preserve actual streaming,
interrupted, failed, recovery and unavailable states. Malformed, mixed and unknown
records retain the original fallback. The dedicated disclosure requires a complete
valid message envelope: role `artifact`, absent or empty-string `text` (non-string
text is never coerced), and only the common metadata `execution_id`,
`native_thread_id`, `native_turn_id`, `native_id`, `native_parent_id`,
`first_sequence`, `last_sequence`, `context_revision` and `attachments` beside
`state` and `artifact`. Role-specific fields such as `phase`, `input_id`,
`inherited`, `turn_timing`, `tool`, `progress`, provider content and unknown
fields select the generic artifact fallback without stripping or repair.
OpenCode reasoning-text, Claude thinking
and other artifacts retain their source-specific rules. Preserve reader gates,
mounting, measured history wrappers, pagination, scroll anchors and live/history
ordering. Disclosure adds no reads, execution authority, RPC, schema, migration,
dependency or native operation. Semantic themes, English/Korean, narrow widths
and 200% reflow keep expanded text readable without horizontal overflow. Component
and browser fixtures establish presentation only; installed CEF/native acceptance
remains separate.

## App information Settings

The closed `app-information` category is last in System, after Backups. English **App information** and Korean **앱 정보** identify the same category. Ordinary category-free Settings entry keeps its original default. Static bundled Settings search and command-menu entries focus information, app updates, recovery, releases, license or notices without checking, downloading, installing or opening a link. Connections has no shortcut to App information; the category stays reachable from the sidebar, Settings search and command-menu entries. Runner Device updates remain in their original screen.

The page uses three ordered sections: DeliDev information, App updates and Related links. Native `desktop_update_context` alone supplies the compiled application version and local six-target platform. Loading, unavailable and failed reads remain explicit; selected server or Worker metadata never supplies a fallback. Original admitted product windows can read native context while disconnected; invalid saved authority is denied. The retained desktop owner caches its original native context read and keeps the same update controller, candidates, drafts, exact uncertain requests and installation outcomes across Settings/category/search changes. Only its stable presentation host moves.

Desktop Check for updates is direct and explicit. Unchecked differs from a confirmed successful check with no matching candidate. Checking, available, preparing, installing, installed, failed and unconfirmed states remain distinct. Update recovery starts collapsed and automatically reveals attention, failure or uncertainty. Original update ID/revision and read-only local installation inspection stay mounted when collapsed; closing the disclosure restores focus to its summary. Exact uncertain checks may retry their retained request; a possibly accepted installation remains inspect-only. Native signed-manifest verification, trusted-window confirmation, original receipt authority and installation lifecycle are unchanged.

When `GetStatus.production_root_ready` is explicitly false, the desktop (non-Worker) card shows the neutral `role="status"` text "Signed updates are unavailable in this build." with help text, and Check for updates stays visible but disabled (disabled attribute and an `onClick` guard), described by the status and help through `aria-describedby`. Activation sends no `CheckUpdate` or native prepare/install call, moves no focus, and shows no failed alert, warning icon or technical reference; Update recovery is not opened. The neutral text replaces only the unchecked fallback, so retained checking, uncertain, failed, available and current presentation stays unchanged. Readiness true, an absent field (legacy server), missing `SIGNED_UPDATES_V1`, pending and disconnected states keep their existing behavior. Readiness gates only a fresh desktop `CheckUpdate`: original-ID `GetUpdate` reads, native read-only inspection, retained candidates, uncertain requests and retry, and installation outcome recovery stay usable, and a later false observation never erases original state. Worker update controls are unchanged. English and Korean strings live in `src/locales/{en,ko}/updates.json`, and layout reuses the existing card tokens.

The page caps content at 1040px, uses 24px section spacing, 8px card corners and 40px controls. Semantic headings and definition lists, shared semantic theme colors and wrapping layouts support English/Korean, keyboard navigation and narrow/200% reflow. Related links render as one grouped list inside the section card: a single 1px bordered group with 8px corners and visible overflow so focus outlines are never clipped. It holds three full-width button rows in the fixed order Official releases, License and Open-source notices, separated by flat 1px dividers with no per-row outlines or default button corners. Related links rows are the only App information controls with a 56px minimum height (16px horizontal padding, vertical space for wrapping); other controls keep 40px. Each row shows a 20px decorative monochrome icon (tag, document, file stack), a 12px gap, a 14px medium-weight label that wraps, and the 18px external-link icon at the trailing edge. Icons are `aria-hidden`, not focusable and never announced. Enabled rows use the subtle surface on hover and show the shared 2px accent focus outline with 3px offset; disabled rows have no hover styling and keep readable muted text. Section-scoped styling resolves the shared Settings button border-color so the group border and dividers keep the semantic border token. The 12px muted source-notice disclaimer sits 16px below the group with unchanged wording. Rows stay in one column at narrow widths and 200% zoom. Button semantics, static search targets, availability and opening/error behavior are unchanged. Native actions use only the closed releases/license/notices selector. `open_app_information_link` captures and rechecks original product-window authority and epoch, dispatches the compiled destination through the bounded opener using the selected general browser destination (system default unless the user chose an installed browser) and denies dispatch after Quit stopping. The custom permission grants only trusted local/saved product documents, never remote origins, external browser children, tray/widget or auxiliary surfaces. Logs contain operation, selector, phase and failure code, never destinations or local paths.

Compiled destinations are the repository's DeliDev-filtered Releases page (search query `delidev%40v`, the URL-encoded `delidev@v` tag namespace), source LICENSE and source `apps/delidev/public` notices directory. Notices copy identifies source notices and does not claim an installed-package license inventory. No arbitrary renderer URL/path, broader opener permission, new business RPC or update channel is introduced; the only preference it consults is the device-local browser destination. Component/browser fixtures, build outputs and native ACL tests must be reported separately from installed CEF, native OS browser dispatch and production signed-install acceptance.

## Schedule creation calendar preview

Repeat and Review share a compact summary with separate Repeats, Scheduling starts
and First run preview rows. English/Korean prose comes from server-normalized
calendar constraints, including AND/OR day semantics. Simple patterns use familiar
sentences; complex patterns state time, month and day constraints explicitly.
The browser does not parse arbitrary cron. The exact original expression remains
in an initially collapsed keyboard-accessible Cron details disclosure; Custom
cron input is unchanged. Wrapped rows preserve the wizard's scrolling/footer.

An enabled draft starts scheduling after save. Its provisional first occurrence
shows a weekday, full date/time in the explicit schedule timezone and relative
wording based on the returned server boundary plus monotonic elapsed time.
Date display follows the device preference. A paused draft starts after enabling
and states that no automatic run is scheduled. Saving confirms the actual next
run; a scheduled time does not guarantee execution. The saved authoritative
`next_run_at` supersedes the creation estimate through the existing success path.

Connect Query scopes reads to the original transport and exact cron/timezone.
Valid changed inputs debounce by 300 ms, immediately hiding obsolete dates.
Every preview read (initial, minute, focus and boundary refresh) records a
monotonic `performance.now()` anchor when the request is issued, before it
leaves the client; the browser wall clock is never used. The estimated server
time is `calculated_at` plus the time since that anchor, so response latency
counts toward relative wording and the boundary refresh (a response delayed
1000 ms for a boundary 10000 ms after `calculated_at` refreshes about 9000 ms
after it arrives). A response whose estimate already reached `next_run_at` on
arrival is never shown as Ready: the state stays Calculating while an immediate
refetch runs. A completed successful response is validated before any date or
constraints are exposed: `calculated_at`, `next_run_at` and constraints must be
present, both timestamps finite, and `next_run_at` strictly after
`calculated_at`. Any failure is Unavailable with no provisional date or
recurrence constraints, the cron/timezone/draft/save validation stay intact and
minute/focus refresh continues. Calculating is reserved for in-flight reads and
the normal occurrence-boundary refresh.
Repeat/Review refresh each minute, at the estimated occurrence boundary, on
returning to the surface and on window focus. Disposed tasks, replaced connections
and changed inputs cannot receive an old date. Polite status updates do not move
focus or announce a per-second countdown. Invalid, calculating, unavailable and
unsupported-server states retain the draft and original save validation.
Unimplemented retains the preset summary and explains that saving determines
the next run; no Custom interpretation is fabricated. All existing mutation,
revision, fresh Local proof, pending/uncertain request bytes and retry owners remain.

## Active conversation question presentation

The Conversation Agent requests tray presents the latest authoritative interaction revision. A successful original answer response RPC joins the same revision projection as list reads, live updates and restored pages. Retain original arrival order, authenticated session scope and page-scoped counts. Keep lightweight revision/presentation metadata across payload eviction so older pages cannot revive an answered form. Full original documents remain in the existing bounded payload window.

After confirmed server submission, remove the original question selection and text inputs. Show compact queued, claimed, transmitted, uncertain, failed or unavailable state while delivery or original receipt recovery remains unresolved. The explicit receipt retry retains the original UUID, revision and request bytes through closure; it cannot create a second answer or native send. Unknown or contradictory observations remain visible without response authority. Native acceptance and closure remain independent from session outcome. Once a revision establishes a question, its question identity and answer mutation key are sticky in the metadata projection: a higher revision that drops or changes the type or native family still advances revision, closure and response state but keeps the original question flag and mutation key, is marked unavailable and stays compact and visible, so the original uncertain receipt and exact retry remain reachable through closure and payload eviction. Stale or equal revisions never overwrite newer metadata.

An uncertain answer transport error collapses the active-tray question to the compact receipt immediately, without waiting for a newer interaction revision: while the question's own answer mutation key has a retained uncertain intent, the original selection and text controls and Send answers are absent and only the compact state with the exact retry remains. The retry reuses the original request UUID, revision and bytes, and no retry or second answer is sent automatically. This applies only to the active tray; Inbox forms, approvals, unanswered questions and the successful queued-compaction and closure-recovery paths are unchanged.

Until a newer revision supplies an authoritative response state, a compact active-tray question whose own mutation key has a retained uncertain intent shows the existing localized uncertain status (`status.uncertain`, Korean "불확실") in its Response line instead of the unanswered `Not submitted` label, so a possibly accepted answer is never presented as unsent. Authoritative newer states (queued, claimed and so on) and compact questions without retained uncertainty keep their existing labels, and the explicit retry, mutation keys and request bytes are unchanged. The compact row also keeps the existing Agent question heading whenever the retained projection selects the compact question body, even when a newer revision of the same interaction changes or removes its `type` (including a contradictory `native-approval`); the row stays unavailable with no new question or approval form and the original exact receipt retry. Genuine approvals keep the Native approval heading and evicted receipts keep their question heading. No localization key is added.

Compact question receipts follow the projection, not RPC completion: a metadata-known question that is absent from the resident payload rows (for example after its page is evicted) keeps its compact presentation, page-scoped count and tray-emptiness blocker while its projection is not retired or an answer mutation is still retained. Successful RPC completion, which clears the retained mutation, therefore never removes a queued, claimed, transmitted, uncertain, failed, unavailable or contradictory question; only authoritative acceptance or confirmed closure (a retired projection with no retained mutation) or an authoritative removal tombstone drops it, and restoring an older payload cannot revive the form. A compact receipt renders at its original reached page and row position through the payload window's projected callback, so it stays before newer page requests after its payload page is evicted; multiple receipts follow retained page/row order rather than projection observation order, each original question renders once across restore/evict cycles, and only questions that no reached page owns (for example new live arrivals) trail the final page. Focused-page protection and exact retained retry identity are unchanged.

Retained interaction projections hold only bounded metadata. `interactionProjection` classifies validity and presentation from the original document first, then stores `closure` as the enum `open`, `native-closed`, `turn-ended` or the fixed `unknown`, and `response.state` as `queued`, `claimed`, `transmitted`, `uncertain`, `canceled`, `accepted`, `none` (no response) or the same fixed `unknown`. No original closure or response-state string, however large, outlives its payload page in the session-lifetime `InteractionPresentationStore`; compact receipts render recognized values as before and `unknown` through the localized `status.unknown` label. This broadens no resource validation and discards no unresolved receipt.

The shared synchronization `Remove` update carries the watched `entityKind` of the originating event. An authoritative stream Remove of an interaction (`entityKind` interaction) is recorded in the owning session's `InteractionPresentationStore` as an identity-only tombstone before any following Snapshot can clear the stream-scoped removed set. The tombstone drops the retained projection and fences that identity: the compact receipt, page-scoped count and tray-emptiness blocker stay absent through later Snapshots and through restoration of an older list page that still lists the id, and later observations of it are not retained. Removals of other kinds, including messages and queue entries never seen in the Snapshot, never reach the store and cannot consume or evict an interaction tombstone. Tombstones hold no documents, are bounded to 2000 identities per session store (oldest forgotten first) and are never shared across session stores. An unresolved question that merely leaves the resident payload page without a Remove keeps its receipt after a Snapshot. Removal sends no answer, cancels no native work, acknowledges no Inbox item and leaves retained original mutation bytes and the mutation registry untouched; approval forms, unrelated ids and revision ordering are unchanged.

An accepted list read joins the same latest-authoritative-revision projection for every reached page before any payload is discarded. The pagination chain runs an optional per-batch `accepted` observer only after the read passes its generation, cancellation, session, cursor-boundary and continuation checks and before payload eviction, so pages outside the interaction chain's three-page payload window still advance their interaction projections (revision, presentation, closure and response state) while only the lightweight projection is retained. A valid accepted or confirmed-closed question with no unresolved response or retained mutation therefore loses its compact receipt, page-scoped count and tray-emptiness blocker after a list refresh alone, without restoring the evicted page. A retained original mutation and unresolved, contradictory or invalid observations stay visible under the existing rules. Canceled, superseded or boundary-rejected reads never run the observer, observation is revision-monotonic so older or equal revisions never overwrite newer metadata, and an observer failure never fails the read. The observer receives only already-validated rows of the owning session and interaction kind, and no answer content is logged.

A successful retry through an evicted compact receipt applies the same acceptance validation as the resident form: the returned interaction must carry the receipt's request ID, the current session and interaction kind, a supported resource schema, and a revision newer than the submitted mutation's expected revision. The comparison basis is the revision the original retained request was submitted against, not the mutable presentation projection revision, so an exact receipt replay whose result equals an already advanced projection still retires its draft. The session-level accepted-result notification owns this retirement, so it completes even when payload restoration replaced the compact receipt before the retried RPC finished and the receipt's own presenter callback no longer runs. Only then does it clear that one request's retained edit draft; absent, mismatched, unsupported, stale or equal-revision results (relative to the submitted revision) and failed or uncertain retries preserve the draft. Unrelated drafts, the original retry UUID and bytes, response validation and native acceptance rules are unchanged, and the resident success path is not altered.

A generic (non-native-family) question counts as natively accepted only when the complete accepted response envelope validates: a UUIDv7 response id, an `input` holding only `answers` that satisfies the original-question response rules below, a strict RFC3339 `accepted_at`, a full claim identity (UUIDv7 `id`, `job_id`, `machine_id`, `instance_id`, `device_id` and a strict RFC3339 `claimed_at`), a `transmitted` or `uncertain` delivery observation with a safe nonnegative integer `sequence`, `native-question-output` acceptance evidence, and an acceptance `sequence` that is a safe integer strictly greater than the delivery `sequence`. Sequences that are not JSON numbers, or that fall outside the safe-integer range, make the envelope invalid. Strict RFC3339 validates the source wall-clock date and time before converting the instant (`apps/delidev/src/rfc3339.ts`): February 30, a non-leap February 29, April 31, hour 24, hour 25, minute 60 and second 60 are invalid even though `Date.parse` would normalize them, while leap days, `Z`, in-range numeric offsets and 1 to 9 fractional digits stay valid; date-only and free-text values remain invalid.

The `answers` of a generic accepted response are bound to the original request in the same document (`questions.questions`) with parity to the server `QuestionRequest.Validate` and `QuestionResponseInput.Validate` rules (`apps/delidev/src/generic-question-response.ts`, `cmds/delidev-cli/internal/domain/question_responses.go`). The original request must hold 1 to 128 questions with unique non-blank ids of at most 128 UTF-8 bytes, string `header` and `text`, boolean `other` and `secret`, and at most 128 options with unique non-blank labels and string descriptions; an absent or null `options` means free text. The `answers` keys must equal the original question ids exactly, so missing and foreign identities are invalid. Any `secret` original question makes the response invalid because secret answers need a protected native capability. Each answer list is an explicit array (an empty array means unanswered) of at most 128 unique non-blank strings, each well-formed UTF-8 without NUL and within the response byte bound (256 KiB). When a question has options and `other` is false, every answer must equal an offered label. The complete response, measured as the server's Go JSON encoding (`{"answers":{...}}` with HTML-sensitive characters and U+2028/U+2029 escaped), must stay within 256 KiB. An accepted generic row that fails any rule stays pending, unavailable and visible, keeps its compact receipt through payload eviction and older-revision restore, and grants no response authority; valid empty arrays, offered labels and permitted custom text retire normally and a matching retained mutation keeps receipt recovery visible. Logs and diagnostics never include answer content. An accepted question with any missing or malformed part stays pending and unavailable, visible, and grants no response authority; a complete envelope retires without a retained mutation, and a matching unresolved retained mutation keeps recovery visible. The OpenCode, Claude and Grok native-family paths keep their own validators.

Retire a question only after authoritative native acceptance or confirmed closure without an unresolved response or retained mutation. Use that same projection for rendering, the page-scoped count and automatic expansion. Preserve unanswered questions and unrelated approval forms, identities and drafts. Original question/answer documents and Inbox inspection remain retained; tray retirement does not delete resources or mark Inbox items read.

Hide the complete Agent requests disclosure only when a successful complete resident read proves there is no displayed request or unresolved operation. Initial loading, errors, continuation and evicted-page restoration remain reachable. A read failure over an otherwise empty tray stays sticky until the read settles: an explicit Retry or boundary Reload clears the error as soon as it starts, but the disclosure, its loading status and its recovery controls stay mounted for the whole pending (including stalled) read. The pending read keeps presenting the prior failure, including its alert and technical details, so the same Retry or Reload control stays mounted but disabled until the read settles. A pending Retry or Reload canceled by suspension (for example switching to another retained session) settles nothing, so the failure stays latched until a later read settles successfully. Only a settled successful empty read hides the disclosure again; a repeated failure keeps Retry or Reload reachable. A healthy background Refresh or Reload over a confirmed empty tray never sets this state and stays hidden, and read cancellation and identity fencing are unchanged. An empty tray adds no completion badge, replacement message or vacant region. The composer moves upward naturally and retains its mounted controller, draft, dimensions, styling and controls at wide/compact widths and short heights. If retirement removes the focused control, focus the next actionable request or the composer. Do not steal focus from another connected active control. No RPC, protocol allocation, migration or native delivery change is required.

### Paid credits in the selected subscription popover

The selected ChatGPT usage popover places a compact Paid credits card above quota within its existing 320px width, 16px padding and viewport-clamped internal scroll. Reuse the subscription presentation contract’s validated saved projection, string-only two-decimal formatter, 24px tabular value, smaller unit and accessible unchanged exact decimal disclosure. Separate multiple buckets in source order with native labels and their original observation times; never sum them. Explicit zero, null/unknown, tiny positive, unlimited, loading, unsupported, stale/future and failed evidence remain distinct. System 76 controls credit display independently of capability-17 inventory admission; other services remain unchanged.

Failed or incomplete saved-resource reads retain original account-bound values and timestamps as historical evidence until a complete accepted replacement. Connection identity replacement resets local disclosure state; authentication loss removes the selected details. Credits do not affect `remainingBadge`, quota windows, read pagination, the existing refresh owner or Recheck saved quota evidence and Manage subscriptions actions. Preserve semantic themes, EN/KO wrapping, narrow and effective 200% reflow, Escape/outside dismissal and opener focus. No new RPC, polling owner, native operation, purchase, consumption or migration is added. The exact-balance disclosure uses the `Overlay` presentation, so opening, pinning or closing it never changes popover height, card, observation, quota or footer geometry or scroll metrics; the existing resize observer still re-clamps only for genuine content or viewport changes. Follow [the subscription presentation contract](apps-delidev-subscription-settings-contract.md#paid-credit-observations) and [its disclosure presentation](apps-delidev-subscription-settings-contract.md#exact-balance-disclosure-presentation).

### Initial startup group disclosures and time

The empty-transcript detailed ordinary Session and General Chat startup block
uses two independent native Disclosure rows, initially closed. Each row places
the left chevron, localized title, an 8px gap, muted integer elapsed seconds, an
8px gap and a decorative 20px running spinner together beside the title. Flat
resting headers apply only to this block. Expansion reveals existing ordered
operations and repository ordinals. Compact Startup details retains its existing
presentation. Narrow layouts and 200% zoom wrap safely; theme hover, visible
focus and reduced-motion spinner behavior follow the shared disclosure family.

Only exact original job/execution metadata in Resource.startup_timing supplies
time. Missing, malformed, reversed or foreign timing is unavailable, never zero.
Live seconds use the paired authenticated Machine/Overview observed_at and a
monotonic presentation timer, once per second even while closed. The clock anchors
at receipt of the server observation; network read duration remains a conservative
presence bound, not additional group duration. Finished time stays fixed without
a spinner and is confirmed only when its matching settlement is established. `finished_at` alone
freezes an interval: Stop, failure and cancellation also write it, so it never
confirms success. Workspace time is confirmed only by `preparation.state` ready
for the same job; agent time only by the same job/execution's active execution
document listing the selected original input first in a complete, valid
`accepted_inputs` list (the same bounded, unique, digest-bound validation used for
session progress). Legacy
documents without that evidence, failed, stopped, lost-owner or still-pending
claimed intervals keep the frozen seconds, no spinner and the Unconfirmed label,
including in the retained row while cancellation is pending. Attention,
inactivity, hidden documents, stale presence or connection
replacement stop ticks and animation. Retained unfinished values are explicitly
unconfirmed. Timing is outside the polite status node and has aria-live off.
Disclosure toggles do not fetch, reset clocks, dispatch or remount controllers;
composer, drafts, first-input proof and initial Info visibility retain their
existing ownership.

### Pull request workspace presentation

The read-only PR workspace follows the integration contract's separately retained
list/selection owners. At available body width 900 CSS pixels or more, list/detail
use 40/60 independent scrolling; compact Back restores list scroll and row focus.
While the standalone Pull requests page is visible, `main` is a vertical flex
container and the page takes the `main` height left after its preceding siblings,
including the compact context trigger, rather
than a full `main` height that those siblings would overflow. The page is itself a
vertical layout, and the workspace panes use the page height left after the
header, notices and pending actions down to the page's 32 CSS pixel bottom
padding. The workspace has a zero flex basis, so long lists scroll inside their
panes instead of growing the page. There
is no viewport-relative height cap, so a tall window leaves no unused band below
the panes. The workspace keeps a 320 CSS pixel minimum height, so `main` scrolls
only when less than that remains, and never when the 320 CSS pixel floor fits.
Both panes keep their own overflow, and resizing the window or changing the
pending-actions notice height reflows the workspace without a GitHub read or a
selection reset.
Selection initially remains empty and displays a localized prompt. Rows and the
compact detail header retain complete wrapping titles, textual state, Draft and
unknown-author notices, relative update times (exact UTC on hover/focus) and their own signed additions/deletions.
Stack-context rows remain distinguished from accepted filtered matches.

The selected detail is a flat document layout. A top toolbar holds Back to results
at the start and Refresh plus Open on GitHub at the end, using the existing Back,
Refresh and Open action icons with localized accessible labels and 40 CSS pixel
targets; handlers, disabled states and the native GitHub opener are unchanged, and
opener and read notices render beneath the toolbar without enabling unavailable
actions. Below it come textual Open/Closed, optional Draft, the PR number, the
complete wrapping title (24px/1.4 semibold), then one wrapping row of avatar,
author or unknown-author notice and `Updated {relative time}`, and a row of
monospace head-to-base branches with the PR's own signed additions/deletions at the
end. Body text is 16px/1.65; content insets are 28px when the workspace is at least
900 CSS pixels wide and 16px in compact layouts; header-to-tabs and tabs-to-body
gaps are 24px. Header and tabs scroll with the detail body (no sticky positioning,
cards or shadows). The tabs use a neutral baseline with a 2px selected underline.
The detail Updated field and the list-row Updated field use `TimestampMode.Relative`: elapsed time shows
now below 60 seconds, then floored minutes, hours, days (24 hours), weeks (7 days),
months (30 days) and years (365 days) at the 60 minute, 24 hour, 7 day, 30 day and
365 day boundaries. The detail time element keeps `dateTime`, native `title` and
`aria-description` equal to the exact source value, so hover shows the exact UTC
value without a custom popup or extra focus stop. The shared presentation
scheduler updates the label at each unit boundary while active and recomputes on
focus/visibility return without any GitHub read or business-state change. Commit
author, committer and observation timestamps stay Exact. List rows use the same Relative mode with a custom exact-UTC tooltip instead of the native title.

Semantic underline tabs are Description, Diff, Reviews, Commits (설명, Diff, 리뷰,
커밋). Arrow/Home/End moves focus without reading; Enter/Space explicitly activates.
Same-PR observations are lazy, disposable and bounded. Scope replacement clears
old observations. Description is inert Markdown plus full source; Diff is an
immutable file-oriented patch plus original snapshot; Reviews is complete published
feedback; Commits preserves full messages in Details and supports Copy full SHA.
The ordinary workspace contains no CI/rules/reviewer verification grid, Overview,
problem history or separate stack-dependencies section. Pending PR actions remains
above the workspace. Existing server/CLI inspection and recovery surfaces survive.
Unknown counts and failed decorative images remain accessible fallbacks.

The stack-context workspace query keeps `retry: false` and stays pending while the
server resumes a read that selection or tab work displaced; the selected detail
remains usable meanwhile. A pending read shows no incomplete notice, cancellation
warning or Retry stack context. The query publishes the final server observation
without issuing another workspace RPC. Only a terminal failure or invalid
observation shows the incomplete notice, Problem and explicit Retry stack context.
Unmounting or scope replacement discards a late result.

### Contextual session recovery cards

Session and General Chat Conversation retain one recovery region immediately
above the composer, after the input tray and outside transcript scrolling.
Independent notices keep their existing order and original controllers. Transcript
read failures remain in the transcript; form validation stays with its input.
The region scrolls internally when several cards exceed its bounded height.
Cards use semantic warning tokens, definitive startup errors use danger tokens,
and all retain a decorative warning icon, text, thin borders, 12px corners and
controls of at least 40 CSS pixels. Narrow layouts wrap text and stack actions.
The transcript, composer node/draft, attachments, queued inputs, Info targets and
original request identities remain mounted through observations and locale changes.
New or changed error text uses the existing alert announcement without focus
movement or a mutation on mount. Unchanged observations add no announcement.

Each card exposes its localized heading, safe cause and supported guidance.
Only secondary codes, versions and opaque references belong in closed Technical
details. The exact `missing_input` plus `quota_exhausted` pair shows Usage limit
reached and localized complete-exhaustion guidance. Legacy, unknown, malformed or
mismatched causes retain a generic heading and visible safe evidence; message
text never establishes exhaustion. Authentication, connection, definitive startup,
budget and uncertain recovery have distinct localized headings. The live stream
card derives its heading from the typed failure code of the snapshot or watch
observation (authentication for `unauthenticated`, connection for
`unavailable`/`server_unavailable`, and the connection heading as the fallback
for unclassified or every other code, including recovery, budget and quota
classifications), never from message text; its message,
guidance, Info target and alert announcement are unchanged. Connection
refresh retains its original failed-observation gate and only reobserves.
Show details opens the original Info target, including Budget and Recovery.
No card grants sign-in, account switching, reset, send, Resume or new retry authority.
Startup correction, delivery and cleanup remain independent visible facts;
original no-send and confirmed-cleanup proof alone can permit startup retry.

## Original dynamic-tool disclosure

Use the original tool disclosure for bounded Codex dynamic observations. Show
the native tool/namespace and independently observed lifecycle status. Expanded
content shows the exact fixed unavailable text when an original reply was
attempted, plus separate localized `Reply delivery` and `Native request` rows.
Transmission or uncertainty never substitutes for native resolution, item
completion, root outcome or cleanup. Preserve nullable native success and
ordered inert text/image/audio reference rows. Do not display internal request
identities, argument contents, media locators or dispatch/retry/approval controls.
Unknown or malformed unions retain explicit unavailable presentation.

## Browser destinations for external links

Settings > System has a Browser category directly after Appearance (`SettingsCategory.Browser = "browser"`, English `Browser`, Korean `브라우저`). It is part of Settings search (`browser-general`, `browser-local` targets) and command-menu navigation. One bordered card (8px corners, 40px controls, content capped at 1040px, labels stacked above selectors at narrow widths and 200% reflow) holds two native `select` controls: General URL destination (`일반 URL 열기 대상`) and Local URL destination (`로컬 URL 열기 대상`). Each offers `System default browser` plus every HTTP(S) handler discovered natively; a muted note states that sign-in and account authorization links always use the system default. Selectors are keyboard operable and close on Esc through the native control. Web and mobile render the category with every control disabled and a native-capability-unavailable message, call no native command and keep their existing behavior.

**Storage and synchronization.** `BrowserStore` (`src-tauri/src/browser_preferences.rs`) persists `browser_preferences.json` in the app config directory (version 1, `revision`, `general`, `local`) with the same bounded, symlink-refusing, atomic-replace and revisioned compare-before-write pattern as shortcut preferences. Each choice is `system-default` or `installed` with a native identity (macOS bundle identifier, Linux desktop-file ID, Windows `StartMenuInternet` key); identities are syntax-bounded to 128 characters of letters, digits and `._-+ ()`, never display names, paths or commands. Both choices default to `system-default`. `read_browser_preferences`, `update_browser_preferences` and `reset_browser_preferences` are admitted for registered Local product windows and bound Saved windows only and publish `browser-preferences-changed` to every admitted window; stale expected revisions return `changed` and the visible choice changes only from an accepted native snapshot, so success is never shown before persistence. A newly selected identity must be registered at update time; an unchanged saved identity may be uninstalled and stays visible as `<identity> (not available)`. Corrupt or newer-version storage keeps its bytes, disables selection, shows an explicit message and offers `Reset browser settings`; reset is accepted only in that state. Other storage problems offer a reload.

**Discovery.** `read_browser_inventory` refreshes the list whenever the page opens and on explicit refresh. macOS scans application bundles for an `Info.plist` that declares both `http` and `https` URL schemes, Linux scans XDG, Flatpak and Snap `.desktop` files that handle both `x-scheme-handler/http` and `/https`, and Windows reads `StartMenuInternet` registrations that publish both URL associations through `reg.exe`. Discovery failure (`browser-discovery-failed`) is distinct from an empty list; both leave `System default browser` available. When an update rejects a newly selected browser with `browser-discovery-failed`, `invalid-input`, or `browser-unavailable` before storage, Settings retains the last verified preference revision and choices, keeps healthy selectors available, and gives definitive failure guidance without replaying the update. A transport rejection, malformed response or other unproven outcome retains the uncertain-save reload gate.

**Classification.** `external_url.rs` accepts only explicit credential-free `http`/`https` URLs of at most 2,048 bytes without whitespace or control characters. A parsed host of `localhost`, any IPv4 `127.0.0.0/8` address or IPv6 `::1` is Local regardless of port, path or query; every other host (LAN addresses, `localhost.example`, a query containing `localhost`) is General. No DNS lookup happens.

**Dispatch.** `open_external_url` (and the provider guidance, App information and GitHub openers) validate and classify the URL natively, read the saved choice directly from storage, resolve an installed identity through a fresh inventory immediately before launch and launch exactly one process with an argv-only recipe: macOS `/usr/bin/open -b <bundle> <url>`, the desktop-entry `Exec` command with field codes substituted on Linux, and the registered executable on Windows (registered arguments are ignored). The URL is one argv value, the environment is a credential-free allowlist, and a stopped (quitting) host launches nothing. A browser still running after a two-second grace period counts as dispatched and is reaped on its own thread, never killed. Unreadable or corrupt existing storage fails closed (`storage-unavailable`); a host with no app config directory has no saved choice, so the system default applies while Settings shows the preference as unavailable; a missing browser reports `browser-unavailable`; a failed launch reports `browser-launch-failed`. There is no fallback to the system default or another browser, no retry and no second launch, and the saved choice is kept. OAuth/subscription authorization calls the system-default dispatcher directly and never reads the preference. `device-browser-links` grants the five commands to `main` and `server-*` webviews only; permission tests resolve the generated ACL.

**Renderer presentation.** `LinkedPre` renders user and assistant message text (generic session messages, Claude text blocks, Grok user input and Grok assistant text) as the original characters with explicit HTTP(S) tokens wrapped in anchors that never navigate the webview; reasoning, tool, artifact, progress, diff, file and details content stays inert. Trailing sentence punctuation and unbalanced closing brackets stay outside the URL, partial streamed tokens are not links until complete, and a second activation while one is pending is ignored. The terminal adapter (`terminal-emulator.ts`) reads rendered `.term-row` text on a plain primary click or hover, joins rows that fill the full grid width, ignores clicks while text is selected, and leaves WTerm `linksEnabled: false`, OSC 8/OSC 52 handling, input admission and parser replies unchanged; its listeners are removed on disposal. The terminal presenter supplies the adapter's opener only in a native Tauri host; web previews keep printed URLs inert without link listeners, pointer affordance or native launch attempts. Failures render a localized dismissible alert (`external-link.*`) naming Settings > Browser; Provider guidance, App information and GitHub openers map the same codes to that guidance.

**Logging.** Operations `external_url_open`, `provider_guidance`, `app_information_link`, `github_open`, `browser_inventory` and `device_browser_preferences_*` log operation, URL class, browser identity, phase and failure code. URLs, query values, credentials and local executable paths are never logged.

**Acceptance boundary.** Component, fixture, ACL and argv tests do not establish installed-browser discovery or launch on macOS, Windows and Linux; record that acceptance separately. No server RPC, capability number, protobuf or database migration is added. The protected account/session browser and the standalone CLI keep their existing behavior.

## Native record version validation

Desktop validators for retained native interaction, usage and subagent records (Claude, OpenCode, Grok and Codex) accept the record's observed native version when it is a valid SemVer at or above the harness baseline, using the shared `harnessVersionAllowed` predicate in `apps/delidev/src/harness-version.ts`. Records below the baseline or with a malformed version stay unavailable and expose no response controls. Equality with a pinned baseline is never required, so a newer admitted installation's requests, usage and child observations remain actionable and visible.

### Claude image attachment admission

The shared image draft permits Claude Code only when every source model declares image input and the original server and Runner report the independent System 106 / Worker 71 pair in addition to 45/25. Follow-ups use the frozen original declaration. Keep the existing draft, upload and error presentation; missing peers retain unsupported guidance without discarding original images. Follow the [image input contract](cmds-delidev-image-input-contract.md#closed-adapter-profiles).

## Saved Worker deletion

The saved-runner list in Settings > Runner Devices shows a red outlined **Delete** beside **Inspect installed harnesses** (accessible name `Delete Worker <name>`). It is enabled only when the server advertises `WORKER_REMOVAL_V1`, the row uses schema 1 and the trusted native local-Worker proof (`readLocalWorker`) was read successfully and names a different machine. The row whose machine ID equals that proof has no Delete action, shows `Managed by this app` and `This app's current local Worker cannot be deleted.`; same-named Workers stay deletable. While the observation is pending or failed, Delete is disabled with explanatory text and an explicit Retry verification action. Unsupported or unknown server capability shows disabled guidance and never falls back to configuration deletion.

Delete opens a focus-contained `Delete Worker?` confirmation with the inert Worker name, the copy `This Worker will lose access to this server and be removed from saved runner devices.` and `Session history and files on the device will be kept. Running work may require recovery.`, a neutral Cancel and a solid danger `Delete Worker`. Initial focus is Cancel; Escape and the close icon dismiss (not while a request is in flight) and the opener regains focus. A fresh confirmation re-reads the native identity: a match or failed read sends nothing. One retained connection-owned `remove-worker:<machine id>` request (it survives Settings category changes until an authoritative result resolves it) carries the machine ID, its observed revision and schema 1; the confirm button is disabled while pending. A stale revision (read or `conflict`) requires the explicit `Review current Worker` action, which re-reads the exact Worker and binds the next confirmation to that authoritative result (never the cached read), and a new confirmation with a new request UUID. An uncertain result keeps the original request bytes and UUID, disables fresh deletion and offers only `Retry original deletion`, which replays the same deletion and carries the Danger tone like the opener and confirmation, while `Review current Worker`, Cancel and Retry verification stay Default. Failures use `role="alert"` with the standard problem presentation; success removes the row only after the authoritative response, announces it with `role="status"`, hides the machine until later reads omit it (stale cached pages cannot resurrect it) and focuses the next row action or the list heading. Copy lives in the `worker-removal` EN/KO catalogs; the row actions wrap below the metadata at narrow widths and 200% zoom, and the solid danger button uses the `--danger-solid-*` theme tokens in light and dark.

## Subagent name list and detail card

The Session information Subagents section renders a semantic `ul` of agent names: one row per child, keyed by the original product child identity, so equal names remain separate children. Rows have no status dots, avatars, badges, counts, secondary text, hierarchy indentation, controls or explanatory paragraph. Names are about 14px text in rows of at least 32px, wrap with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` inside the 360px rail and use the muted section heading and a subtle hover/focus background in light, dark, English and Korean.

A name is the accepted native Resource display name (`Resource.subagent_display`, joined by the original child ID) or, when it is missing, blank, longer than 256 Unicode characters, control-bearing or foreign, the stable localized `Subagent N` ordinal. An invalid name never invalidates the child page. Only Codex children use names: metadata on a Claude Code or OpenCode child is ignored for its row and for retained parent names, and those children keep ordinals. A row observed in the current payload window is authoritative, so unusable metadata on it deletes any older retained name; retained names of rows that left the window are kept so parent labels stay stable. Names are inert text and never grant identity or control authority.

Each name is a focusable trigger. Existing parent (a retained name or ordinal, or Root session), independent status, observed and requested model, partial recent output, exact usage with unavailable and partial markers, nullable decimal counters and original usage strings appear only in a noninteractive card built from the resident validated payload. Pointer hover opens it after 300ms; keyboard focus opens it immediately; a 150ms departure grace covers the gap between source and card; Escape suppresses it until re-entry. Outside pointer or tap, scroll outside the card, resize, source removal, session or connection switch, disabled ownership and payload eviction dismiss it. Opening a card sends no request or mutation. The card is at most about 320px wide with 16px padding and 8px corners, prefers the left of the right-hand rail, flips right or below/above and clamps to 8px viewport insets with bounded vertical scrolling. It has no focusable actions, focus trap or live announcement.

The hover controller is the shared `session-hover-card` primitive: the sidebar and the Subagents section each mount their own provider, so timers, listeners and the active card are never shared. Paging, whole-page validation, capability gates, successful-empty hiding, Retry, Diagnostics source evidence and root transcript behavior are unchanged.
